stories.summary: A perennial herb endemic to the limestone mountains of west-central mainland Portugal. It grows on rocky outcrops and stony limestone soils, producing white or pinkish-white flowers from March to June. Its habitat is declining locally because of wind-farm construction and quarry expansion.

A flowering shrub endemic to Portugal’s Berlengas archipelago, where it grows on rocky coastal cliffs and granite slopes. It bears small, pale-pink flowers in clusters at the ends of long stalks during April and May.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Armeria berlengensis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European law as a priority species under Annex II and is also listed under Annex IV of the Habitats Directive.

A bellflower-family plant endemic to the Azores, it bears pinkish-white, bell-shaped flowers. It usually grows in rocky recesses on coastal cliffs, though it can occur on tiled roofs; higher-altitude communities suggest its distribution may be broader than currently known.

A small annual daisy native to Mediterranean countries eastward to Iran. It is often slightly hairy, with a few small leaves that may be toothed or grow on the flower stem, and has finely short-haired seeds.
Evergreen herb or shrub native to Africa, widespread in forest regions from eastern Sudan to southern Angola. It is often sticky and has pale to dark purple or blue flowers with white throats.

A flowering shrub or small tree native to the Andes of Ecuador and Colombia, it is now extinct in the wild. It bears hanging, fragrant, yellow trumpet-shaped flowers and remains widely cultivated as an ornamental.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts of the plant are poisonous.

stories.summary: Bush or small tree endemic to Ecuador and listed as Extinct in the Wild since March 2014. Its exceptionally large, hanging trumpet-shaped flowers open white and may remain white or age to peach, pink or apricot.
stories.edibilityNote: Flowers, leaves and seeds are exceptionally poisonous in large quantities; swallowing them is likely to cause severe neurological and physical symptoms.

stories.summary: Flowering plant endemic to Madeira. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation.
A flowering plant native from the Caucasus through Central Asia to the western Himalaya. It tolerates poor soil, drought and nearby paving, making it suitable as a street tree.
An evergreen, branched shrub endemic to Madeira. It has leathery, spoon-shaped to broad-tipped leaves and small white flowers spotted pink to red, blooming from October to June.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago. It is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation, specifically Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.

A tropical tree native to the Atlantic Forest from Rio de Janeiro to southeastern Minas Gerais, Chrysophyllum imperiale is endangered following habitat loss. It has large pale leaves and solid oval yellow fruits, which were much appreciated by Brazilian emperors Pedro I and Pedro II.
stories.edibilityNote: The yellow fruits were historically much appreciated by Brazilian emperors Pedro I and Pedro II.

stories.summary: Flowering plant endemic to Madeira. It is protected under Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.

Plant endemic to mainland Portugal, restricted to south-facing limestone coastal cliffs between Sesimbra and Cape Espichel. In the 2020 mainland assessment, only about 500 mature plants and two locations were estimated, and it was assessed as Endangered following recent declines in habitat quality and plant numbers.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Convolvulus fernandesii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Flowering plant found in Portugal; the subspecies Crambe fruticosa subsp. fruticosa is endemic to Madeira.
A mustard-family plant endemic to the Canary Islands. It has rough, stalked leaves with blunt teeth, while its stems are more or less smooth.
A hawthorn native to the Mediterranean Basin. Wild plants produce plentiful, unusually plump haw fruits, while different varieties have orange, yellowish or red-tinged fruit.
Evergreen tree native to eastern and southern Asia. New leaves are deep purple-crimson before becoming glossy green above and blue-green below, while its acorn cups have distinctive concentric rings.
stories.edibilityNote: Acorns are edible; dried, ground acorns can be mixed with cereals as flour, and roasted seeds can substitute for coffee.

stories.summary: A slow-growing succulent shrub native to northwestern and north-central Namibia, it has a swollen base, large shiny leaves and grape-like fruits. It sheds its leaves during the drier winter, and its fruits are extremely poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: The grape-like fruits are extremely poisonous and should be avoided.

stories.summary: A small or medium-sized deciduous tree endemic to China. It sheds its leaves around December in the Northern Hemisphere and remains dormant through winter. Its valuable rosewood was used in Chinese furniture, and heavy exploitation left most commercially sized trees cut down by the early twenty-first century.
A herbaceous plant native to Taiwan and the Chinese areas of Guangdong, Hong Kong and Hainan. Its fruits are berries.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Eryngium galioides is associated with temporary pools and other seasonally waterlogged wetlands. In mainland Portugal, assessments conducted from 2016 to 2019 classified it as Vulnerable amid continuing habitat decline and threats including agricultural expansion, drainage and prolonged droughts.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Eryngium galioides
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A tree-form spurge native to the Arabian Peninsula, specifically the arid regions of Saudi Arabia and Yemen. Its cactus-like trunk and upward-curving branches form a candelabrum-shaped crown, and leaves appear at branch tips under suitably warm, humid conditions.

A low, spreading evergreen plant endemic to Madagascar, it naturally grows in dry forests, dry shrubland and rocky areas. It blooms from April to June, with flowers ranging from chartreuse and yellow-green to yellow or red, and is threatened by habitat loss.
A plant endemic to Madagascar. It occurs naturally in dry forests and dry shrubland and is threatened by habitat loss.

Perennial flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa in the western Mediterranean. It has a thick woody base, erect branching stems, yellow nectar glands and black seeds. It grows in forests and damp shrubland, especially beside temporary waterways and in troughs.
A plant native to Madagascar and Europa Island in the Mozambique Channel, it inhabits dry forests, dry shrubland and rocky areas. It is threatened by habitat loss.

An evergreen shrub endemic to the Azores, the Azores tree spurge has robust green stems and thick, leathery, dark blue-green leaves marked with white veins. Its large yellow-green flower heads are strongly honey-scented from May to June.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant is toxic if eaten; its milky white sap may also irritate skin or eyes.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation, including Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.

A substantial evergreen shrub endemic to Taiwan, where habitat loss threatens it. It has large, hand-shaped leaves and produces spherical clusters of cream or white winter flowers followed by black fruit in spring.

A cactus endemic to the Chihuahuan Desert of northeastern Mexico, where it grows on rocky limestone slopes. It may grow alone or in large clumps, bearing conspicuous red or yellow spines and rings of yellow-to-red flowers around its tip.
Tall semi-deciduous shrub or small tree endemic to the Azores. Fossils suggest it was also native to Madeira before becoming extinct there, and it is threatened by habitat loss.
A small flowering shrub found in Europe, including parts of Great Britain. It grows well in moist, nutrient-poor soil.
A flowering plant native to continental Portugal.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant native to western Mexico and Guatemala.

A small, slow-growing tree native from Mexico through Central America and Florida to the Caribbean and northern South America. Its exceptionally hard, heavy, self-lubricating wood can sink in water, while its dark green leaflets fold together during the hottest part of the day.
A flowering plant native only to Jamaica.

An annual flowering plant endemic to the southwestern coast of mainland Portugal. It grows in open patches on sandy-clay ground, including coastal scrub clearings, cliffs, rocks and dunes; it was assessed as Endangered in mainland Portugal, with ongoing habitat decline and uncertainty over its two northernmost populations.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Herniaria algarvica
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to coastal Portugal, Herniaria maritima inhabits clearings among creeping woodland and junipers on fixed coastal dunes. It grows on sandy soils that are neutral or alkaline.
A flowering perennial native to Western Europe. It forms greyish mats with creeping, rooting stems, rounded hairy leaves, and resin-scented yellow flowers whose petals are edged with red dots.
A small terrestrial herb of high Andean forests and páramo in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Venezuela and Bolivia. Its flowers are usually yellow or white, but are rarely purple or orange.

An evergreen shrub or small tree native to Madeira and the Canary Islands. It has glossy leaves with mostly rounded edges and few spines, though young leaves can be thorny, followed by small white flowers and red fruits.
Perennial plant found from eastern France to Sweden and in the mountains of Uzbekistan. Its leaves are woolly on both sides, and its small flower heads contain bright golden-yellow florets.

A tree fern native to parts of China and the western Malay Peninsula. It is often prostrate, forming colonies on open forest slopes and disturbed ground, and has a woolly rhizome. Extensive collection in Southeast Asia has reduced its populations.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.

A perennial aquatic herb native from Europe to Siberia and the western Himalaya, it grows in quiet freshwater such as ponds, lakes and slow streams. Its floating flowers have numerous white petals surrounding a red or yellow centre.

A perennial aquatic plant endemic to western Europe and associated with fast-flowing water. It lacks floating leaves, instead bearing long, narrow, tassel-like segments. White flowers rise above the water and have overlapping petals around a yellow centre.

Soft-wooded herbaceous plant native to much of Africa, including Madagascar, and southwestern and southern Asia. It is deep-rooted and often erect, with broad leaves and thick white flower clusters whose fibres were traditionally harvested in Arabia for stuffing cushions and saddle pads.

An aquatic flowering plant native to the Azores, Morocco, Iceland, the Faroes and most of Europe except the dry southeast. It usually grows submerged in nutrient-poor freshwater and takes in most of its carbon dioxide through its roots; if falling water exposes them, it stops using one of its two photosynthetic processes.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Littorella uniflora
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A small creeping herb found in shallow water around European lakes and pools. Its stems root where leaves emerge, and its yellow-green submerged foliage can turn bright green or reddish on exposed mud.

A flowering plant commonly found in New Zealand from sea level to about 900 metres. It has long, sword-like green leaves, sometimes with red midribs, followed by central green flowers in October and November and yellow-orange summer fruit.

A medium-sized tree fern native to New Zealand. It is slow-growing and long-lived, with a thick, soft, rusty-brown fibrous trunk and a distinctive skirt of retained dead leaves. A local Tauranga variety regularly branches into numerous forks.

A shrub or small tree with subspecies native to New Zealand and Norfolk Island, māhoe bears flowers and purple fruits directly on woody stems. Its fallen leaves often decay between the veins, leaving distinctive skeleton-like remains.

A deciduous shrub native to central and southern Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. It has white spring flowers and small black ripe fruits, which are edible raw or cooked but are bland and often made into jam, compote or spirits.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruits are edible raw or cooked; they are bland and often processed into jam, compote or spirits.

stories.summary: A climbing wild rose native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, it bears fragrant deep-pink flowers and relatively few thorns. Its oblong hips hang downwards.
A rhizomatous aquatic perennial native to subarctic and temperate Eurasia. Its submerged leaves are round and wrinkled, and its faintly fragrant yellow flowers have a star-shaped central disk.
A flowering plant native from Europe to the Russian Far East, commonly called eight-stamened waterwort.

An aquatic subshrub native across scattered parts of the Mediterranean, western and eastern Europe, the eastern Mediterranean and western Himalayas. It has simple, broad leaves and remains low-growing.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A compact evergreen fern endemic to New Zealand, where it grows in scrub and forests. Its fronds can carry more than 30 pairs of round, dark-green, leathery leaflets.
Wild barley native to Europe, including Madeira, Crimea and the northern Caucasus, as well as northwestern Africa and the Levant. It has been introduced to Australia and New Zealand.

A large cactus native to Baja California, Baja California Sur and Sonora in northwestern Mexico. It is exceptionally tall, heavily branched and bears large white flowers that open at night. Its fruits were traditionally an important food for the Seri people of Sonora.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruits were traditionally an important food for the Seri people of Sonora.

stories.summary: A columnar cactus endemic to Mexico, Indian comb forms a tall, many-branched tree. Its white flowers open in the evening and close by midday, while its golden-spined fruits split when ripe to reveal red, juicy pulp and black seeds.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten raw or cooked and made into syrup, preserves, jam or wine; the Mayo historically made foods from ground seeds and cornmeal.

stories.summary: A marine red alga of unspecified native origin, it occurs in Guam and the Houtman Abrolhos and was introduced to Hawaii from Guam in 1950. It reproduces sexually and through fragmentation, and even small amounts of remaining tissue can regrow rapidly.

A perennial flowering plant native to KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape in South Africa, it is widely grown in gardens. Its open-faced blue, purple or white flowers appear from late spring to summer, and its powerful roots can break concrete.
stories.edibilityNote: The leaves of subspecies orientalis are poisonous.

stories.summary: A large shrub or small tree native to Japan, Taiwan, southern and eastern China, and Vietnam, Taiwan cherry blooms early and has characteristic bell-shaped flowers. It is widely grown as an ornamental but is invasive in some parts of New Zealand.

Subtropical palm native to southern Japan, Taiwan, the Ryukyu Islands, southeastern China and Hainan. It has fan-shaped leaves and can become invasive in some wetlands and island ecosystems outside its native range.

A flowering tree native to eastern Australia, it may begin life growing on another plant or on rocks. Mature trees have spreading crowns and yellow-brown buttressed trunks; rusty leaf undersides help distinguish them from similar figs. Their small yellow figs ripen red throughout the year, especially in spring and summer.

An aquatic or semiterrestrial succulent originally from Australia and New Zealand. Its stiff shoots carry narrow opposite leaves, and it forms dense carpets along muddy pond margins or elongated growth underwater without dying back in winter.

A perennial grass native to most of Africa, southern Asia, southern Iran and Sicily, buffelgrass is deep-rooted and drought-tolerant. Where invasive, it spreads quickly, ignites readily and regrows rapidly after fire.

A flowering prickly poppy native to Mexico, Mexican poppy has sticky yellow sap. Introduced widely beyond Mexico, it has become invasive in Australia, Africa, tropical Asia, New Zealand and several oceanic islands.

A creeping plant native to dry parts of the Mediterranean Basin in North Africa, southern Europe and West Asia. It grows on rocky coastlines, with fleshy leaves, narrow-petalled violet flowers and many small fruits near its thorns.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Fagonia cretica
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A perennial herb native to the Canary Islands, southern Portugal and parts of the Mediterranean. It bears vivid yellow, daisy-like flowers with darker centres and thrives in dry coastal settings, often on sandy soil.

A small deciduous tree native to the Mediterranean region, including the Sahara in Morocco, and to Somalia. It has shiny green leaves and rounded dark-yellow fruit described as edible, although that claim is marked as needing citation.
stories.edibilityNote: The rounded dark-yellow fruit is described as edible, although the source marks this claim as needing citation.

stories.summary: Flowering plant native throughout the Mediterranean region. Its fruit is edible.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is edible; no preparation is specified.

stories.summary: Annual herb native to much of the United States, eastern Canada, Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean and Venezuela. It grows upright with paired oblong, finely toothed leaves that may be hairy or smooth. Its flower structures can be solitary or clustered, with flat white or red appendages surrounding the flowers.

An annual herb native to the Caribbean, Central America, Mexico, most of South America and most of the United States. Its slender, sometimes purple-tinted stems trail along the ground, bearing finely toothed oval leaves and tiny, often hard-to-detect flowers.

Annual herb native to the Americas, matted sandmat grows as a low mat of spreading stems that root where their joints touch the ground. Its tiny paired oval leaves accompany scalloped white, petal-like structures with red nectar glands.

Evergreen perennial native to China, India, Japan, Nepal and Vietnam. It forms ground-covering sod with narrow leaves, white to pale-lilac flowers and blue berries. Large spreading stems and tuberous roots grow underground.
An annual herb native to Australia and New Zealand. It has green or white flowers and favours well-drained sites, especially those with calcareous soils.

A palm native to northern and western Africa, the Levant and Arabian Peninsula. Its trunk forks into branches topped by fan-shaped leaves, while female trees bear woody, single-seeded fruits that remain on the tree for long periods.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit rind and pulp, unripe kernels, germinated seed shoots, young-fruit juice and sap are consumed in foods, drinks and palm wine.

stories.summary: Fast-growing evergreen tree native to New Zealand. It has a rounded crown of dense foliage and leathery, glossy yellow-green leaves. Small greenish flowers appear from late spring to midsummer, followed by dark purple or black berries that ripen from autumn to winter.

An evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand, tarata has yellow-green, curly-edged leaves that smell strongly of lemon when crushed. Fragrant yellow-cream spring flowers are followed by black seed capsules, and young conical trees become rounded as they mature.

A large deciduous oak tree native to most of Europe and extending into Anatolia and Iran, the sessile oak has stalked, evenly lobed leaves and stalkless acorns. Its male flowers appear in spring, and its acorns mature in about six months.

A green seaweed of unspecified native origin, it occurs widely in coastal waters and intertidal pools. It is bright green with a soft, silky texture and branches arranged in two opposite rows; fertile males become yellowish-green while females remain dark green.
A green alga found in the British Isles and other coastal locations. It forms bright green tubes or flat strips, often with ruffled edges, and is edible.
stories.edibilityNote: The species is edible and can be used as food.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub native to Mexico and Central America. It has a thick, often elephant-foot-like base and clumps of narrow, spineless leaves. In Central America, flower petals are eaten after the bitter anthers and ovaries are removed, then blanched and cooked; tender stem tips are eaten in El Salvador.
stories.edibilityNote: Flower petals are eaten after bitter reproductive parts are removed, then blanched and cooked; tender stem tips are eaten in El Salvador.

stories.summary: Large palm native to Mexico, the Caribbean, Florida and parts of Central America. It has a stout, exceptionally smooth grey-white trunk with a characteristic bulge beneath its green crown, while its fruit darkens from green through red to purplish-black.

Deciduous tree native to southern Mexico, El Salvador, Guatemala, Hispaniola, Honduras, Nicaragua and Cuba. It has succulent stems and fragrant, sticky, cotton-candy-pink flowers packed with hundreds of stamens. In Central America, a highly intoxicating drink is made from the tree, though the part and preparation are unspecified.
stories.edibilityNote: In Central America, a highly intoxicating drink is made from the tree; the part and preparation are unspecified.

stories.summary: A flowering tree native to Mexico, the American coral tree has bright red flowers shaped like little machetes. In southern Mexico, only the red part of the flower is boiled and cooked with scrambled eggs or tuna; the seeds and rest of the tree are described as highly toxic.
stories.edibilityNote: In southern Mexico, only the red flower parts are boiled and cooked with eggs or tuna; seeds and other parts are highly toxic.

stories.summary: A woody perennial tree found in Mexico, the southeastern USA, and parts of Central America and the Caribbean, it has reddish to red-purple bark that peels away in papery sheets. Its clustered flowers range from white to Mexican pink, while its ripe yellow fruit is edible and used in alcoholic drinks, syrups, jams and soups.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe fleshy fruits are edible; the sweet-and-sour fruits are used in alcoholic drinks, liqueurs, syrups, jams and soups.

stories.summary: An evergreen tree or shrub native to the tropical rainforests of West and Central Africa, the fiddle-leaf fig has large, leathery leaves shaped like a fiddle. Their prominent veins and wavy edges make the plant especially distinctive.

A deciduous plane tree native to northeastern and central Mexico and Guatemala. Its five-lobed leaves have dark, waxy upper surfaces and much paler undersides covered with fine white hairs, turning yellowish brown in autumn.
A flowering shrub native to eastern Madagascar, although its natural distribution is poorly understood. It has heart-shaped, serrated leaves and hanging clusters of fragrant pink flowers.
A plant endemic to Mexico and Mesoamerica. Its clear sap can blister or irritate skin, and ingestion can cause vomiting and diarrhea.
stories.edibilityNote: Ingestion can cause vomiting and diarrhea.

stories.summary: A perennial, semi-woody shrub reported from the North Atlantic region, especially dry grassy and rocky places across much of Europe. It has white flowers with yellow centres and evergreen, narrow leaves covered in greyish or whitish hairs, especially underneath.

A rhizomatous herbaceous perennial endemic to south-central Chile, it produces tall flower stalks and elongated leaves. Its lilac-to-whitish flowers have yellow bands and wine-red streaks on the inner segments.

A bulbous flowering perennial native to mainland Europe, excluding the British Isles, and Turkey. It grows in dry pastures, rocky places and open woods, producing narrow leaves and clusters of lily-like white flowers in spring and summer.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Anthericum liliago
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An asphodel-family plant native to North Africa, Southern Europe, the Middle East and South Asia, it has a fibrous root system. It has been introduced to Australia and the Mascarene Islands.

A flowering herb native to tropical and temperate Asia and Africa. It has succulent, triangular to egg-shaped leaves, while its inner flower parts enlarge into papery structures around persistent, hard red fruits with a netted pattern.
Small, stemless aloe native to South Africa. Its blue-green leaves have sometimes faint lengthwise lines and smooth pink margins, and it bears red flowers.

An orchid native to the Mediterranean, growing in damp meadows, open fields, marshes and sometimes scrub. Its flower spikes appear from April to May or early June, with lips ranging from yellowish through pink to magenta; southern English records may not be naturally occurring.
A perennial herb native to mainland Portugal. It inhabits peat bogs, marshes and other very wet places, usually near the coast, and has disappeared from several historically recorded sites.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Rhynchospora modesti-lucennoi
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An aquatic fern native to numerous countries across Africa and Asia, as well as Brazil, Trinidad and Tobago, and several Indian Ocean islands. It creeps and spreads in water but may form cushions on land, with adults typically growing terrestrially. It is eaten in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, though the plant part and preparation are not specified.
stories.edibilityNote: Eaten in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh; the plant part and preparation are not specified.

stories.summary: A small, delicate fern occurring across the Mediterranean basin, it depends on seasonal flooding in temporary freshwater pools. Its spores survive the dry period but germinate only when the ground is completely saturated.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Pilularia minuta
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering water-plantain, this species includes the subspecies baetica, which is native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant in the mustard family, recorded from mainland Portugal and the Azores. The supplied account does not give an unambiguous native origin.

A small red marine alga whose native origin is not stated, it grows upright with cylindrical, repeatedly branched filaments. It occurs in rock pools and shallow coastal waters across the British Isles, but is very difficult to distinguish from some related species.

Salt-loving annual succulent found beside saline water in Europe. Its jointed bright-green stems turn red or purple in autumn, and it has tiny scale-like leaves. It is edible raw or cooked and is usually cooked in unsalted water because of its high salt content.
stories.edibilityNote: It is eaten raw or cooked and is usually boiled in plenty of unsalted water because the plant is naturally salty.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to Mexico, it grows mainly in deserts or dry shrubland. Many small, green succulent leaves cluster densely around its stems.

A spreading evergreen shrub native to China and the Himalayas, bright bead cotoneaster has arching greenish to purple-black branches and leaves with hairy undersides when young. Clusters of berries appear after its white flowers.

A deciduous shrub native to Japan, Korea and northeastern China, border privet has relatively small leaves. It is invasive in parts of the United States and has become particularly common around southern New England, the mid-Atlantic and the Great Lakes.

A perennial herb native to Eurasia, from Europe east to western Siberia, autumn hawkbit has branched stems bearing several bright yellow flower heads. It flowers from June to October and is frequent in damp grassland and meadows.

A perennial sedge of circumboreal mountain regions, tufted bulrush grows in wet, acidic bogs, moorland and heaths. It forms dense tufts of wiry stems, with leaves reduced to pointed basal sheaths and very small brownish flower heads at the tips.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Trichophorum cespitosum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to Europe and now widespread in the United States. Its pink or lavender flower clusters rise above sticky stem areas that trap small insects, although the plant is not currently regarded as carnivorous.

An annual grass native to Eurasia and naturalized in North America. Its harsh, hairy stems, leaves and flower branches bear reddish spikelets with long awns. Its seeds and awns can penetrate livestock skin, mouths, eyes and intestines.

A low-growing, hairless perennial flowering plant native to Europe and Western Asia, lesser celandine has fleshy, heart-shaped dark green leaves and glossy bright yellow flowers. It emerges in late winter and can form extensive carpets; in North America it is introduced and invasive. Raw plants are poisonous, but cooking or drying removes toxicity, and Mesolithic Europeans ate the roots boiled, fried or roasted.
stories.edibilityNote: Cooked or dried plants have been eaten; Mesolithic Europeans ate roots boiled, fried or roasted. Raw plants are poisonous.

stories.summary: A perennial herb native to eastern Asia. Its summer flowers are orange-red with darker spots, and its autumn seed pods open to reveal shiny black seed clusters resembling blackberries.

A perennial flowering rush from northwestern Africa, almost all of Europe and the Caucasus, and introduced elsewhere. It forms large, dense tufts with vivid green, ribbed stems and a spherical flower head that appears to grow from the stem's side.

Perennial flowering plant native to Europe, western Asia and parts of the Middle East. It is the only member of its genus with yellow flowers and has square stems with paired, toothed leaves that may bear silvery markings.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

Downy perennial flowering plant native to Eurasia. It has strongly veined, unstalked leaves and tiny greenish-white, funnel-shaped flowers that appear in June and July. The fruits split into four shiny white nutlets that can persist into winter.

A small annual flowering plant native to Europe and parts of North Africa, possibly extending into western Asia, it is usually grey-green and covered with short, fluffy hairs. Its tiny yellow flower heads begin as five-sided pyramids and open into star shapes.
Small perennial herb native widely across North America and Eurasia. It grows in moist soils and seasonal pools.
Plant species native to much of Europe and Asia. Known as sickle alfalfa or yellow lucerne, it forms a nitrogen-fixing partnership with the bacterium Sinorhizobium meliloti.
An aquatic plant widespread across Europe and Asia and naturalized in many other regions. It generally grows in wet places at lower elevations.

Flowering plant native to the central United States, it may grow as an annual, biennial or perennial. Its simple leaves alternate along the stem, while its four-petalled flowers range from white or pink to red.

Biennial flowering plant native to eastern and central North America, reaching north to Quebec. Its upper flowering stems have soft white hairs, and its light pink flowers turn vivid red-pink in late summer to early autumn.

An herb native to Southeast Asia, small water-pepper has creeping, slender stems, narrow tapering leaves and minute pale-violet flowers. In Malaysia and Indonesia, its shoots and young leaves are eaten raw in salads, used to flavour peppery dishes, or made into tea.
stories.edibilityNote: In Malaysia and Indonesia, shoots and young leaves are eaten raw in salads, added to peppery dishes for aroma, or used as tea leaves.

stories.summary: A low-growing succulent native to rocky upland meadows in Georgia, northern Iran and northeastern Turkey. Its creeping stems root as they spread, while its flowers range from white to deep red and its upper leaves turn burgundy in autumn.

A deciduous shrub or small tree native to the listed regions of mainland Portugal. It is highly branched and sometimes thorny, with twisting reddish-brown branches and white flowers. Its fruit may be eaten cooked or raw when fully ripe; the flowers and oil contained in the seeds are also edible.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit is eaten cooked or raw when fully ripe; flowers are used as garnish or tea, and the seed contains edible oil.

stories.summary: A climbing perennial rose native to the Mediterranean, the evergreen rose has very prickly stems and glossy leaves that persist through much of winter. Its slightly fragrant white flowers bloom from May to July.
An annual herb of the Old World, ranging from North Africa through Europe into Asia.

A flowering plant native across Europe eastward to West Siberia and Kazakhstan. It usually grows in fens and damp meadows, though continental records include oakwoods and hot, dry limestone. Crushed foliage has a mildly parsley-like scent.
stories.edibilityNote: Food or seasoning records are hard to find, but the plant is not listed as poisonous.

stories.summary: Deciduous shrub native to the Carpathian Mountains of Romania and western Ukraine. It bears strongly fragrant, dark pink flowers in slender clusters in early summer and has a very restricted wild range.

A slow-growing, slender date palm native to southeastern Asia, from southwestern China through northern Laos to northern Vietnam. Its many grey-green leaflets droop slightly, and it bears small yellowish flowers followed by edible, thin-fleshed, date-like fruit.
stories.edibilityNote: The small, thin-fleshed, date-like fruit is edible.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to central and southern Mexico. Its thick, dark-green, spiny leaves form a spiral rosette and leave imprints on underlying leaves. It flowers once, usually after 15–25 years, producing a tall stalk of greenish-yellow flowers before dying.

A cactus native to Mexico in North America. It forms a tree-like shrub with upright branches and yellow-to-orange flowers; its yellow-green, red-tinged fruit is edible but bears small bristles and spines.
stories.edibilityNote: The yellow-green, red-tinged fruit is edible and is covered with small bristles and spines.

stories.summary: A small succulent perennial found in the Chihuahuan Desert of Coahuila, Durango and Nuevo León, Mexico. Its compact rosettes have rigid green leaves patterned with distinctive white lines, usually without marginal teeth but ending in one to three spines.

A tree-forming flowering plant native to Puebla and northern Oaxaca in Mexico, it is endemic to the Tehuacán Valley scrubland. Older plants develop a greatly swollen trunk base and carry erect, blue-grey leaves with finely rough, sharp margins.

A small evergreen shrub native from Italy north to Austria and Slovakia and east to Turkey and Crimea. It has flattened, leaf-like stems bearing tiny true leaves and yellow flowers; male and female flowers occur on separate plants, and red berries are rarely produced.

Shrubby cactus occurring in the temperate, dry parts of central Mexico. It can form closed stands and has unusually large pads; its yellow flowers mature into reddish, sweet-and-sour fruit used for drinks, preserves, sweets and spirits.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is prepared as fresh juice, preserves, sweets, crystallized fruit, dried fruit, wine and spirits.

stories.summary: A fleshy perennial native to the Mediterranean Basin and Middle East, from the Azores to Oman. It has very succulent dark-green leaf rosettes and pale-green, bell-shaped flowers held horizontally rather than drooping.
An orchid occurring from Peru to Bolivia.
Tree native to Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador. It has a swollen trunk base, furrowed bark and slender leaves, and grows in deciduous tropical forests.
An evergreen flowering perennial endemic to eastern Mexico, elephant’s-foot is not a true palm. It has a greatly swollen, water-storing trunk base and terminal tufts of recurved, leathery leaves.

Tree endemic to Oaxaca, Mexico, where it grows in dry forests and shrublands. Its stem expands into a large circular base beneath long, straight, thin leaves. It is considered vulnerable and is threatened by habitat conversion and illegal collection for ornamental trade.
An orchid native from Chiapas in southern Mexico through Central America to Costa Rica. It is Costa Rica's national flower.

A flowering shrub native to the tropical Americas from extreme southern Mexico and Belize through much of Central America and northern South America, including many Caribbean islands. It grows upright on cane-like stems and has large green leaves, often patterned with white. Its sap is toxic, and ingesting any part may cause severe reactions or death.
stories.edibilityNote: The entire plant contains calcium oxalate crystals; ingestion may cause anaphylactic shock, respiratory failure or death.

stories.summary: Flowering vine of unspecified native origin, widespread across much of Central and South America. Its thick, waxy, heart-shaped leaves have large oval holes.

A palm found throughout Mexico and Central America, it grows in colonies from short horizontal stems at or below ground, forming dense or open clumps. Its round fruits turn from green to black or purple-black as they ripen.
An evergreen, trunk-forming shrub native to the Chihuahuan Desert and other dry habitats of northeastern Mexico. It grows slowly and bears exceptionally long, narrow blade-like leaves.
An orchid occurring from Mexico to Colombia and southeastern Brazil. Its seeds are exceptionally small.
A cactus endemic to Mexico’s Central Plateau. It is the largest and tallest Astrophytum species, with a solitary cylindrical body, white woolly flakes and canary-yellow summer flowers.
A cactus native to central Mexico. Its solitary spherical stems are covered in white down and spines, and its reddish-purple spring and summer flowers sometimes form a complete ring around the tip.

A flowering cactus native to northeastern Mexico. Its clustered round stems are hidden beneath white, downy spines with long hairs arranged like bird-feather segments. White or greenish-yellow flowers appear in late summer.
Cactus native to southern Mexico, where it is endemic to moist lowland rainforest. It has unusual flat, leaf-like stems and fragrant flowers that open for only one night.

An evergreen succulent native to semi-desert areas of Mexico and common throughout Puebla, the Mexican firecracker forms rounded rosettes of fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves covered in irritating white hairs. In spring it produces red flowers with yellow tips on tall stalks.
Cactus native to Mexico, where it is common and widespread across much of the country.

A flowering cactus from Hidalgo, Mexico, the rattail cactus grows on rocks or other plants in dry forests and seems rare and seldom collected in the wild. Its profusely branching stems eventually trail and bear bristle-like spines, while its scentless crimson flowers open by day for three to five days.

Evergreen succulent perennial native to semi-desert habitats in Mexico. It forms compact rosettes of pale blue-green fleshy leaves and bears pink, yellow-tipped flowers in winter and spring. It also produces multiple offsets.
Perennial succulent native to Oaxaca, Mexico. It grows slowly and has a distinctive pink colour.

A deciduous tree native to Mexico and endemic to cloud forests in northern Oaxaca, this magnolia has exceptionally broad leaves and large white flowers. It was once thought extinct but was rediscovered in 1977.

A short-trunked plant from northeastern Mexico, Berlandier’s sotol grows on open rocky ground and in open woodland. Its thin, waxy blue leaves vary in appearance and have irregular upward-pointing edge spines. Numerous green to yellow flowers appear from May to June on a tall, narrow, woody flower stalk.

Cactus native to north-central Mexico, growing on canyon walls and volcanic rock in semi-desert. White hair-like spines conceal radial and hooked central spines; cream flowers are followed by cylindrical red fruit.

A cylindrical cactus endemic to Guerrero and Morelos in central Mexico, it inhabits dry tropical forest and arid scrub at roughly 1,600–1,900 metres. Red-brown or white spines cover the stem, while pink funnel-shaped flowers form a ring around its tip and produce bright red berries.

A solitary cactus of unstated native origin, it is distributed across Coahuila, Durango, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas in Mexico. Its blue-green body bears abundant milky sap and a strong black central spine, while its flowers range from whitish to vivid pink or crimson.

A cluster-forming cactus native to Jalisco and Aguascalientes in western-central Mexico. Dense white wool surrounds its tightly packed tubercles and numerous white spines, with longer curved brown spines standing out. Rings of deep pink flowers appear across the upper surface in spring and summer.

Tree fern native to the tropical and subtropical Americas, from southern Mexico through Central and South America. It has an upright cylindrical trunk and large, twice-divided fronds, and illegal extraction puts it at risk of extinction.

Herbaceous perennial native to temperate Europe, Mediterranean Europe, North Africa, western Asia, the Caucasus, Iraq and Iran. It has square stems with conspicuous winged corners, while its paired leaves bear many translucent dots and its pale yellow flowers grow in clusters.
A flowering plant whose native origin is stated only for subsp. crispa, which is endemic to mainland Portugal.

A flowering plant from Europe and the Mediterranean, early star-of-Bethlehem usually blooms from January to March or April. It has yellow, six-petalled flowers and twisting, thread-like basal leaves, and grows mainly in dry grassland.

Tree endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. Its rough, flaky or fibrous trunk bark contrasts with smoother pale bark above, and it bears white flowers in groups of seven; honey produced from it is renowned for its quality.
stories.edibilityNote: Honey produced from the tree is renowned for its quality.

stories.summary: A large woodland and forest tree native to eastern Australia, it has fibrous grey bark and a broad, often gnarled form. Cream-white flowers appear from November to March, and it typically grows on floodplains and along watercourses in alluvial soils.
A tree endemic to southeastern Australia. It has smooth white-to-yellowish bark, lance-shaped adult leaves and white flowers, with flower buds grouped in threes or sevens depending on subspecies.

A small to medium-sized tree endemic to southeastern Australia. Its smooth, powdery grey or pink bark peels in long ribbons, and it has white flowers in groups of three followed by woody cup-shaped or bell-shaped fruit.
Shrub-like perennial native to Mexico, tree stonecrop is a hardy garden plant whose leaves turn red in winter.

A trailing annual herb, Algerian tea occurs around the Mediterranean in dry or disturbed ground, dunes and ditches. Its tiny flowers are gathered in clusters and surrounded by conspicuous silvery, scale-like bracts.
A plant native to Mexico, Central America and South America. It has very short leaf stalks and small leaves and was traditionally used in Peruvian herbal medicine.
A flowering sedge found across most of Europe, including Britain, as well as Northwest Asia and North America. It can grow into a tall tussock.
A red alga distributed throughout tropical to warm-temperate waters worldwide. In Hawaiian cuisine it is a bitter, iodine-like condiment traditionally added to poke.
stories.edibilityNote: Traditionally used in Hawaiian cuisine as a bitter condiment and poke ingredient.

stories.summary: A flowering shrub native to tropical Asia, specifically Malesia and Papuasia, chenille plant has separate male and female plants. Female plants bear long, hanging clusters of furry purple-to-bright-red flowers, with large leaves ranging from bright green to reddish copper.
A palm tree endemic to Palawan and Danjugan Island in the Philippines. Its fruits become bright scarlet, usually in winter, inspiring the name Christmas palm.
stories.edibilityNote: Its fruits are sometimes said to substitute for betel nut in buyo prepared for chewing.

stories.summary: A dwarf evergreen shrub or small tree of unknown wild origin, found in Japan and Taiwan. It has bright green oval leaves with rounded or notched tips and is widely shaped into hedges, topiary and bonsai.

A grass-like sedge native to West Africa, Madagascar and the Arabian Peninsula, umbrella papyrus is widely grown as an ornamental in gardens, ponds, pots and homes. It needs abundant moisture, can grow in shallow water and requires protection from cold weather.

A tall, branching annual herb of uncertain origin, with one subspecies originating in India and another in America. Young leaves are hairy and magenta before turning green. Its young shoots and leaves are eaten cooked, or raw in small quantities, while the seeds are prepared like rice or quinoa or ground for flour.
stories.edibilityNote: Young shoots and leaves are cooked or eaten raw sparingly; seeds are cooked like grain or ground into flour.

stories.summary: A perennial clover native to Europe. It grows in grassy places, mainly on clay soils, and has yellowish-white flowers.

An erect or reclining herb widespread across Europe, Asia, Africa and Canada, false cleavers is considered a noxious weed in many places. It has square stems, narrow leaves arranged in whorls and white or yellow-green flowers.
A palm native and endemic to Round Island, Mauritius. Its trunk swells near the base and tapers upward, and it carries only four to six open leaves at a time.
Aquatic plant native to Southern Africa. It is used in freshwater aquariums but is invasive in some countries and legally restricted in the European Union.

An evergreen tree native to China, banana shrub bears strongly fragrant cream-white flowers, sometimes with yellow or purple colouring. Its flower buds and new leaves have a velvet-like covering, while mature leaves are leathery and glossy dark green.
A plant native from the Solomon Islands to Vanuatu. It is widely grown as an ornamental beyond its native range and has been introduced to many tropical countries.
Azalea species native to southern and western Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu and Yakushima in Japan. Its many cultivars include the Satsuki azaleas.

An evergreen tree native to South and Southeast Asia, although its exact origin is unknown. It has yellow flowers and compound leaves with paired leaflets, and is often planted for shade in cocoa, coffee and tea plantations.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves, tender pods and seeds are eaten in Burmese and Thai cooking only after boiling and discarding the water; buds also feature in Burmese dishes.

stories.summary: An aquatic flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. A 2020 mainland assessment found it very scattered, absent from many historical sites but present in some newly discovered populations, and classified it as Vulnerable.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Groenlandia densa

stories.summary: A perennial vine native to Europe, with paired, pointed leaves and small star-shaped flowers ranging from dark purple to black. Its slender seed pods contain seeds with fluffy tufts that carry them on the wind.

A perennial plant occurring from northeastern Spain through central Mediterranean countries to northern Europe, Asia Minor and Tunisia. It has glossy leaflets, pale yellow flowers and segmented cylindrical seed pods, and usually grows in sunny, warm, dry scrub or woodland margins.

A low-growing succulent flowering plant typical of the Mediterranean region. It has creeping stems, paired turquoise-green or grey-green leaves, and small white flowers dotted with black, often growing among rocks and rural tuff walls.
A palm tree native to Mexico and parts of Central America. It produces nuts used as vegetable ivory and is also used to make cohune oil.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A grey-green, short-lived perennial herb native to the Mediterranean region. It forms a basal leaf rosette and conspicuous blue-purple, or sometimes white, flowerheads that are popular in dried arrangements.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Catananche caerulea
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant whose typical variety is native to mainland Portugal, Scorzonera angustifolia is known there as narrow-leaved scorzonera. That variety is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A hardy herbaceous perennial native to France, Spain, Portugal and Morocco. It has grey-green foliage and upright clusters of delicate white flowers with purple stamens in early summer.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Lysimachia ephemerum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant in the aster family, it includes the subspecies Tragopogon crocifolius subsp. crocifolius, which is native to mainland Portugal.
A tuberous herbaceous perennial native to the western Mediterranean region, including southwestern Europe and northwestern Africa. It produces dense spikes of purple flowers in spring.

A flowering shrub native to the Indian subcontinent, Tibet, Sichuan and Yunnan in China, and Myanmar. It is low, spreading and rabbit-tolerant, making it suitable for rock gardens and hedges, though it can become invasive.
Succulent flowering plant native to Mexico. It has soft, spineless leaves and, after many years, produces an unusually curved, swan-neck-like flower cluster before the flowering rosette dies.

Small fern native to northern Atlantic islands and adjacent western and southwestern Europe. It usually grows on exposed coastal clifftops and has one pointed leaf blade beside a narrow, spore-bearing spike.

An annual flowering plant native to Mediterranean Europe, it has fern-like divided leaves and flat clusters of pure white flowers. Unevenly sized florets give the blooms a memorable lace-like appearance throughout much of summer.

Wild rose native to Europe, found mostly in southern Europe and occasionally as far as the Caucasus. It resembles sweet briar but has smaller leaves, white-to-blush petals and very little scent from its flowers or leaves.
A perennial flowering plant native to Europe. It bears clear blue, five-petalled flowers after producing teardrop-shaped buds in early summer, followed by small beige ball-shaped seed heads.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Linum narbonense
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, hairy ironwort belongs to the mint family.
Flowering plant with the subspecies Dipcadi serotinum subsp. serotinum native to mainland Portugal.

A scrambling shrubby vine native to central and western China. It is practically thornless, though stout shoots may carry a few prickles. Its small, fragrant white or pale-yellow flowers are among the earliest roses, usually opening in May in the Northern Hemisphere but later after cold weather.

Herbaceous perennial native to the Mediterranean area. It has waxy, channelled basal leaves and funnel-shaped white flowers from April through June; in ancient Greece its roots were a staple food, while roasted stalks and seeds were also eaten.
stories.edibilityNote: In ancient Greece, roots were a staple food; roasted stalks and seeds were also eaten.

stories.summary: A seaweed found widely in warm tropical waters, including parts of the Atlantic, Caribbean and Pacific. Its pale to dark-green, feather-like upright fronds rise from a shared creeping stem anchored into sandy seabeds.
A tree found from Mexico to Costa Rica in dry deciduous forests. Young trunks bear large conical thorns, while the giant fruits enclose seeds in soft white fibre formerly used to stuff mattresses.
A tree native to various parts of Latin America, it can grow tall and bears petal-free male and female flowers on the same plant. It occurs in cleared farmland, forest plains and rocky hillsides.

A fruit tree native to Central and South America. Its often twisted pods contain seeds surrounded by sweet, cottony white pulp, which is eaten raw and likened to ice cream. The seeds are reported edible only when cooked.
stories.edibilityNote: The sweet white pulp is eaten raw; seeds are reported edible only after cooking, which destroys trypsin and chymotrypsin inhibitors.

stories.summary: A flowering tree native from central Mexico south to Nicaragua, it bears thick thorns at the nodes of young branches. Its large, ribbed yellow-green fruit grows directly from the trunk and branches and is eaten raw, cooked, pickled or preserved.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten raw or cooked and is sometimes pickled or made into preserves.

stories.summary: An evergreen tree or shrub native across the Caribbean, Mexico, Central America and northern South America. It has a dense rounded crown, strongly fragrant greenish-white flowers, and round capsules that open to reveal seeds with brightly coloured coverings.

Tree or spreading shrub endemic to New Zealand and now known only from the northern South Island. Its bark peels in long strips, and young branches tend to droop. Crowded white or pale-pink flowers can make whole hillsides look snow-covered.

A flowering subshrub endemic to Australia, false sarsaparilla grows prostrate or climbs, with leathery leaves and clusters of mostly purple flowers, though other colours sometimes occur. It can regrow from its roots after fire.

A flowering plant native to South African woodlands and Eswatini. It has arching strap-like leaves and showy red, orange or yellow flowers, sometimes with a faint sweet scent. It contains small amounts of lycorine and is poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: Contains small amounts of lycorine and is poisonous.

stories.summary: A plant native to the Mediterranean basin, coastal medick is now found worldwide. It forms a partnership with a nitrogen-fixing bacterium.

Herbaceous flowering plant native to the Mediterranean region. It has bright blue flowers and blackish roots that are blue-red inside; the roots yield a red dye used since antiquity and to colour some cheeses and wines.
stories.edibilityNote: Root dye colours some cheeses and low-quality wines; alkannin is approved as food colouring in Australia, but EU approval has been withdrawn.

stories.summary: An orchid native around the Mediterranean from southwestern Europe and northern Africa to western Asia, its flower resembles a female sand bee and attracts males for pollination. Most subspecies are pollinated by male Andrena bees.

An evergreen perennial found throughout the Mediterranean Basin, with feathery branches of needle-like modified stems and small greenish-white to yellowish flowers. Along the Croatian coast and islands, its spring shoots are gathered for risottos or fried with scrambled eggs.
stories.edibilityNote: Spring shoots are gathered along the Croatian coast and islands, then used in risottos or fried with scrambled eggs.

stories.summary: A dwarf, deciduous perennial native to southwestern France and Spain, Crocus nudiflorus produces deep-purple to lilac-purple flowers in late summer or autumn. Its leaves emerge later, during winter and spring, and its underground corms spread by runners to form clumps.
Flowering plant found in the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa.
A subshrub native to Kenya and Tanzania. It has succulent stems that become woody near the base, year-round pink or white flowers, and mature fruit capsules that burst open.

Bulbous perennial herb regarded as native to Belize, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru and Venezuela. It bears large, white, vanilla-scented flowers, and its unusually succulent seeds may be up to 90% water.

An evergreen shrub native to southern East Asia, mainland Southeast Asia and northeastern South Asia, it has glossy dark-green leaves. Its strongly fragrant white flowers bloom in summer and autumn, gradually becoming creamy yellow and waxy.
stories.edibilityNote: Flowers are reported eaten raw, pickled or preserved in honey; in China, petals are used to scent tea.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to Portugal and Spain.

A large, semi-evergreen shrub endemic to much of southern and eastern Africa, from Kenya and Angola south. It has drooping branches, textured sage-like leaves and strongly scented flowers ranging from white and cream to mauve and purple.
An orchid native to the western Mediterranean and Macaronesia. Its stem bears two unequal leaves with heart-shaped bases, while its yellowish-green flowers resemble small bells.
A flowering plant native to Morocco, Portugal and western Spain. It typically produces only one leaf.
A flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula and northern Morocco, it grows in pastures, dry farmland, fallow ground and uncultivated fields, mainly on limestone-derived soils.
A small flowering plant native to Europe and parts of North Africa and the Middle East.

Bulbous perennial flowering plant native to Mediterranean Europe and North Africa. Its long, shiny leaves can conceal the short stem, while its large, lightly spicy-scented flowers are usually shades of blue; white wild forms occur occasionally.

A fern whose natural range is centred on southern South America, from Araucanía south to Cape Horn and from the Chilean coast to the Magellanic forest tree line, including nearby Argentina. It also occurs in Australia and some Pacific islands.

A poisonous perennial vine occurring in North Africa and the southern Iberian Peninsula, from Algeria to Portugal. It is usually an evergreen climber, though it rarely trails along the ground, and bears brownish-purple to reddish flowers.
Flowering plant whose subspecies Linaria aeruginea subsp. aeruginea is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.

Perennial herb native to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula and northwestern Africa. It usually grows in moist places near waterways and bears flowers ranging from orange-red or orange-purple to greenish yellow with orange spots.

A herbaceous European lily widespread from Spain to Finland and Ukraine. It bears scentless bright yellow-orange flowers with reddish-brown dots; only the eastern variety consistently produces small aerial bulbs in the upper leaf axils.
True lily native to the Balkans and Middle East. Unlike other lilies, it forms a winter rosette that dies the following summer, followed by pure-white, strongly fragrant flowers with yellow throats.
stories.edibilityNote: In Taiwan, its flowers and bulbs are used as food.

stories.summary: A stem-rooting lily endemic to Taiwan and Japan's Ryukyu Islands. It bears outward-facing, trumpet-shaped white flowers with a strong fragrance. Like most true lilies, it is highly toxic to cats.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A flowering shrub native to southern Texas, Mexico, the Caribbean, Central America and South America. Its aromatic leaves are used as a cooking herb in Ethiopia and to flavour foods such as Oaxacan mole sauces.
stories.edibilityNote: In Ethiopia it is used in spiced butter; its leaves also flavour foods including Oaxacan mole sauces.

stories.summary: A herbaceous evergreen perennial native to East Asia, where it grows beneath shady forests in China, Japan and Korea. It forms clumps of arching, grass-like leaves, with white to violet-purple flower spikes followed by blackish berries that may persist into winter.

A fruit tree native to warm regions of Asia. Its rough red-skinned fruit has translucent, juicy flesh eaten fresh or processed into juice, preserves and dried fruit, although the fruit of L. c. philippensis is inedible.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten fresh or processed into juice, preserves and dried fruit; L. c. philippensis bears inedible fruit.

stories.summary: A moss distributed across the Northern Hemisphere and Madagascar. It forms extensive, loose yellow-green to brown-green mats of sturdy, irregularly tree-shaped shoots and rarely produces spore capsules.

An orchid native to the Mediterranean and Caspian Sea regions, from Portugal and Morocco to Iran and Turkmenistan. In mainland Portugal, it grows in dry, sunny meadows and scrub clearings on limestone soils. Assessments conducted there in 2016–2019 classified it as Critically Endangered, with only two known subpopulations.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Anacamptis collina
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An aquatic plant native to Australia, it occurs most commonly in shallow, stagnant water. Its whorled leaves change from thread-like underwater forms to thicker intermediate leaves and smooth linear forms, and its female flowers lack petals.

An herbaceous biennial native to the western and central Mediterranean Basin, it occurs across southern Europe and North Africa. Its two accepted subspecies have partly separate ranges, one mainly European and the other spanning Spain and northwestern Africa.
Plant native to France, Spain and Portugal, naturalized in the United Kingdom and cultivated elsewhere. It is also sometimes treated as a subspecies of another daffodil.

An aquatic perennial found mainly in western Europe, with scattered populations elsewhere, including North Africa and Newfoundland. It grows from creeping underground stems in shallow, nutrient-poor water and produces delicate submerged leaves that usually decay after its floating leaves appear.

An orchid native to Asia Minor and parts of Europe and North Africa, the dense-flowered orchid forms a basal rosette of oblong leaves above round underground nodules. From April to June, upright stems bear clusters of small white to pink flowers.
An orchid native to the Mediterranean Basin and Europe’s Atlantic coast. Its flower spike carries greyish-pink flowers whose sepals and petals form a hood.
Highly variable orchid native to Europe and the Middle East. Its flowers resemble spiders, with yellow-green sepals and a velvety red-brown lip marked by a distinctive silvery-blue H.

A flowering plant with no explicitly stated native origin, it is found from Mexico and the West Indies to subtropical South America. It grows in habitats ranging from tropical savanna and forest to mountains, shrubland and grassland, and has not been documented north of Mexico.

Evergreen perennial native to Argentina and Chile, with clumps of grey-green, sword-shaped leaves. Its creamy white, cup-shaped flowers have golden centres and bloom from May to June in the Northern Hemisphere.

A hardy flowering bulb native to the Pyrenees of southwestern France and northwestern Spain, it bears deep purple early-summer flowers with yellow markings. Its stiff, sword-shaped dark green to teal leaves begin growing in early spring, before the snow has fully melted.

Bulbous flowering plant native to eastern South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, where it grows in wet areas near streams, marshes and drainages. It has lance-shaped leaves and deep orange to orange-brown flowers, and has escaped cultivation and become established in parts of the United Kingdom.

Creeping flowering herb native from western Asia through India to East and Southeast Asia. It resembles a true strawberry but has yellow flowers, while the common variety bears glossy red fruit. Its fresh berries are edible but less palatable than true strawberries.
stories.edibilityNote: Fresh berries are edible but less palatable than true strawberries; Khasi people also chew the roots with betel nuts.

stories.summary: A moss with a cosmopolitan distribution across climates ranging from the Arctic to deserts. When wet, it is bright green with loose leaves; when dry, the leaves wrap around its stems and turn reddish brown. It can remain dormant through years of drying and resume activity after rehydration.

A bulb-bearing herbaceous perennial native to the western Mediterranean region of Iberia, Italy and northwest Africa. It produces a dense, pyramid-shaped cluster of numerous blue flowers; its foliage dies back in summer and reappears in autumn.
A flowering bromeliad native to Chile. It can grow on other plants or in well-drained soil, and bears edible fruits resembling those of Greigia sphacelata but smaller, eaten in the same way.
stories.edibilityNote: The smaller fruits resemble those of Greigia sphacelata and are eaten in the same way.

stories.summary: A sedge with no stated native origin, it occurs from Western Asia through southern Europe to northwest Africa. It grows on rocky and grassy slopes.

A perennial shrub native to Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela. Its clustered tubular flowers gradually change from yellow to red, creating a marmalade-like display against dark green oval or elliptical leaves.
Fern native from the southern United States through Mexico, the Caribbean and Central America to western South America. It grows in rocky hammocks and moist forests.

Herbaceous perennial tuberous plant native to the Mediterranean region, the poppy anemone bears single, showy flowers with black centres. Wild flowers are usually red but may be white or blue, blooming from winter to early spring in their native range.

A highly variable tree occurring along Australia’s east coast, coastal banksia ranges from a small, gnarled shrub in exposed sites to a tall tree in shelter. Its leaves contrast dark green upper surfaces with white undersides, and its densely packed flower spikes are usually pale yellow to yellow.
stories.edibilityNote: Historically, Indigenous Australians consumed its nectar by licking stroked hands or steeping flower spikes overnight; early settlers used the nectar as syrup.

stories.summary: A semi-evergreen, clump-forming perennial native to western Europe, including Britain, France, Spain and Portugal. Its long, narrow leaves are usually spotted white or pale green, while its spring flowers change from pink to blue or violet.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

Annual herb native to coastal western Europe, where it grows on sandy dunes and heaths. It forms low, greyish, hairy rosettes with pale, usually paired flowers; its fruits resemble tiny storks’ bills and open to reveal feathery seed appendages.
A flowering plant native from western and northern Europe east to northern Russia.

A perennial flowering herb native to Atlantic Europe, including England, western France and the northwestern Iberian Peninsula, it grows on coastal cliffs and dune grassland. It was assessed as Endangered in 2001.

A flowering plant found around the Mediterranean Basin and extending into northwestern Europe. Its upper leaves join around the stiff stems, and it bears bright yellow flowers. It grows in chalk or limestone grassland and on dunes.

A flowering plant found mainly in western and Mediterranean Europe and also in southern Australia. Its four-petalled yellow flowers, sometimes tinged pink, open only in sunlight, and it grows around seasonally flooded pools and on sandy or peaty acid grassland.
A flowering plant native from Europe to China.

A succulent perennial endemic to central Mexico’s Sierra Mixteca. Its branched stems may stand upright or spread along the ground, while its blue-grey, cylindrical leaves develop reddish tips in dry conditions.

A mat-forming perennial herb native to Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean. Its stems root at their joints, enabling it to spread vegetatively into dense ground cover that can prevent other plants from regenerating.
A perennial herb native to the Caribbean and South America. Its banana-like leaves accompany upright flower clusters with red bracts and pale-yellow tubular flowers.

A small evergreen perennial native to Japan, where it grows on open and forested slopes. It forms grasslike leaf tufts above short rhizomes and bears purple or white flowers; the ‘Kokuryu’ cultivar develops nearly black leaves and black berries.
A large, tree-like yucca of the far southeastern Chihuahuan Desert, occurring in northeastern Mexico. It may branch and bears snowy white flowers.
A cactus native to central Mexico, it forms dense clusters of elongated stems covered in very sharp yellow or brown spines. White or yellow flowers appear from late winter to early summer.

A cactus from the Mexican states of San Luis Potosí, Querétaro, Guanajuato, Puebla and Oaxaca, it grows in oak forests and grasslands. Its rounded body bears curved yellow-to-red spines, and striking pink flowers appear from early spring to summer.
Cactus native to northern and southern Mexico. It bears bell-shaped purplish-pink to red flowers in winter and early spring, and its curved spines were traditionally used as fishing hooks.

A flowering cactus native to central Mexico, usually forming clumps but sometimes growing alone. It has long white spines, white wool and blue-green tissue, with crowns of carmine-pink flowers followed by small, tart, technically edible fruits.
stories.edibilityNote: The small fruits are described as technically edible, with a tart, fruity flavour; only animal consumption is specifically reported.

stories.summary: A cactus occurring in the Mexican states of Nuevo León, Coahuila and Tamaulipas. It usually grows alone, with flattened spherical blue-green or pale-green stems, strong central spines but no outer spines, and yellowish-white flowers followed by red fruits.

A cactus found in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico, it has a conspicuous shrub-like or tree-like form with sharply barbed spines. Its yellowish, lumpy fruits are retained throughout winter and are often mistaken for flowers.
stories.edibilityNote: The dry, bland fruits are said to have been eaten by Indigenous people in Arizona and New Mexico.

stories.summary: An epiphytic cactus native to southern Mexico, where it inhabits cloud forests in the Sierra Madre de Oaxaca and Chiapas Highlands. Its flattened, leaf-like stems arch downward, and it bears large scarlet, funnel-shaped flowers with greenish throats.

A succulent cactus native to the Mexican states of Hidalgo, Guanajuato and Querétaro, it forms clusters of bluish-green stems with white spines and yellow flowers. Its gracilis subspecies produces abundant offsets that detach easily, while the two recognized subspecies differ noticeably in their spines and flowers.
A flowering agave native to central, northeastern and southwestern Mexico.

A giant succulent native to the Mexican states of Oaxaca, Puebla and Veracruz, it forms a massive rosette of exceptionally large leaves. After many years, each rosette produces one towering branched flower stalk whose flowers open red and turn yellow, then fruits and dies.
stories.edibilityNote: It is used for pulque and is also collected from the wild to make mezcal.

stories.summary: A perennial succulent shrub native to tropical and subtropical North and Central America, Devil’s Backbone has smooth leaves and bright red, slipper-shaped bracts. It generally flowers in mid-spring, and its flowers have no scent.
stories.edibilityNote: Roots, stems and leaves are toxic; swallowing root juice or even a few seeds can cause severe vomiting and diarrhea.

stories.summary: Fast-growing leafy perennial shrub native to Mexico and believed to have originated from the Yucatán Peninsula through Central America to Panama. Damaged plants release irritating, often toxic latex, and some varieties have stinging hairs. Young leaves and tender stem tips are eaten cooked, but raw leaves contain toxic cyanogenic compounds, so thorough cooking is essential.
stories.edibilityNote: Young leaves and tender stem tips are eaten boiled, steamed or stir-fried; raw leaves are toxic, and thorough cooking is essential.

stories.summary: A perennial stonecrop from northeastern Mexico, it has many branching stems and rosettes of thick, grey-green, spoon-shaped leaves. This highly variable plant bears upright, loosely clustered orange-yellow flowers and is widely grown ornamentally.

A succulent native to Tamaulipas, Mexico. Its powdery leaf coating gives it a ghostlike appearance, while its thick leaves detach easily from the rosette and its spring flowers are white with red spots. It is used as an edible vegetable.
stories.edibilityNote: Plants of this species are used as edible vegetables.

stories.summary: A flowering succulent native to Tamaulipas, Mexico, it forms a rosette of pinkish-white leaves and bears red flowers. The ‘Topsy Turvy’ cultivar originated in California and has leaves positioned upside-down.

A pine tree native to the highlands of Mexico, it has long grass-green needles that droop with a weeping effect. Its pale pink to salmon timber is moderately soft and brittle, with a strong aniseed smell when freshly cut.

A rainforest vine found from southern Mexico south to Panama, though the supplied information does not explicitly identify its native range. It climbs by roots and bears very large, triangular leaves that are often cut almost to the central rib.

A plant native from southern Mexico to Ecuador. It is cold-hardy in cultivation, but is unlikely to flower after freezing back to the ground. Traditional uses include treating asthma, diabetes, fever, headaches and several other ailments.

A perennial insect-eating herb native to El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, it changes from sticky, prey-catching summer leaves to small non-carnivorous winter leaves. Pink, purple or violet flowers appear twice a year.
Tree native to Central America, commonly known as the tree fuchsia.
Small shrub of unknown origin, distributed in Asia and Mexico. Its terminal flower clusters are yellow with red at the base, and it grows beside streams in mountain, oak and pine forests.

A submerged, free-floating aquatic plant of unspecified native origin, it has been reported across parts of Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Florida and the Dominican Republic. Its leaves divide three or four times into threadlike tips, distinguishing it from rigid hornwort.

An agave found in central Mexico, forming a single open rosette of thick, light-green to yellow-green leaves with strong dark-brown tip spines. Its tall, narrow flower cluster bears blossoms that are reddish-purple at first and yellow when open.

A succulent of unstated native origin, it is recorded in the Mexican states of Hidalgo, Puebla and Veracruz. This stemless plant forms a cluster of leathery grey-green to green leaves, with a tall flower stalk bearing a red stem and red bracts.

A cactus native to the Baja California peninsula, it forms a richly branched shrub or small tree with blue-green branches. Its pale greenish-white flowers open by day and night, and its spherical red fruits are edible.
stories.edibilityNote: The spherical red fruits are edible.
