stories.summary: A large shrubby cactus native to central and northern Mexico, developing candelabra-like branches when mature. Its creamy-white flowers last less than a day. Its dark-purple berries are edible and sold for consumption in Mexico.
stories.edibilityNote: The dark-purple berries are edible and sold for consumption in Mexico.

stories.summary: Solitary or branching cactus native only to Mexico, specifically limestone hills and dry forest in Hidalgo, Guanajuato, Querétaro and San Luis Potosí. It has blue-green, frosted, ribbed stems with yellow spines. Its bell-shaped yellow flowers are followed by pale, fleshy fruits tinged red.
A fern indigenous to the Neotropical Caribbean and Amazon rainforest, and to the Azores. It is known as the mossy finger fern.
A cactus native to Oaxaca, Mexico, it has slender stems with about seven ribs and numerous needle-like spines. Flowers grow at the stem tips, followed by round, somewhat flattened fruits.
A cactus of unstated native origin, listed in CITES Appendix II. Its flowers are visited by broad-billed hummingbirds.
A prickly pear native to the tropical and subtropical Americas. It usually has more than three spines at each spine-bearing spot, distinguishing it from Opuntia stricta.

A shrubby cactus native to Coahuila, Mexico, it forms broad clumps of round to wedge-shaped green or blue-green stem segments. It bears up to six yellow or reddish needle-like spines and large yellow flowers flushed with red.

A low, mat-forming shrub cactus found in Baja California Sur, Mexico, at elevations up to 50 metres, Opuntia pycnantha has densely spined, round to short-oblong stem sections. Its yellow flowers are flushed red, and its fruits are heavily spined.

A flowering cactus native to the Chihuahuan Desert of North America and parts of South America. In Queensland, Australia, it is an invasive agricultural weed whose long spines can painfully injure people and animals and damage vehicle tyres.

A prickly pear cactus occurring in Guatemala and southern Mexico, including the Yucatán dry forest. Its widely spreading branches bear slender flattened pads with several spines at each spine-bearing point, followed by yellow-to-rose flowers and red mature fruits.

A broadleaf red shrub native to Mexico and South America. It has purplish stems, small white flowers with creamy bracts and colourful foliage; broken stems release irritating, poisonous sap that can severely damage internal organs if swallowed.
stories.edibilityNote: The sap is poisonous and can severely damage internal organs if ingested.

stories.summary: Perennial herb native to the tropical Americas. Its arching stems hold conspicuous dense balls of flowers and fruit capsules away from the stem. Its milky sap can irritate skin and eyes.
A lycophyte native to Mexico and Central America, Selaginella martensii is commonly known as variegated spikemoss or Martens's spike moss.

A rhizomatous fern native to a broad area from northern Mexico to eastern Brazil, it has fan-shaped pale- or dark-green fronds with spore structures along their divisions. It favours humid tropical settings and low light in cultivation but does not tolerate cool temperatures.
A flowering succulent native to central Mexico, specifically Puebla and Veracruz. It forms clustered rosettes of pointed green leaves with red margins and bears yellow flowers.

A succulent native to Mexico, it grows naturally on rocky ground and cliff faces. Its evergreen leaves are bright orange-copper and may develop red or orange edges in strong sun, while white star-shaped flowers bloom in spring.
stories.edibilityNote: It is not listed as toxic by the ASPCA, but no human food use is documented.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago.

A trailing succulent perennial native to southern Mexico, burro’s-tail is known in the wild from two ravines in central Veracruz and nearby vertical volcanic cliffs. It has fleshy blue-green leaves and summer flowers ranging from pink to red; its fragile leaves detach easily but can readily form roots and new plants.
A perennial succulent native to Mexico, it grows on rocks at higher elevations. It has thick, flattened purplish or bluish-green leaves and dark red flowers in summer.

Succulent species reported as native to Nuevo León in northern Mexico. It forms symmetrical rosettes of fleshy, silvery-grey leaves and produces pale pink or coral flowers from late winter to early spring.

A flowering perennial native to Chiapas, Mexico, it naturally grows on other plants in wet forests and cloudy highland settings. Its deep forest-green, velvety, heart-shaped leaves have striking ivory to light-green veins, and it produces orange berries.
stories.edibilityNote: Poisonous to humans when ingested; calcium oxalate crystals in the leaves can cause mouth and throat pain, nausea, swallowing difficulty and other symptoms.

stories.summary: A tropical palm native to Madagascar, it forms multiple cane-like stems and upward-curving leaves that create a butterfly-like outline. Its fruit ripens from yellow or gold to dark purple or black, and it is widely grown as an ornamental or houseplant.

A desert plant native to the Chihuahuan Desert and other dry habitats of northern and central Mexico, it forms a symmetrical rosette of firm, narrow leaves. In midsummer it produces a towering spike of small white flowers.

A trunk-forming plant found in Mexico's Zacatecas and Coahuila, growing on open ground, gypsum dunes and rocky slopes. Its dense, waxy blue leaves have upward-pointing marginal spines, while tall, narrow flower stalks carry green to cream flowers.

An evergreen epiphytic perennial native to rainforest habitats from southern Mexico and Central America into northern and central South America. Its foliage forms a star-shaped rosette topped by orange and red bracts; cultivated varieties may flower in maroon, red, orange, yellow or pink.

Perennial herb originally native only to South America. Its creeping rhizome produces dense rows of stems and turf-like growth; unusually for a rush, it often occupies very dry Andean roadsides and abandoned fields.

A bulbous perennial endemic to South Africa’s Cape Province, it bears long-lasting white or cream flowers whose brown or green centres fade with age. The flowers turn toward the sun, while the fleshy leaves die after flowering.

An evergreen tropical shrub or small tree native throughout Mexico and Central America. It has glossy, willow-like leaves, funnel-shaped yellow flowers and deep red-black fruit; all parts are toxic to most vertebrates, and many human poisonings are known.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are toxic, and human poisonings include intentional swallowing of the seeds.

stories.summary: A slow-growing flowering epiphyte native to southern Mexico, El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras. Its broad greenish-silver leaves form a sculptural rosette, and its red-purple tubular flowers have petals that last for months.

An evergreen perennial herb endemic to dry areas of Nuevo León in northeastern Mexico, woolly spiderwort has fleshy leaves arranged in a precise geometric pattern. Greyish-white hairs cover almost the entire plant, contrasting with its bright purplish-pink or purple three-petalled flowers.

An evergreen perennial subshrub native to the tropical Americas, from Mexico through Central America and the Caribbean to Bolivia and southern Brazil. Its fruit capsule is enclosed by a fleshy purple-black covering, giving it a berry-like appearance; a variegated form called ‘Mexican Flag’ is grown ornamentally.
A herb native to tropical America. Its arrow-shaped leaves have a bluish tone; both the leaves and rhizome can be eaten after cooking.
stories.edibilityNote: The leaves and rhizome are eaten cooked.

stories.summary: A herbaceous ornamental plant whose native origin is not stated in the supplied information. Its summer display has a mauve to rose-purple sheath with pale margins around a yellow spike. The green, unmarked leaves are semi-erect and not arrow-shaped like those of other species.

A perennial flowering plant native to Mexico, Colombia and Central America. It has large, bright pink, funnel-shaped flowers and green strap-like leaves, and commonly blooms soon after heavy rain. It contains toxic alkaloids; ingestion can cause vomiting, convulsions and death.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant contains toxic alkaloids; ingestion can cause vomiting, convulsions and death.

stories.summary: A bromeliad native to the West Indies and Latin America, ranging from parts of Mexico south to Brazil.
A bushy shrub native from New Guinea to Queensland, Australia. It has alternate, long-stalked leaves and white flowers with five petals, and is often grown as an ornamental.
A flowering plant native to Oaxaca and Chiapas in Mexico, eyelash begonia is a popular houseplant available in several cultivars.
Flowering begonia native to Mexico and Central America. Its rhizome grows upward rather than along the ground, and pink or white flowers appear in winter.
Flowering plant native to southeastern Mexico, where it grows in extremely dense shade in tropical forests.

An evergreen shrub or small tree native to mainland China. Its spiny compound leaves are joined by fragrant yellow flowers in late winter and early spring, followed by grape-like clusters of blue-black, wax-coated berries.
stories.edibilityNote: Berries are used in preserves, drinks and sweets, usually cooked or sweetened; flowers and simmered young leaves are also eaten.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to southern Mexico and Central America, Centradenia inaequilateralis has pink-purple flowers. Its cultivar ‘Cascade’ has received the Royal Horticultural Society’s Award of Garden Merit.

A small tree native to Brazil, strawberry guava has oval leaves and thin-skinned fruit ranging from yellow to dark red or purple. Its juicy fruit and skin are edible, fresh or made into jam and juice, although removing the skin gives a sweeter flavour. It is highly invasive in many tropical regions.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit's skin and juicy interior are edible; it is eaten fresh or made into jam and juice, sometimes after removing the skin.

stories.summary: A shrub or woody-based plant native to tropical America, it grows wild beside roads and in disturbed vegetation across several forest types. It is heavily branched, with broad leaves and upright pale-green or yellowish flower spikes; its fruits turn black when dry.
An evergreen shrub from New Guinea and the Solomon Islands. It has flattened, jointed green stems and arrow-shaped leaves, with both spreading and climbing growth.
Plant species in the genus Hintonia. It contains coutareagenin, described as an antidiabetic active substance.

Evergreen perennial endemic to Guizhou and Yunnan in southern China and to Vietnam. Its dark-green oval leaves have slightly textured or serrated edges and four raised silvery patches, while underground rhizomes help it spread.

An evergreen climber native to tropical West Africa, with opposite pairs of oval to oblong leaves. Its striking flower clusters combine red petals with white to pale-purple outer cups, making it a popular ornamental in frost-free conditions.

Tree native to the Magellanic and Valdivian temperate forests of Chile and Argentina. It has glossy green leaves with whitish undersides, creamy white fragrant flowers and bluish berries. Indigenous people historically ate its astringent bark, which is also used as a pepper substitute in Argentina and Chile.
stories.edibilityNote: Indigenous people historically ate the astringent bark; it is also used as a pepper substitute in Argentina and Chile.

stories.summary: Perennial herb native to South America. Its slightly wavy, variegated leaves may be green, red, yellow or mixtures of these colours, making it popular as an ornamental edging plant. Its edible leaves are also harvested from the wild.
stories.edibilityNote: The edible leaves are harvested from the wild.

stories.summary: Neotropical mistletoe native to Colombia, Mexico, the Mexican Gulf and Venezuela. It has hairless branches, opposite leaves and terminal groups of three yellow-to-scarlet flowers, each above a cup-shaped bract.

A deciduous tree native to tropical and subtropical South America, it may grow as a tree or shrub depending on water availability. It has dense, zigzagging branches with strong spines. Its sweet but scarcely fleshy fruits are edible, although there is no market or habit of human consumption.
stories.edibilityNote: The sweet, scarcely fleshy fruits are edible, but there is no market or habit of human consumption.

stories.summary: A highly branched shrub or subshrub native and endemic to Mexico, it grows mainly in high-mountain grasslands and open pine forest. Its densely woolly foliage is aromatic when crushed, and it bears bright yellow flower heads.
Aromatic shrub endemic to Mexico. It bears rounded, lobed leaves and yellow flower clusters, blooming in the dry season, roughly November to March.
A sedge native to southern parts of North America, most of Central America and northern parts of South America.

A perennial chilli shrub originating in ancient Peru and across the Andean region of South America, it has white or cream flowers and usually downward-hanging pods with citrus or fruity flavours. Heat varies widely among cultivars. Ají amarillo is used fresh in Peru and dried and ground in Bolivia.
stories.edibilityNote: Ají amarillo is used as a condiment, mostly fresh in Peru and dried and ground in Bolivia.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub or small tree native to the South American Andes of Argentina, Bolivia and Peru, tamarillo grows quickly but is relatively short-lived. Its edible fruit is eaten fresh or made into juice, preserves, fruit salad and sauces, although unripe fruit is slightly toxic.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten fresh or prepared as juice, preserves, fruit salad and sauces; unripe fruit is slightly toxic.

stories.summary: A shrub whose native origin is not stated, giant devil's-fig is found from Mexico to South America, including disturbed sites. It is recognized by its woolly, often rust-coloured covering and bears large velvety leaves, white flowers and green berries.

A flowering agave native to southern Mexico and Guatemala. This sterile hybrid is propagated vegetatively, usually from suckers, and bears narrow, toothed leaves ending in a strong spine. Its leaf fibre is used for rope, twine and other products.
stories.edibilityNote: It is reported as an ingredient in traditional Mexican henequen liquor and mezcal.

stories.summary: Succulent flowering plant native to Oaxaca and the area near Tehuacán in Puebla, Mexico. It forms a grey-green leaf rosette tipped with sharp black spines and bears small grey-and-red flowers on tall, sturdy stems.

Succulent plant native to Hidalgo, Tamaulipas, Guanajuato and Queretaro in Mexico. It forms a basal rosette of sword-shaped leaves with spiny, undulating margins, and produces tall stalks bearing greenish flowers.
An upright shrub native to Central America, firespike has glossy opposite leaves and terminal spikes of waxy red to burgundy flowers. It blooms in summer and autumn and is sensitive to frost.

A perennial herb or undershrub native to southeastern Africa, with narrow, lance-shaped leaves. Widely grown as an ornamental, it also feeds monarch butterfly caterpillars, which retain the plant's toxic compounds as a defence against predators.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts can be toxic if swallowed, affecting the heart, breathing, nervous system and stomach; sap can also injure the eyes.

stories.summary: A semi-deciduous flowering tree native to Central and South America, it forms a broad, symmetrical umbrella-shaped crown. Its leaves fold in rainy weather and at night, while its pods contain sticky edible pulp that can be made into a lemon-flavoured drink.
stories.edibilityNote: The pod pulp is edible and made into a lemon-flavoured beverage; in Cambodia, fruit and, during famines, young leaves are eaten.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub growing naturally in Vanuatu and occurring across the Pacific Islands. Its broad, sometimes crinkled leaves are coppery green with red splashes, and fine hairs cover both leaves and branches. Male flowers hang in long spikes, while the shorter female spikes are often hidden among the foliage.

A tuberous flowering plant native to Brazil, Sinningia speciosa produces large, velvety, brightly coloured flowers and is a popular houseplant. It often becomes dormant, when its tuber is kept cool and dry until growth resumes.

A scrambling perennial plant native from Mexico and the Caribbean through Central and South America to Argentina and Bolivia. It may creep over the ground or climb trees as a woody vine, bearing yellow flower heads and narrow fruits tipped with two backward-barbed points.

Perennial deciduous legume shrub or small tree native to southern North America, the Caribbean and most of South America. It has dense foliage, clusters of small white flowers and seed pods that turn from green to brown. Unlike most plants formerly placed in Acacia, it is thornless.
stories.edibilityNote: The bark is used to produce alcoholic beverages, and the root is used in Mexican pulque.

stories.summary: A tree-shaped cactus of unstated native origin, found in parts of Mexico, coastal Venezuela, Colombia and the Dutch Caribbean. Its white flowers open at night and last until midday; its variably coloured, thorn-covered fruits shed their thorns when ripe and contain red flesh.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten by humans and described as good tasting.

stories.summary: A cactus species, Opuntia pilifera is listed in CITES Appendix II.
An herb whose native origin is not stated in the supplied information.
A fern native to South America.

A Mexican succulent native to the Durango–Sinaloa border and Chihuahua in the Sierra Madre Occidental, Echeveria affinis also occasionally occurs in San Luis Potosí. It grows at high elevations in rocky, very dry places and is adapted to poor, mineral-rich soils.

A succulent flowering plant native to the rocky canyons and arid hillsides of central Mexico. It forms a small, usually solitary rosette of thick, pointed green leaves; some varieties develop red or bronze tips, while summer flowers may be pink, orange or red.

A succulent native to Mexico and endemic to its Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt. It is fleshy and hairy throughout, with rosettes of green or brown leaves and intense red tubular flowers in autumn and winter.

Flowering plant found in the Mexican states of Puebla and Oaxaca. It forms large rosettes of broad green leaves edged in purple-red, followed by a tall branching display of pink flowers from September to October.

A succulent flowering plant native to Mexico, where it is widespread and fairly common in northern Oaxaca and southern Puebla. Its purplish striped leaves, knobby stems and seasonal flowers make it distinctive.
A flowering succulent native to southwestern and central Mexico.
A succulent flowering plant native to Mexico, it has also been introduced to the Dominican Republic, New Zealand and Vietnam.
Ornamental plant of undocumented native origin.

A large, thorny climber native to South Africa and Mozambique. Its downward-pointing thorns help anchor climbing shoots, while fragrant white flowers are followed by bright red berries that attract birds.
A flowering bromeliad native to Central America and western Mexico, extending north to Sinaloa.

An ornamental plant from Latin America. Its large heart- or lance-shaped leaves have striking green, white, pink and red blotches. All parts are poisonous if eaten, causing mouth burning and swelling, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous; ingestion can cause mouth burning and swelling, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea.

stories.summary: A small palm native to rainforests in southern Mexico and Guatemala, the parlour palm has a slender green trunk and flexible, spineless stems. It can begin flowering while still unusually small, producing clusters of tiny yellow to orange-red scented flowers.

A climbing plant found from Mexico to Central America. Its young, waxy leaves overlap like shingles as it grows along the ground; on reaching a tree trunk, it climbs using anchoring roots and develops larger adult leaves.

A palm-like, rhizomatous plant endemic to Mexico, it forms tree-like rosettes whose numerous mature leaves remain attached to the stem. Its upright flower clusters appear whitish-yellow from a distance and bear small, separate male or female flowers.

An aquatic perennial reported as native from Mexico through Central America and separately in eastern and southern Brazil. It grows along rivers, lagoons, ponds and swamps, bearing dense groups of lilac or rarely white flowers.

An aquatic perennial native to Eurasia and North Africa, growing in relatively deep, still or slow-flowing calcareous fresh water. Its large, translucent, shiny leaves have distinctive net-like veins, and it has no floating leaves.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Potamogeton lucens
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A fan palm native to southern China and northern Vietnam. It grows in multi-stemmed clumps with glossy, deeply divided evergreen leaves and bamboo-like trunks exposed as old fibrous sheaths fall away.

A large palm native to the Lesser Antilles, Colombia, Venezuela, and Trinidad and Tobago, it has a pale trunk topped by a green crownshaft. Its angled leaflets give the fronds a bottlebrush appearance, and its ripe fruit is purplish-black. The terminal bud is edible, while immature flower clusters have historically been pickled as a vegetable and young-flower sap fermented into alcohol.
stories.edibilityNote: The terminal bud is edible; immature flower clusters were historically pickled, and sap from young flower clusters can be fermented into alcohol.

stories.summary: A tree native from Mexico to Nicaragua, and perhaps Costa Rica, Bocconia arborea grows in temperate areas associated with seasonal and irrigated crops. It has deeply cut leaves with brownish or grey felted undersides and small, dark, glossy seeds.

A grass-like iris-family wildflower native to Mexico, Central America and South America. Its flowers are often white with blue or purple centres but may also be yellow, pink or violet, followed by rounded brown seed capsules.
An orchid whose native status is not stated, found from north-central and southern Mexico through Central America.

A herbaceous perennial native to parts of Mexico, the Caribbean and northern South America. Its glossy, deeply veined leaves arch from the base, while its cream flower spike and white surrounding bract turn green with age.

A flowering plant that grows on other plants, native to Central America and Mexico. Thick, twisting leaves covered with fine gray hairs rise from a swollen base, and the plant bears red flower clusters with bright violet flowers.
A flowering plant endemic to Mexico.
A flowering plant native to southern Mexico, Central America, Colombia and Venezuela. It has long, lance-shaped leaves and yellow flowers marked with brown spots.

Robust herbaceous plant native to central Mexico and Central America. It can reach four metres, with huge waxy green leaves and flower structures combining a white to yellowish-green sheath with a pale yellow to ochre central spike.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant is described generally as a food source; no part or preparation is specified.

stories.summary: An orchid of unstated native origin, widespread from Mexico south to Costa Rica.
A tree of unspecified native origin, this species is reported from Mexico through Central America to Colombia, Venezuela, the Guianas, the Amazon, Peru and Brazil.

A begonia native to southeastern Brazil, where it grows beneath the Atlantic rainforest canopy. Its olive-green oblong leaves have silver spots and red-purple undersides, while its clustered flowers are white or pink with yellow centers.

An annual plant native to the Mediterranean and Asia, rocket has deeply lobed leaves and creamy-white flowers marked with purple veins. Its sharp-tasting leaves are widely eaten in salads, while its flowers, young seed pods and mature seeds are also edible.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves, flowers, young pods and mature seeds are edible; leaves are eaten raw or cooked, and aged seed oil is used for salads and cooking.

stories.summary: A vigorously climbing woody vine native to tropical Asia. Its fragrant tubular flowers open white at dusk, turn pink on the second day and red on the third, while changing from horizontal to drooping.
Climbing herbaceous plant native to Mexico, El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras.

A perennial herb or shrub native to Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Guatemala, El Salvador and Chiapas in Mexico. It has yellow-green leaves, sometimes with purple veins, and showy flowers ranging from bright red to pinkish cream, surrounded by contrasting colourful bracts and calyces.
Evergreen shrub native to Mexico, with cup-shaped scarlet flowers produced mainly in summer. It is cultivated as an ornamental plant and needs a warm, sheltered position in temperate areas.

A trailing plant native to South American tropical rainforest, it has hanging shoots and tiny, thick, fleshy, button-like leaves that may weave around one another. It can grow on trees, rocks, rotten logs or the forest floor, favouring moist, shaded conditions.

Plane tree endemic to northeastern Mexico, mainly parts of Nuevo León, San Luis Potosí and Tamaulipas. Its olive-green leaves turn yellow-green in winter, while white flowers bloom from December through February.

Perennial flowering climber native to Mexico, with isolated sightings elsewhere in tropical Central and South America. Its hooked tendrils cling to supports, while its large, scented, bell-shaped flowers open white and turn violet as they mature.

A flowering shrub or small tree native to the Americas from Mexico through Central America into South America, as well as the Caribbean. It is covered in spines and stinging hairs, with pink or purple flower clusters and spongy green or pinkish fruit.

A perennial herb native to southern Mexico, parts of the Caribbean, Central America, Colombia and Venezuela. It was historically used as a natural sweetener in Mexico and parts of Central America, although bitter compounds, especially camphor, have limited wider use.
stories.edibilityNote: Historically used as a natural sweetener in Mexico and parts of Central America.

stories.summary: A scrambling shrub native to southern and central Africa, Cape honeysuckle is normally evergreen but may lose its leaves in colder climates. Its narrow tubular flowers range from orange and orange-red to apricot, appearing at varying times but usually from autumn to spring.
A succulent plant, Short-leaved Stonecrop spreads slowly.

An epiphyte or tree found from Mexico to Costa Rica and in the Antilles. It has cream-coloured latex and petals, while its rounded fruit remains green when mature. It grows in evergreen or secondary forests and along roadsides in the Atlantic zone.
Erect perennial shrub native to the Canary Islands. Its pale green leaves and stems have long white hairs, while its flowers range from pale purple to deep magenta.

A herbaceous perennial native to Puebla, Tamaulipas and Veracruz in Mexico, roseleaf sage grows in shady places such as forest edges. Its beetroot-red flowers are enclosed by large, colourful paired bracts, which fall away as the flowers expand.

A small to medium-sized tree native to rainforests of southeast Queensland and the extreme north of adjacent New South Wales, Australia. It has glossy leaves with wavy edges, white or pink flowers and rounded woody fruits that are edible.
stories.edibilityNote: Its rounded woody fruits are edible.

stories.summary: Evergreen shrub from Mexico, Mexican orange has three-part aromatic leaves that smell like basil when crushed, and scented white flowers in spring, sometimes followed by limited autumn flowering.
Shrub or small tree native to South and Southeast Asia, China and Australasia. It has fragrant white or cream flowers and orange-red berries containing hairy seeds.
Tree native to Bolivia, Peru, Mexico and the United States (Florida).

A shrub native to Central America, it occurs from Mexico to Costa Rica and sometimes grows on other plants. Its hanging flowers have pink-to-red tubes and green petals, while the elongated green berries develop purple speckles when ripe.

A bunchgrass widely distributed across Eurasia, Africa and the Americas, though its native geographic origin is not specified. It forms tight tufts of wiry leaves and delicate silvery or purplish flower heads on wavy, hair-like stalks.

An annual grass distributed around the Mediterranean and Middle East, with no native range explicitly stated. It has been widely introduced to drier regions worldwide. Compared with sea fern-grass, it has a more open flower cluster and a ridged flowering stalk.

A small tree or shrub native to Mexico, Montanoa bipinnatifida often grows in groups and sometimes flowers so young that it does not yet look woody. It has very large, opposite leaves deeply divided into toothed lobes, and broad, branching clusters of flower heads with white outer flowers and yellow centres.
A Mexican subshrub found in Jalisco, Zacatecas, Aguascalientes, Hidalgo, Guanajuato and San Luis Potosí. Its flower heads contain only disc flowers, with no ray flowers.

A herbaceous perennial native from Mexico through Central America to Colombia and Ecuador, tree dahlia has hollow, cane-like, four-sided stems and large leaves. Its nodding flowerheads are typically lavender or mauvish-pink.
stories.edibilityNote: Petals can be eaten in salads or soups; Q'eqchi' people in San Pedro Carchá, Guatemala, use the leaves as a dietary supplement.

stories.summary: Evergreen flowering shrub native to Mesoamerica and widespread from Tamaulipas in Mexico to Costa Rica. In autumn it bears fragrant, flat clusters of white-to-pink, daisy-like flowers that attract butterflies, above light-green toothed leaves.

An evergreen upright shrub endemic to Mexico's cloud forests. Its reddish-purple branches carry large, slightly rough dark-green leaves, while scented mauve, lilac or magenta-blue flower clusters appear in spring with a bursting-fireworks appearance.

An annual herb described as a North American species and widespread from Mexico through parts of Central and South America. Its finely divided leaves accompany many small, bright yellow flower heads. Its lemon-flavoured flowers are reported as edible garnishes, although the source flags this claim as needing a citation.
stories.edibilityNote: The lemon-flavoured flowers are reported edible and used as garnish, but the source marks the claim as needing a citation.

stories.summary: A semi-epiphytic shrub or vine of unspecified native origin, occurring from southern Mexico to Colombia and Ecuador. It has leathery leaves, striking orange tubular flowers and soft orange-yellow berries enclosed by the persistent flower cup.

An evergreen shrub presumed native to temperate Andean regions of Colombia, Peru and Chile, pepino is not known in the wild. It bears sweet edible fruit with melon-like colour and a flavour resembling honeydew and cucumber, often eaten fresh as a snack.
stories.edibilityNote: The sweet, mild-flavoured fruit is often eaten fresh as a snack.

stories.summary: Domesticated shrubby pepper native to Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador and known only in cultivation. Its hairy leaves and black seeds distinguish it from other peppers, while its variously coloured fruits range from mild to extremely hot.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruits are eaten fresh, dried, ground or as paste; seeds and white membranes are often removed, and boiling can reduce their heat.

stories.summary: Shrub native to Mexico, rosy cestrum has pink flowers.
A robust flowering vine native to Mexico, Central America and northwestern South America. Its long-lasting dark purple flowers eventually fade to white.
A tall, heavily branched yucca native to central Mexico, it bears straight leaves in rosette-shaped bunches at the end of each stem. Its hanging flower clusters contain many white flowers.

A succulent flowering plant native to central Mexico from Querétaro to Mexico State, thread agave forms a stemless rosette of dark to bronze-green leaves marked with ornamental white bud imprints. Its tall flower stalk bears densely packed yellowish-green to dark purple flowers in autumn and winter.

Small agave native to the Guadalajara region of Jalisco and the Ceboruco volcano area of Nayarit, Mexico. Its grey-green leaves bear distinctive overlap marks, large edge spines and a thick brown tip spine.

A trunk-forming agave of arid Puebla, Oaxaca and Veracruz in Mexico. It produces offshoots and has stiff green leaves with toothed edges and a dark-brown tip. Its tall, open flower cluster bears green to yellow flowers, typically from July to August.

A tree-like plant native to Texas and Mexico’s Chihuahua and Coahuila regions, it grows in desert, steppe and semiarid areas. Its trunk supports a crown of thin, stiff, sharp-pointed leaves and a large cluster of white flowers.

A perennial plant believed to be native to central and southern Mexico, though it is no longer found wild. It grows from underground tubers or tuberous roots and produces strongly fragrant, waxy white flowers.
stories.edibilityNote: The flowers are used in cooking in Indonesia.

stories.summary: A thornless evergreen shrub or small tree native to Australia. Its branches and narrow leaves hang down, while its shiny black seeds carry a crimson appendage.
stories.edibilityNote: The seeds are edible.

stories.summary: A bushy evergreen perennial native from Southeast Asia to Australia. Cultivated forms are prized for exceptionally varied leaves combining colors such as green, cream, pink, red and dark purple, with patterns and shapes that differ widely.

Rhizomatous perennial native to South Africa, the large fortnight lily has long, rigid, sword-like green leaves. Its white flowers carry yellow and violet markings, bloom abundantly during summer, especially after rain, and last only a couple of days.
An evergreen tree native to Borneo, Java and Peninsular Malaysia. It has long, spirally arranged leaves and gray to reddish bark marked with small horizontal flecks.

A bulbous herbaceous perennial native to Mexico, four-leaved wood-sorrel has four-part leaves and is widely grown as an ornamental. Its flowers and leaves are edible with a sharp lemon flavour, but eating too much can be harmful because its oxalic acid can interfere with nutrient absorption, especially calcium.
stories.edibilityNote: Flowers and leaves are edible and lemon-flavoured, but excessive consumption can be harmful because oxalic acid may interfere with nutrient absorption, especially calcium.

stories.summary: A wild banana species native to eastern South Asia, the eastern Indian subcontinent, northern Southeast Asia and southern China. Its lush leaves form upright clumps, and it has red to maroon flowers and blue-green fruit containing seeds.
stories.edibilityNote: Natural clones, including wild saba bananas, produce edible fruit; seeded fruit is considered inedible, while historical cooking and eating of wild bananas is only assumed.

stories.summary: A terrestrial orchid native to Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Peru and Bolivia.

A unicellular green microalga found worldwide in freshwater and terrestrial habitats, it has spherical cells with a pea-green, cup-shaped chloroplast. Since the 1990s it has been considered a protein-rich food source and is now sold internationally as a dietary supplement or food additive.
stories.edibilityNote: Since the 1990s, it has been used internationally as a dietary supplement or protein-rich food additive, including powders, tablets, capsules and extracts.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, bastard balm is not protected under Portuguese or European Union law.
Plant native to the Mediterranean Basin, including Crete, blue hound's-tongue is invasive in parts of Texas and Missouri.
Woody-stemmed trailing perennial native to Italy and North Africa. Its light blue to violet flowers often have paler centres, and its stems do not twine.

A fast-growing tree native to the Indian subcontinent and parts of mainland Southeast Asia, neem is evergreen but sheds many leaves during dry winters. It has fragrant white flowers and smooth, olive-like fruits containing bitter-sweet, fibrous pulp.
stories.edibilityNote: Tender shoots and flowers are eaten as vegetables in India; young leaves and flower buds are cooked or pickled in Southeast Asia. Neem oil is toxic to small children.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to western Peru, small-flowered tobacco has also been introduced to the Canary Islands. It is a parent of Nicotiana rustica, the economically important Aztec tobacco.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A deciduous tree native to Southern Europe and Southwestern Asia, manna ash retains smooth, dark-grey bark even when old. Dense clusters of slender, creamy-white flowers appear after the new leaves in late spring.

Small shrub-like succulent native to the Western Cape of South Africa. Its overlapping leaves grow in four rows, while vivid red flowers crowd into flat-topped clusters from December to March in its native habitat.
A flowering plant native to central and southern Europe.
Flowering legume native to mainland Portugal.

A European perennial herb of wet places, with creeping stems that root at their joints. Its flowers are usually blue, occasionally white, and it grows beside water or in wet grassland, bogs and marshes.
A bulb-forming perennial of Europe and the Mediterranean, Meadow Gagea has generally yellow flowers, sometimes striped green on the back.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Gagea pratensis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A self-supporting shrub that can grow to about 42 centimetres.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
Evergreen or semi-evergreen fern native to southern and western Europe. Its bright green, soft-textured fronds usually droop downslope, while cinnamon-brown scales coat the stalks and most midribs.

A low-growing plant of dry limestone rocks, occurring in parts of Europe, North Africa and the eastern Mediterranean. Its small leaves are green above but densely hairy and grey below, and its yellow flowers have five petals.

Evergreen shrub native near the southern coast of South Africa’s Western Cape. Its yellow, orange, or crimson flower heads resemble pincushions because their long styles project outward and curve upward; it flowers mainly from mid-July through November.

An evergreen succulent shrub native to Madagascar. Its olive-green, angular leaves become woolly near their tips and have darker tooth tips; it can reproduce through seeds and plantlets. It is naturally toxic to humans and may irritate exposed skin.
stories.edibilityNote: Naturally toxic to humans; exposed skin may become irritated and itchy.

stories.summary: A branching cactus probably native to the Peruvian Andes. Its stems bear spiral rows of bumps, long greyish-white spines and distinctive awl-shaped rudimentary leaves. It has become invasive in parts of the Mediterranean region and Australia.

A stem succulent native to Madagascar. Its silvery trunk bears large thorns and does most of the photosynthesis, while narrow leaves cluster at the top; outdoor plants develop large, fragrant white flowers but indoor plants rarely bloom.

A heath native to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini. Its form, hairiness and flowers vary markedly across its range, including a white-flowered form in Eswatini and Mpumalanga; it can resprout from its woody base after fire.
A flowering cactus native to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, cane cactus is widely grown as an ornamental. It has become invasive in Europe, South Africa and Australia.
A small tree native to South Africa, with opposite branches and oval, pointed leaves that are hairy underneath. Its flowers are deep red.

A semi-evergreen shrub native to South Africa. Its narrow pink tubular flowers have crimson lobes and yellow throats, arranged in a single plane along one side of the stem. It flowers throughout summer but may behave as a perennial in cooler areas.

Perennial flowering plant native from Europe to the western Transcaucasus and northwestern Africa. It sprawls across damp woodland floors, rooting where its softly hairy stems touch moist soil, and bears small lilac flowers from late spring to early summer.

A large, upright columnar cactus from South America, the Venezuelan apple cactus has grey-green to blue stems with variable spines that may be absent. Its large cream flowers open for one night, and its thornless fruits contain sweetening white flesh and crunchy edible seeds.
stories.edibilityNote: The thornless fruit has edible white flesh and small crunchy seeds; the flesh sweetens when the fruit opens fully.

stories.summary: An evergreen shrub or small tree from Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Thailand, it produces showy red, pink or white bell-shaped flowers in early to mid-spring. Its broad, dark green leaves have a silvery, fawn or brown hairy coating underneath.

A moss with green, bluish-green or occasionally yellowish growth and toothed leaves that curl when dry but spread when moist. Its distinctive spherical capsules begin green, then become brown and ridged with age.
A corm-growing plant endemic to the Western Cape, it occurs from Piketberg and the upper Olifants River Valley to the Kleinrivier and Riviersonderend Mountains as part of the fynbos.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A biennial herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. The entire pale grey-green plant, including its fruit, is densely covered in soft, star-shaped hairs, while yellow flowers form a long, dense spike.

Herbaceous perennial native to the south-eastern Alps and the Balkans. Its five-lobed leaves are aromatic when crushed, and pale pink flowers appear in summer. Cultivated varieties range from white through pink to magenta.

Tender perennial herb native to humid, wet parts of Brazil and Paraguay. Its elongated leaves contain intensely sweet compounds; Guaraní people used the plant for centuries to sweeten yerba mate and as a treat, while processed leaf extracts serve as sugar substitutes.
stories.edibilityNote: Guaraní people historically used the plant to sweeten yerba mate and as a treat; processed leaf extracts are used as sugar substitutes.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, rock toadflax occurs in mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.

Shrub or small tree native and widespread in New South Wales and Victoria; one subspecies is thought native in northern Tasmania but naturalised in the south. It has widely spreading, sharp needle-like leaves and warted woody fruit ending in a prominent beak with two small horns.
An annual clover distributed in Central and Western Europe, it has slightly drooping heads of five to seven bright yellowish-orange flowers from May to July. Its pods all turn in one direction.

A climbing or scrambling flowering plant endemic to eastern Australia. It has yellow flowers with more than thirty stamens, and their smell has been variously reported as resembling mothballs, animal urine or faeces.

An erect shrub endemic to eastern Australia, it has narrow leaves, shaggy young stems and crowded white flowers. Fire kills the plant, but it regenerates from seed and can also colonise sunny, unburnt sites.

A spreading shrub endemic to eastern Australia. It bears many mainly white flowers for several months from July, while its needle-shaped leaves end in sharp points and its rough fruits have a network of veins. Outside Australia it is invasive in South Africa, New Zealand and Portugal.

An upright shrub endemic to central eastern New South Wales, especially associated with sandstone country around Sydney. It has thin, firm bark, broad pointed leaves, relatively large white or pink flowers, and mature fruit that remains on the plant.
A small herbaceous perennial native to Australia. It has usually pale flowers and distinctive semicircular leaves that are dark green above and paler beneath.
An erect woody shrub endemic to eastern Australia. It has sharp-smelling leaves and dense heads of small white or pinkish flowers, which are widely used in floral arrangements.

A small, shrubby willow with a Eurosiberian Boreo-temperate range, it is widespread around western and northern European coasts. Its highly variable forms range, at least in the UK, from low, creeping, hairless plants to upright shrubs with silky leaves, occupying dunes, heaths, moors and fens.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Salix repens
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A water lily native to southern and eastern Asia, it blooms by day and has partly submerged or floating round leaves. Its flowers are usually white or blue, with angular petals creating a star-like shape.
stories.edibilityNote: Rhizomes require boiling to neutralise toxins and have been eaten as famine food or medicine; cooked stems are also consumed as a vegetable in Bangladesh.

stories.summary: A flowering plant whose subspecies Sedum hirsutum subsp. hirsutum is native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A rhizomatous perennial iris native to temperate and tropical Asia, fringed iris spreads by wiry runners into dense carpets. Its pale blue, lavender or white flowers have fringed petals and a yellow or orange crest.
stories.edibilityNote: In Japan, ground rhizomes provide starch; however, rhizomes and leaves are poisonous if mistakenly ingested and can cause stomach pain and vomiting.

stories.summary: A low evergreen subshrub native to most of Europe and North Africa, with another passage also placing its native range in Asia. It forms creeping mats and strongly scented lilac, pink-purple or magenta flower clusters. It can be used like domestic thyme as a milder-flavoured herb.
stories.edibilityNote: Used as an herb like domestic thyme, but with a milder flavour.

stories.summary: Deciduous to semi-evergreen oak tree native to southern Portugal, Spain, Tunisia, Algeria and Morocco. It has shallow-lobed leaves and bears acorns in shallow cups. A 2016–2019 mainland Portuguese assessment classified its single national population as Critically Endangered, with fewer than 250 mature trees estimated around Serra de Monchique.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Quercus canariensis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A houseplant species native to Brazil’s Atlantic Forest, the zebra-plant is sensitive to both too much and too little water. Its yellow bracts can persist for weeks, although the flowers last only a few days; the widely grown ‘Dania’ variety has deep green leaves with prominent white veins.

A succulent shrub originating from Central Africa, African milk tree is known only in cultivation. Its upright, two- or three-sided dark-green stems have pale V-shaped markings, paired thorns and drop-shaped leaves. It has never been known to flower and may be a hybrid; its poisonous latex can irritate skin.

An epiphytic orchid occurring from Trinidad and French Guiana through Venezuela and Colombia to northern Brazil. It has upright leafy stems and crowded, successively opening flowers that may be lavender, red, orange or yellow.

An evergreen flowering perennial native to tropical and southern Africa, the spider plant has long narrow leaves and fleshy, tuberous roots. Its arching flowering stems carry plantlets that droop, touch soil and form roots. The roots are reportedly edible, although preparation is unstated and mild laxative effects are claimed.
stories.edibilityNote: Tuberous roots are reportedly edible, with raw or cooked preparation unstated; Nguni people claim mild laxative effects.

stories.summary: Perennial fern native to Asia, extending from Southeast Asia to China, Japan, India, Sri Lanka, Pacific islands and Australia. Known as the Asian sword fern, it can grow up to 3 feet tall and has been introduced to the Americas and Hawaii.

A perennial flowering plant native to southwestern Europe and North Africa, it grows in somewhat moist meadows in Portugal’s Algarve under moderate grazing. There it has often been confused with another buttercup, so population estimates may be low.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Ranunculus macrophyllus
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A multicellular red alga with no explicitly documented native origin, Amphiroa rigida occurs across Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia, North and South America, the Caribbean, and islands in the Indian and Pacific oceans.

An evergreen perennial native to streams and seashores of Japan. It forms loose clumps of large, round or kidney-shaped, slightly fleshy leaves. Clusters of yellow, daisy-like flowers appear in autumn and winter.

A branching shrubby plant native to Western Cape Province, South Africa. Its small, fan-shaped leaves smell of lemon and have distinctively crinkled edges; small white-to-pink flowers appear from spring to summer.
stories.edibilityNote: The leaves are reportedly eaten in salads or used to flavour cakes and stir-fries; the source marks this section as unreferenced.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Antirrhinum meonanthum is present in mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and the Madeira Archipelago.

Flowering plant native to the Iberian Peninsula, where the typical subspecies is endemic; subsp. fontiqueri is reported as endemic to mainland Portugal. Both subspecies occur in mainland Portugal and are not protected under Portuguese or European Community law.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.

A tropical tree native to the Greater Sunda Islands, Malay Peninsula, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Its crushed leaves are aromatic, and its edible bell-shaped berries have thin skin and white, spongy flesh; they are eaten fresh and used in salads, sautéed dishes, and pickles.
stories.edibilityNote: The edible fruit is eaten fresh, in salads and lightly sautéed dishes, and made into pickles in Indian Ocean island cuisines.

stories.summary: A short-lived perennial herb endemic to Spain’s Sierra Nevada, with some reports from the nearby Sierra de Gádor. In the narrow sense, it has multiple flowering stems, narrow hairy grey-green leaves and yellow flowers; its fruits may be upright or drooping.

A herb whose native origin is not stated, it is found mainly in the Mediterranean region, especially Spain, France and Italy, in dry meadows. It has a small underground bulb, two threadlike leaves and usually no more than four yellow, star-shaped flowers. It flowers in February and early March.

Rare tufted perennial flowering plant with no explicitly stated native origin; it is found in mountainous southern Europe and southwest Asia, and was first noted in Ireland’s Caha Mountains in 1964. Its wiry stems rise from a woody base, bearing needle-like, often side-curving leaves and white five-petalled flowers from late spring through summer.

A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal, Murbeckiella boryi belongs to the mustard family. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation, including Annex V of the Habitats Directive.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A saxifrage native to Ireland, Portugal and Spain. It forms a rosette of elongated succulent leaves around an upright, leafless flowering stem and grows among acidic rocks in humus-rich alpine habitats. It is native to Ireland but absent from Great Britain.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Scrophularia herminii occurs in mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation, including Annex V of the Habitats Directive.

Flowering plant of unstated native origin, recorded across many mountain systems of the northern Iberian Peninsula. It grows in wild mountain grasslands, especially stony places. The subspecies caespitosus is endemic to Portugal’s Serra da Estrela and is legally protected.
Flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.

A tree endemic to southeastern Australia. It has thick, rough, stringy bark on its trunk and larger branches but smooth bark on thinner branches, along with curved adult leaves, white flowers and woody cup- or barrel-shaped fruit.

A small to medium flowering tree native to Tasmanian woodlands, cider gum has mostly smooth bark, bluish-green leaves and white flowers in groups of three. Tasmanian Aboriginal people used its sap to make a fermented beverage called way-a-linah.
stories.edibilityNote: Tasmanian Aboriginal people used the tree's sap to produce the fermented beverage way-a-linah.

stories.summary: Flowering sedge native to Africa, Australasia, Europe and the Pacific islands. It is commonly known as floating club-rush or floating scirpus.

A perennial rush native to southern Australia, New Zealand, Norfolk Island and Lord Howe Island. It forms vigorous tufts, bears many straw-coloured flowers and usually grows in periodically flooded, nutrient-poor soils around fresh or brackish waterways.

Ground-growing fern native only to Australia, including southeastern mainland regions and Tasmania. Rows of spore clusters line its fronds, which can carry buds that grow into small plants. As those buds become heavier, the fronds sag until they can root in the soil.

A tree endemic to southeastern Australia. It has thick, rough reddish-brown to black bark, with flower buds usually grouped in threes, white or pale pink flowers, and woody cylindrical or rounded fruit.

An erect flowering shrub native to continental Europe, Scandinavia, the Black Sea region, Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan. It is a pioneer of recently scoured riverbanks in mountainous areas and may have white, cream or pink flowers.
A perennial herb native to eastern Australia and New Zealand, often growing beside shady streams.
A tall, dense shrub or occasional tree native to southeastern Australia. Its papery bark and small, prolific flower heads distinguish it from similar species, and it often grows in swampy areas.
stories.edibilityNote: Aboriginal people used nectar from the flowers to make sweet drinks.

stories.summary: A shrub or small tree endemic to coastal Australia, it grows on dunes and cliffs and tolerates salt well. Its purple to black fruit is edible and suitable for jams and jellies.
stories.edibilityNote: The purple fruit is eaten and used to make jams and jellies.

stories.summary: A large shrub or small weeping tree native to southeastern Australia. It has rough grey fibrous bark, dense foliage with narrow hook-tipped leaves, and cylindrical clusters of pale flowers followed by woody capsules.

A shrub endemic to the Azores, it occurs on every island except Corvo and Graciosa. Its pointed, serrated leaves may turn reddish-yellow in autumn, while its clustered pinkish-white flowers are followed by fleshy, cylindrical black fruit.
A flowering plant described as endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and native to Madeira, but introduced to the Azores.

Evergreen perennial native to mountainous southwestern Europe, from the Pyrenees to Portugal. It forms dense clumps of white or near-white flowers from mid to late spring and prefers moist, well-drained sandy soil.
Flowering plant whose variety velucensis is native to mainland Portugal.

A flowering plant native to the high mountains of the Iberian Peninsula and southern France, Silene ciliata occurs in Portugal only in Serra da Estrela, in meadows on granite sand. Portugal’s 2020 mainland Red List assessed it as Endangered, with only two identified locations and continuing habitat decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Silene ciliata
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An upright shrub endemic to the Canary Islands, it has oblong leaves and terminal clusters of numerous white flowers. Flowering lasts from late winter to early summer.

A perennial herb or shrub found in southern and eastern Europe, Turkey, the Caucasus and Algeria. It has upright ochre-orange stems that are mostly leafless and scarred, with grey-green leaves clustered near their tips and flower heads.

A perennial sedge native to Eurasia, Africa and Australia, growing in wet ground and shallow water. It forms dense clumps of three-angled stems, with bladeless leaf sheaths and compact heads of cone-shaped flower spikes beside a stiff, stem-like bract.
Flowering grass with two subspecies documented as native in Portugal: subsp. farctus in mainland Portugal, and subsp. boreo-atlanticus in mainland Portugal and Madeira.

A succulent shrub or small tree of unspecified native origin, it is widespread in eastern South Africa and Eswatini and also abundant in the drier southern Cape. It commonly has reddish stems and green leaves. In Southern Africa it is commonly eaten, usually in salad or soup, but should not be confused with the mildly toxic jade plant.
stories.edibilityNote: Commonly eaten in Southern Africa, usually in salad or soup; it should not be confused with the mildly toxic jade plant.

stories.summary: A small banana species native to Southeast Asia, including Bangladesh, Burma and India, flowering banana has green foliage tinged with pink. It bears pink flowers and small dark pink or crimson, seeded, inedible fruit, while its brightly coloured bracts make it a memorable ornamental.
stories.edibilityNote: The male bud may be cooked or used in salads; the seeded fruit is inedible.

stories.summary: Green seaweed native to the northeastern Atlantic from Ireland south to the Azores and Cape Verde. Its highly branched fronds feel spongy and felt-like and bear colourless hairs visible underwater; it grows on exposed rocks in deep pools on the lower shore.

A dwarf, aromatic groundcover shrub native to oceanic parts of northwestern Portugal and Spain, the Azores and Madeira. It forms mats of narrow, smooth leaves and bears flattened heads of rose, lilac or white flowers from late spring into summer.

A sprawling perennial herb native to the western Mediterranean, from southwestern France through the Iberian Peninsula to the Azores, Morocco and Algeria. It grows in damp ground or water and overwinters underwater in its native habitat. In Portugal, the whole plant, fresh or dried, is added to stews, salads, soups, cheeses and sauces, and used in liqueur infusions.
stories.edibilityNote: In Portugal, the whole plant is used fresh or dried in savoury foods and in liqueur infusions.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to southern Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina, giant sea holly has very long, narrow leaves resembling pampas grass. Introduced to Portugal, it has been legally classified there as invasive since 1999 and has established in damp areas around the Tagus and Mondego river basins.

A perennial flowering shrub endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and Aquitaine, with an Azorean subspecies that may be a separate species. Male and female flowers usually grow on separate plants, although some southwestern Iberian plants also bear bisexual flower clusters whose fruit tends to be underdeveloped. Its ripe, white, tough-skinned fruits are edible, mildly acidic and lemony; people in Iberia have eaten the berries since at least the Middle Ages.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe white fruits are edible, mildly acidic and lemony; the berries have been consumed in Iberia since at least the Middle Ages.

stories.summary: Small pinkish seaweed recorded from the Faroe Islands and Norway to the Mediterranean, including waters around Britain and Ireland. It forms firmly attached, flat lobed crusts that may become knobbly or bleached, commonly in shallow pools and beneath cover down to 8 metres.
A plant native to the Caribbean.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Silene portensis subsp. portensis is native to mainland Portugal.

A medium-sized red marine alga whose native origin is not specified; it occurs from Norway and the Faroes to Senegal, the Mediterranean and the Canary Islands. Its flattened branches alternate between long and short forms, with curved side branches creating a comb-like pattern.

A small, uncommon seaweed found around Great Britain and Ireland, the Azores, and the Atlantic coast from Massachusetts to Virginia, Gymnogongrus griffithsiae grows in lower-shore rock pools and just below the shore. It is dark purplish brown, with erect, stiff fronds that fork in one plane and have slightly flattened tips.

Small red marine alga of unstated native origin, recorded around the British Isles and from Norway and the Mediterranean to the Indian and Pacific oceans. It grows in shaded upper-shore sites as dark brown, creeping, moss-like branches visibly pinched at intervals.
A multicellular red marine alga with no stated native origin, found across Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia, as well as islands in the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans.

A red alga with no specific native origin stated, Amphiroa beauvoisii is widely distributed, mainly in tropical and subtropical waters. It attaches to intertidal rocks by a calcified base and produces flat, branching, fan-like growth whose form varies with location.
Perennial herb native to the mountains of Southern Europe, with a fuzzy woody stem and paired leaves. Its generally violet flowers appear between May and August depending on altitude.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant can be brewed and served as tea.

stories.summary: A wild banana plant originally from Assam and the eastern Himalayas. It bears fuzzy pink fruits on upright flower stalks, and the ripe fruits peel themselves back. Their soft, sweet flesh is edible, but the tough seeds can chip a tooth.
stories.edibilityNote: The soft, sweet fruit flesh can be eaten, but the tough seeds can chip a tooth.

stories.summary: A bulbous perennial native to South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province, silver squill is often cultivated and grows well with minimal care.
Flowering plant endemic to Brazil. Its centre turns red shortly before flowering, creating its characteristic blushing appearance.
Evergreen flowering climber native to Colombia, with red stems and large heart-shaped leaves. Its deep-red, fragrant flower structures appear in summer and autumn.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are toxic because they contain calcium oxalate and should be kept away from young children.

stories.summary: Wetland plant native to Japan, Korea and eastern Asia. Its long, narrow, slightly curved leaves grow in very moist soil or partly or fully submerged, while its rhizomes can spread aggressively into dense groundcover.

A hornwort whose native origin is not stated. It grows in moist soil and waterways, forming a nearly flat, dark green, slightly glossy body. When numerous, its slender green spore capsules resemble tufts of grass.

A seaweed with no native origin specified, Ulva clathrata occurs across parts of Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, as well as several oceans, gulfs and seas. It is light green and forms thin, cylindrical threads.
A green seaweed found worldwide, Flexuous Gutweed is a large, tubular and highly variable alga. Its branches have cells arranged lengthwise and sometimes crosswise.

A tree-like cactus from southern South America, probably including Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina. Its branching, segmented stems are usually spineless, while large white flowers open on summer nights and are followed by red-to-yellow fruits with white pulp.
stories.edibilityNote: In Rio Grande do Sul, the fruits are appreciated by local people.

stories.summary: Small flowering tree native to the Caribbean, including Jamaica, Hispaniola, Puerto Rico, and the Leeward and Windward Islands. Its showy flowers make it a popular ornamental.

Fast-growing perennial vine endemic to Rio de Janeiro state in Brazil. Its long woody stems twine around supports, while pink-red funnel-shaped flowers appear over a long period from spring into autumn.

Perennial plant native to several countries in southern South America. Purple cultivars have three-part leaves that fold down at night, when disturbed or in harsh sunlight; white or pale pink flowers also close at night.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves and flowers are edible in moderation, but large quantities may cause toxicity from soluble calcium oxalates.

stories.summary: A tender trailing perennial native to southern Africa, it has aromatic, glossy, rounded leaves that sometimes show deep purple centres and undersides. White, pale violet or pale pink flowers may appear sporadically year-round, especially in spring and late autumn.
Fruit tree native to the Amazon rainforest in Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Ecuador. It bears pale green fruits that turn bright yellow when ripe, with juicy, aromatic and strongly acidic pulp.
stories.edibilityNote: The acidic fruit is eaten fresh, preferably with sugar, or processed into juices, nectars, marmalades, ice creams and other foods.

stories.summary: Creeping evergreen flowering perennial native to rainforests of Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador and northern Brazil. Its dark green leaves are marked by strongly contrasting veins, from white to deep pink or red, while its stems are lightly fuzzy and its flowers small and pale.

A perennial flowering plant native to eastern Brazil's Atlantic Forest, northeastern Argentina and Paraguay. It is cultivated as a decorative potted or landscape feature plant in warm temperate and subtropical climates.
Herbaceous plant native to Venezuela, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru. It has been introduced to places including Hawaii and the Galápagos Islands.

A rhizomatous flowering plant native to the eastern Himalayas from southern Bhutan to northern Myanmar. It is prized for dark leaves marked with prominent silvery-grey bands and is usually grown for foliage rather than flowers.

Evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand. Its leaves usually have seven sharply toothed leaflets, with young leaves shiny and purplish underneath. Māori used its timber to make fire by friction and its fruit juice as a dye.

Soft-wooded shrub native to eastern Australia; in New Zealand it is reported as indigenous, though some authorities consider it introduced. It has blue-purple flowers and orange-red to scarlet fruit. Ripe berries were traditional Māori food and were stewed or made into pies and jam by early European settlers; using leaves in hāngī is now discouraged because they contain poisonous alkaloids.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe berries were traditional Māori food and early settlers stewed them or made pies and jam; leaf use in hāngī is now discouraged.

stories.summary: A climbing cactus native to Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela, yellow dragonfruit has exceptionally large night-blooming flowers. Its spiny yellow fruit has edible white flesh with a pleasant, mildly sweet flavour; hybrids may have differently coloured skin or flesh.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit’s white interior is edible and mildly sweet; hybrid fruit may have pink flesh.

stories.summary: Salt-tolerant flowering plant native to Portugal. It grows in estuary and lagoon salt marshes, with fleshy stems and scale-like leaves that are green in spring and summer but reddish in autumn.

A woody evergreen vine native to southern tropical India, it bears long hanging clusters of strongly curved flowers. The flowers are rich yellow with maroon to brownish-red tips and appear from spring to autumn.

A densely branching flowering subshrub found from Mediterranean Europe and northern and central Africa through western Asia, Cressa cretica also occurs in Southeast Asia and Australia, where its native status is unclear. It has silky-haired leaves and white flowers and grows in salty, seasonally wet places.
A flowering plant introduced in mainland Portugal.

A fast-growing tropical tree native to tropical South America. Its edible fruit ripens from green to yellow and has a soft-spined surface that bruises and blackens easily, contributing to a shelf life of under a week. The very soft, sweet pulp is usually eaten fresh, though it is also cooked and made into wine in Brazil.
stories.edibilityNote: The sweet fruit pulp is usually eaten fresh; chefs sometimes cook it, and it has been made into wine in Brazil.

stories.summary: A perennial shrub or subshrub native to South America, lemon verbena has glossy, pointed leaves that release a strong lemon scent when bruised. Its leaves flavour foods and drinks, including fish, poultry, jams and herbal tea, and are also used to flavour liqueurs.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves are used to flavour cooked dishes, marinades, dressings, jams, puddings, yogurt and beverages, and to make herbal tea and flavour liqueurs.

stories.summary: An aromatic, spiny deciduous shrub or small tree native to Japan and Korea; its natural range also includes mainland China. Its scarlet berries burst open in autumn to scatter black seeds. Young leaves and ground or prepared fruits are used as flavorings in Japanese and Korean cooking.
stories.edibilityNote: Mature fruits are ground as spice; immature berries are blanched, salted or simmered, while young leaves, shoots and male flowers are eaten in Japan and Korea.

stories.summary: A stemless evergreen shrub native to south-central and southeastern North America. Its sharply pointed, sword-like leaves often fold under their own weight, and tall summer flower clusters rise above them with creamy white, bell-shaped blooms.

A deciduous tree native to tropical Southeast Asia and northern Australasia, it produces masses of golden summer flowers. Its pods change from red to black as they ripen, and the tree is widely planted as an ornamental.

A creeping wetland perennial native to Western and Central Europe, creeping marshwort is rare throughout its range. Its trailing stems root at their joints and can form mats where flooding, mowing or grazing keeps taller vegetation in check.
stories.edibilityNote: Its leaves taste mild and parsley-like, but the source only speculates about edibility and documents no clear human food use.

stories.summary: A low-growing, hairless perennial flowering plant native to western Europe, found in ditches, streams, and fresh or brackish wetlands. Its hollow stems root where nodes touch the ground, and crushed leaves smell of carrot. Traditionally harvested in several Mediterranean countries, its young leaves and tender shoots are eaten raw, boiled, or as a condiment, though it can be confused with allegedly poisonous lesser water parsnip.
stories.edibilityNote: Young leaves and tender shoots are traditionally eaten in several Mediterranean countries, raw in salads, boiled, or used as a condiment.

stories.summary: A small marine red alga recorded from Great Britain and Ireland south to Portugal and the Mediterranean. Its flattened, fan-shaped fronds grow from a disc-like anchor and divide into blades with rounded tips.

Flowering herbaceous perennial native to southern China, the Himalayas, India and Indochina. It grows along forest edges and in mountain grasslands, producing flowers from red and orange to almost yellow.

A perennial flowering herb native mainly to Missouri and Arkansas, with additional populations in Louisiana and Illinois, Drummond's goldenrod spreads through underground stems. A single plant can bear 200 or more small yellow flower heads in a large, sometimes drooping, branched display.

A small bulb-growing species of garlic native to the Mediterranean region, Allium chamaemoly has an extremely short or absent flower stalk, so its flowers appear at ground level. Its white flowers usually have a purple stripe, while its flat, grass-like leaves often bear long white hairs.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Allium chamaemoly
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A bulb-forming perennial wild onion native to southern Iberia, the Balearic Islands, Sicily and North Africa; it might be introduced in the Azores. Its narrow leaves bear conspicuous long white hairs, and its white flowers have yellow anthers.

A tall herbaceous perennial of unstated native origin, giant fennel has hollow stalks and produces resin from its root or lower stalk. Its young stems and flower clusters were eaten in ancient Rome and remain eaten in Morocco, though culinary use can cause poisoning.
stories.edibilityNote: Young stems and inflorescences were eaten in ancient Rome and remain eaten in Morocco; poisoning can occur, and Sardinia has poisonous and non-poisonous chemotypes.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

Clump-forming, fleshy-leaved plant endemic to South Africa's Eastern Cape Province. Its small light-green rosettes usually have slightly bristly leaf margins and transparent streaks or tips; in the wild, the plant is mostly buried in sand with only these tips showing.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A herbaceous perennial native to the Mediterranean. Its nearly leafless upright stalks carry yellow flower heads ringed by thorny bracts, including stiff golden inner bracts, and it flowers from June through August.
A low, trailing succulent endemic to New Zealand. Its fleshy, three-sided leaves and white-to-deep-pink daisy-like flowers distinguish it on cliffs, gravel beaches, salt meadows and estuaries.
stories.edibilityNote: European settlers ate its bland, fleshy capsules and pickled its leaves.

stories.summary: A tree fern native to New Zealand.

A deciduous flowering climber native to mountainous Asia from Afghanistan to Taiwan. In late spring it produces masses of scented white or pink flowers for about four weeks, each with four petals and prominent yellow anthers.
A Centaurea species found in the Iberian Peninsula.

A culinary herb in the buckwheat family, French sorrel has a tart, slightly lemony taste from oxalic acid and may become bitter later in the season. It is eaten in salads, soups and sauces, especially sauces for fish.
stories.edibilityNote: Used as a culinary herb in salads, soups and sauces, especially with fish; tart from oxalic acid and sometimes bitter later in the season.

stories.summary: A low woody flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and occurring across southwestern Europe and North Africa. It grows in scrub and uncultivated ground, flowering from May to July.

A herb found only on the Iberian Peninsula, mainly at inland sites in Spain and a small neighbouring area of Portugal. Its recognised subspecies and varieties are largely geographically separate, and the plant blooms from April to October in habitats including woodland edges, scrub and roadsides.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
An ornamental rhizomatous perennial herb native to Europe.

A flowering rush native to northwestern Africa, many Mediterranean islands, warmer parts of southern, central and eastern Europe, and western Asia, sand rush favours wet, nutrient-poor rock, sand or clay soils. It often occurs in clay pits, old brickyards and along roads.

A sedge native in Wallonia, sweet galingale is also widespread across Africa, southern Europe, the Indian subcontinent and western Asia. It has creeping underground stems and upright triangular stalks, and grows in shallow water or damp ground such as pond edges. Its thick yellowish underground stems are traditionally harvested to distil sweet-scented oil for perfume.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A flowering plant in the daisy family, Leucanthemopsis pulverulenta includes a subspecies endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. This subspecies occurs in mainland Portugal and is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
An annual herb of unstated native origin, with broad leaves and a self-supporting growth form.
Annual flowering plant native to the Palearctic, from the western Mediterranean to Central Asia. It grows in sandy, well-drained ground, particularly coastal and desert dunes.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Within Portugal it is characteristic of major-river floodplains, occurs at only three known locations along the Douro and Tagus, and was assessed as Endangered with an estimated population of about 500 mature plants.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Andryala ragusina
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A lupine native to Iberia. Some accessions may have potential for grain or forage.
stories.edibilityNote: Some accessions were described as potentially good grain, but actual human food use is not documented.
