A plant native to Europe, it is also widespread across temperate Asia and North Africa.
Flowering geophyte native to mainland Portugal. It has dark purple, glandular-hairy stems and spikes of dark reddish-purple flowers.

An evergreen perennial herb native across the Iberian Peninsula, Balearic Islands, France, Italy, Malta and North Africa. Its solitary flower heads have overlapping bracts whose broad, spoon-like tips create a pinecone appearance, surrounding white to pink florets that often have purple tips.
Annual herb with no native origin stated in the supplied source. It is self-supporting, has simple leaves and remains very small.

A small evergreen shrub native to Europe’s western Mediterranean region, Cneorum tricoccon has a nearly rounded form. Its yellowish flowers appear from June to July, followed by seeds ripening from August to September.
stories.edibilityNote: Its fruit is described as having no food value, but not explicitly as inedible.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to southeastern Europe, including parts of Italy, Greece, Albania and the former Yugoslavia.
An evergreen tree native to Japan and the Ryukyu Islands. Its nuts are edible but bitter and contain tannins, which soaking in water removes; it is also cultivated as an ornamental.
stories.edibilityNote: The bitter nuts are edible for people; soaking them in water removes their tannins.

stories.summary: Ornamental shrub native from central China to the Korean Peninsula. It flowers in May and bears small, sour fruit reported to have a pleasantly sweet flavour and to be used in pies.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is reported to be sweet but sour and used in pies.

stories.summary: A plant native to China, Mallotus japonicus is also found in Japan and Korea. It has red young shoots and large leaves traditionally used to wrap food; its young leaves are edible when boiled.
stories.edibilityNote: Young leaves are edible when boiled; large leaves were traditionally used to wrap food.

stories.summary: A flowering grass native to Europe and Asia. It was deliberately planted in North America and now occurs in several US states.
A tree in the olive family, with no native origin stated in the supplied text. Its toothed oval leaves are dark green above and dark blue beneath, with both surfaces hairless.

A shrub native to South Africa, the limestone pincushion grows in coastal fynbos on limestone deposits. Its globe-shaped flower heads are usually grouped in twos or threes, with bright yellow flowers that turn orange over time. Flowering occurs between August and December.

A tropical strangler tree native to Southeast Asia and Northeast Australia, it begins on a larger tree and eventually engulfs it. Dense woolly hairs, greyish-white bark and bright yellow-to-red fleshy fruit distinguish it.

A wood-sorrel-family plant native to Central America and western South America, spiral woodsorrel is cultivated ornamentally. Its cultivars include foliage ranging from bright yellow-green and copper-red to nearly black or variegated purple.

An endangered tree fern of mountain rainforests in East and Southeast Asia. In Japan, its new leaves and shoots are boiled to remove bitterness before being eaten, while its boiled core is a festival food on the Yaeyama and Ishigaki islands.
stories.edibilityNote: Stem starch is eaten in China and Taiwan; Japan uses boiled young leaves and shoots, and boiled core as a regional festival food.

stories.summary: A succulent shrub native to South Africa’s Western Cape, Eastern Cape and southern KwaZulu-Natal, it grows on dry, rocky ground. Its rounded, powdery gray leaves have red edges and resemble silver dollars, while star-shaped pink or white flowers appear in summer.

Plant occurring in two widely separated areas: the mountains of southern France and north-central and eastern Spain, and the Baltic islands of Öland and Gotland. It lacks runners, and its flower cup has teeth about as long as its tube.

An aromatic perennial shrub endemic to the Madeira archipelago, it grows on rocky coastal sites in Madeira and the Desertas and is common around Porto Santo’s peaks and islets. It has whitish-grey felted growth, triangular leaves and dense clusters of small yellow-centred flower heads.
Plant endemic to the Canary Islands, frequent in dry areas at lower elevations. It has rounded flower heads and flat leaf lobes.

A salt-tolerant shrub distributed across parts of Africa, the Middle East and eastward to India, with no specific native origin stated. Its woody-based, heavily branched growth occurs naturally in salt-affected habitats, including coastal bushland, saline inland sites, desert wadis and dry riverbeds.

A moss of unspecified native origin, it is widespread in Europe and reported from nearby parts of Africa and Asia. Its broad, dull-green leaves have a nerve that stops short of the tip, and it rarely produces spores, usually dispersing through small orange gemmae.
A liverwort native to Eurasia and Northern America.

Bulbous flowering perennial native to South Africa, specifically the Eastern Cape, KwaZulu-Natal, Free State and Drakensberg Mountains. It bears faintly scented, bright pink flowers with frilly tips in late summer and autumn, while its strap-shaped leaves do not appear until spring.

A creeping flowering shrub native to rocky slopes in Tibet, Sichuan and Yunnan in China. It is drought-tolerant and has small glossy leaves, tiny rose-like flowers and showy red fruit; its low growth also suits bonsai.

A deciduous shrub native to central and eastern Europe and southwest Asia; Spanish plants may also belong to this species. Its leaves have pale grey hairs underneath, while its small white or pale pink flowers are followed by dark red fruits.
A plant species found on Atlantic Forest hillsides in Paraná and Santa Catarina, Brazil. It grows 4–6 metres tall, but can reach 30 metres in cultivation, and fruits from January to March.
Flowering plant endemic to the Canary Islands. It forms large leaf rosettes close to the ground, with tall spikes of yellow flowers; its five subspecies are native to different islands.

An evergreen climbing shrub native to western Iberia and northern Morocco. Its aerial rootlets cling to trees, cliffs and walls, while unsupported plants form ground cover; it has broad leathery leaves and black ripe fruits.

A deciduous tree native to the Caspian region of northern Iran and southeastern Azerbaijan. Its smooth bark peels into a patchwork of pink, cinnamon, green and pale yellow, while its glossy leaves turn purple, orange and brilliant red in autumn.

Orchid native to Peru, Bolivia and Brazil, mainly found in very wet, moss-covered, semi-boggy areas. Its fragrant flowers are green with red-brown markings and have a white lip marked with violet. Successfully pollinated flowers close slightly and may remain colourful for up to three months.

Coastal succulent occurring along western South Africa from around Cape Town and the Cape Peninsula east to Mossel Bay. Numerous serpent-like stems arise from a short central base, giving it the appearance of Medusa's head.

A flowering plant native to Bangladesh, Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and southeastern and south-central China, where it inhabits tropical swamps and rainforests. It has lance-shaped leaves growing from a central point and occasionally produces white flowers followed by oval reddish fruits. Its calcium oxalate crystals are poisonous if ingested and can severely burn and swell the mouth and tongue.
stories.edibilityNote: Calcium oxalate crystals make the plant poisonous if ingested, causing severe burning and swelling of the mouth and tongue.

stories.summary: A small deciduous tree native to China, Taiwan, Myanmar, Laos and Vietnam. It bears white flowers in early spring and variably coloured plums; fully ripe fruit can be eaten raw, while the pits and leaves are poisonous to humans.
stories.edibilityNote: Fully ripe fruit can be eaten raw; pits and leaves are poisonous, with crushed pits especially advised against.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to Colombia. It occurs in the departments of Antioquia, Boyacá, Cundinamarca, Meta and Santander.

A tree found across the Indian subcontinent, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, usually beside rivers or dry riverbeds. It has a buttressed trunk, broad crown, smooth grey bark and fibrous, five-winged fruit. Its leaves feed the moth that produces commercially important wild tassar silk.
An annual, self-supporting herb, brown vetchling has broad compound leaves.

A sub-shrub and herb native to the western Mediterranean region, felty germander has small pink-to-white flowers. Its leaves are used in cooking and medicine, although the plant may cause liver toxicity.
stories.edibilityNote: Leaves are used in cooking; the plant also has traditional medicinal use and potential liver toxicity.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to Bolivia, southern Brazil, northern Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. Widely introduced through drier tropical and subtropical regions, it has escaped gardens and become an environmental weed in parts of Australia.

Bromeliad naturally found in Atlantic Coast restinga vegetation from Bahia to Espírito Santo in eastern Brazil. It forms many long, thorny leaves and may be orange, green, crimson or yellow. It usually grows on the ground but can also grow on other plants.

A subtropical succulent native to the arid Karoo of South Africa’s Eastern Cape, Euphorbia obesa is a thornless, ball-shaped plant. It usually has eight ridges and grey-green skin marked with lighter or darker horizontal stripes, sometimes developing red and purple areas in direct sunlight. Its latex is toxic.
A climbing wintergreen flowering plant occurring in Madeira and the Canary Islands. It has few or no thorns, simple flower clusters and fruits that turn black when ripe.
A perennial herb whose native origin is not stated. It is self-supporting, with simple broad leaves and dry fruit.

A densely foliaged shrub or small tree native to Australia, moonah has rough dark bark and a trunk often twisted by wind. Its white or cream flower spikes appear mainly in summer, followed by woody capsules spaced along the branches.
A geophyte occurring in KwaZulu-Natal, from the Ngome Forests to the KwaZulu-Natal Midlands. It has fewer than ten subpopulations and has lost 30% of its habitat in the past 90 years.
Flowering plant whose subspecies Silene psammitis subsp. psammitis is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant whose listed varieties, var. nitida and var. meridionalis, are native to mainland Portugal.

A large shrub or small tree endemic to southern and eastern South Africa and neighbouring territories such as Eswatini, it bears abundant, extremely fragrant flowers with long tubes accessible only to nocturnal hawkmoths. Its hard, woody fruit can remain on the tree for years if large browsers or elephants do not eat it.
An asphodel endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.
A flowering shrub native to South America, shell flower grows in shady, damp places and has yellow flowers.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and the Madeira Archipelago, belonging to the pea family.

Small herbaceous plant of unspecified native origin, found in the central and southern Iberian Peninsula. It has hairy reddish, usually unbranched upright stems and vivid yellow flower heads in spring; its seeds bear tufts for wind dispersal.

An Iberian-endemic herbaceous perennial, Leucanthemopsis pallida is usually covered in whitish hairs and woody at the base. Its outer flowers may be yellow or white; above 1,700 metres they are white, often tinged with purple.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Ranunculus ollissiponensis subsp. ollissiponensis is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant with no explicitly stated native origin for the species; its Madeira subspecies is endemic to Macaronesia.

A low shrub or small tree native to the Canary Islands, western Morocco and Western Sahara. Its spineless, partly succulent stems carry leaves clustered at their tips. In the Canary Islands, the leaves were gathered and cooked as greens, while its milky latex is poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: In the Canary Islands, leaves were historically gathered and cooked as a green vegetable; the milky latex is poisonous.

stories.summary: A shrub endemic to Macaronesia, occurring on some Canary Islands and Madeira. It is distinguished by hanging flower clusters, divided leaves with oval leaflets, and pear-shaped fruits.
Perennial flowering plant endemic to La Palma in the Canary Islands. Its many flower heads have pink outer flowers and mauve-purple centres, accompanied by roughly rounded, toothed leaves.

A climbing groundcover native to Australia, climbing saltbush spreads in vine-like, light-green branches with small, semi-succulent arrowhead leaves. Its inconspicuous green summer flowers become conspicuous tiny bright-red berries in early autumn. Early European settlers around Adelaide boiled it with other saltbushes as a substitute for greens.
stories.edibilityNote: Early European settlers around Adelaide boiled the plant with other saltbush species as a substitute for greens.

stories.summary: A flowering shrub endemic to La Palma in the Canary Islands. It normally produces numerous spikes of blue flowers in early summer, although a hybrid may have white or pink flowers, and it tolerates cold poorly.
Flowering plant native to the western Mediterranean. Its tissues contain the diterpenoid alkaloid graciline.

Germander endemic to southwestern Portugal, it is restricted to the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park. It grows in low scrubland on fixed dunes, cliffs and coastal rocks, on sand or limestone.

A small shrub native to France, Spain and the Mediterranean, it grows in sandy ground around beaches. Its white flowers are tinged purple and bloom in March and April; in mainland Portugal it is restricted to limestone sea cliffs in the southwestern Algarve.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Astragalus tragacantha
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A perennial herb endemic to the western Mediterranean, the shrubby violet blooms throughout winter and into early spring. Its flowers naturally occur in colours including magenta, gold, blue, purple, maroon and off-white.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Viola arborescens
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A shrub endemic to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula, in southern Portugal and southwestern Spain. Usually low-growing, it has narrow dark-green leaves and white flowers with a yellow spot at each petal’s base.

An annual thistle native to the Mediterranean region and Middle East, with deeply lobed, grey-green leaves marked by white veins. Sharp spines edge the leaves and surround its dense purple flower heads.
stories.edibilityNote: On Crete, tender shoots are peeled and eaten raw.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.
A flowering plant native to continental Portugal.
A flowering plant native to Spain, including the Balearic Islands, France, including Corsica, Portugal and Sardinia. It belongs to the lily family.
A slow-growing shrub native to southern Africa, it has solitary reddish flowers, often bright red in Richtersveld. Its seeds develop inside distinctive inflated capsules resembling Chinese lanterns.

A flowering plant found in southern Spain and parts of North Africa, growing among rocks and at the foot of rocky slopes. It has thick, hairy, heart-shaped leaves and pink flowers crowded towards the tops of its flower spikes.
A perennial or biennial herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It has tall glandular-hairy stems, deeply lobed leaves and solitary yellow flowers marked dark purple at the base.

A moss with no native origin stated, dwarf neckera occurs in much of Europe, southwest Asia, North Africa, the Canary Islands and Madeira. It forms slightly glossy green mats and often bears threadlike shoots used for vegetative reproduction. It usually grows on tree bark in shady, humid forests, but occasionally occurs on rocks or old walls.
Flowering plant represented in mainland Portugal by three varieties described as native there.
An ornamental sedge native to central and southern Japan. Its many cultivars are mostly variegated, and it tolerates heavy shade and wet soil while spreading slowly as ground cover.

A planktonic green microalga found in temperate or tropical nutrient-poor lakes and estuaries; no native origin is stated. Its colonies sit in a lipid-rich matrix, and much of its hydrocarbon oil lies outside its thick-walled cells.
stories.edibilityNote: Its hydrocarbon oils are described as inedible.

stories.summary: Evergreen succulent perennial native to the southern Alps in Europe. It forms rosettes of thick, water-storing leaves, usually green with reddish-purple tips, and reproduces both by budding and by flowering once before dying.

A unicellular desmid found worldwide in acidic waters, especially around the edges of large ponds and lakes. Its symmetrical cell is deeply divided into two identical halves, whose corners extend into paired straight or slightly curved spines.
An evergreen shrub endemic to Brazil, becoming semi-deciduous in cooler areas. Its non-fragrant flowers open pale purple and fade to white.

A flowering plant whose subspecies globulariifolia is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal. The variety major is likewise Iberian-endemic and present in mainland Portugal, where it has legal protection under European conservation measures.
A prostrate shrub native to Spain and Portugal.

Perennial herb endemic to the southwestern coastal strip of the Iberian Peninsula. In mainland Portugal it grows in sandy scrub and open pinewoods between Olhão and the São Vicente plateau; assessments conducted in 2016–2019 classified it as Vulnerable because of its limited range and declining habitat and mature population.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Armeria macrophylla
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Wild onion native to Spain, Portugal, Morocco and Algeria in the western Mediterranean.

A perennial wild onion native to parts of the Mediterranean, including southern Europe, North Africa and the eastern Mediterranean. It bears tight flower clusters with white tepals that may have pink or red midveins.
A flowering plant originating in Central Asia that produces apples. It has been introduced to mainland Portugal and the Azores.

A succulent shrub whose native origin is not stated, it has grey-green shoots and broad, simple leaves. Its daisy-like flowers have yellow centres and petals that vary between pink and purple with the season.
A rainforest tree endemic to eastern Australia. It has narrow, glossy leaves and end-of-branch clusters of white flowers, followed by spherical red berries with white flesh surrounding one seed.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

Woody flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and introduced in the Azores. A 1913 account describes lance-shaped leaves and stems that become almost leafless, with flowering from July to November. It occurred mainly in central and southern cultivated ground, hedges, paths and coastal sands.

Perennial bulbous herb native to the western Mediterranean, including central and southern Portugal, Spain and North Africa. Its narrow green leaves have a white stripe that tends to fade during flowering, while its flowers are white inside with a broad green stripe outside.
A unicellular green alga with a cosmopolitan distribution. It lives in fresh water across a wide range of acidity and alkalinity.

A compact, highly branched shrub of unspecified native origin, it grows in rock crevices in South Africa. It has grey, hairy twigs, tightly rolled needle-shaped leaves and dense heads of small white flowers.
An evergreen shrub or small tree native to South Africa. Its reddish, bare twigs carry leathery leaves with differently coloured surfaces, while its small fragrant flowers are white and purple.

A freshwater green alga with a cosmopolitan distribution, Gonium pectorale usually forms colonies of 16 cells, though colonies may have 8 or 32. Its typical colony has four central cells surrounded by 12 cells with their flagella pointing outward.

An aromatic, deciduous spiny shrub native to parts of East and Southeast Asia and the northern Indian subcontinent. Its fruit and seeds provide timut pepper, valued in Nepalese cooking for its aroma and numbing sensation, while winged leaf stalks help distinguish the plant.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit and seeds are used as timut pepper; in Nepal they season sauces, pickles, meats, dumplings and other dishes.

stories.summary: A herbaceous perennial native to Mexico. Its dark red to brownish-red flowers smell like chocolate, with the fragrance becoming stronger toward the end of the day, but the plant should not be eaten.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant is explicitly described as unsuitable for eating despite its chocolate-like scent.

stories.summary: A cactus with an uncertain native range because sources disagree. It has been introduced to regions across the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Madagascar and eastern Australia.

A low, shrubby thistle native to Madeira and the Canary Islands, growing on cliffs and rocky slopes. Its narrow, leathery leaves have densely white-felted undersides, and its flower heads contain creamy-yellow tubular florets surrounded by stiff bracts.
A flowering plant in the daisy family, native only to the Madeira archipelago.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it is recorded in mainland Portugal.
A cactus of unspecified native origin. After its spines are removed, the fruit is eaten raw or stewed, dried for winter, or ground into flour for mush by the Zuni people.
stories.edibilityNote: The Zuni remove fruit spines, then eat the fruit raw or stewed, dry it, or grind it into flour for mush.

stories.summary: A moss whose native origin is not stated, recorded in Europe, North Africa, the Azores, the Canary Islands and North America. It usually forms loose mats on deciduous trees, with creeping main shoots and short upright branches. Its capsules sit on short side shoots and are partly enclosed by elongated leaves.

Rare subtropical rainforest tree of unspecified native origin, occurring on volcanic soils around the Mount Warning area of eastern Australia. It has unusually large, thick leaves; its pale fruit is unpleasant raw but valued in mixed preserves.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is unpleasant raw but described as an excellent ingredient in mixed preserves.

stories.summary: Fern native to Madeira and Africa from Kenya to South Africa, occurring in subtropical regions.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. Its wider range is limited to southwestern Iberia, northwestern Morocco and the Canary Islands, where it inhabits saline margins of small coastal brackish lagoons that dry in summer. In mainland Portugal it is currently known only from the southern Algarve coast.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Frankenia boissieri
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering shrub native to Eswatini, KwaZulu-Natal and South Africa's Cape Provinces. It is known as the sweet pea shrub and is considered of least ecological concern in South Africa.

A small deciduous tree or shrub native to northeastern China, Korea and the Russian Far East, it has lobed leaves that turn red, yellow and orange in autumn and may remain dried on the plant through winter. New growth bears white, sticky hairs, distinguishing it from the similar Acer sieboldianum.

A shrub found in the Western Ghats’ shola forests in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Its purplish-blue flowers appear in September and October on a documented 12-year cycle; each individual reproduces once and then dies.

A Kalanchoe species native to Madagascar, Kalanchoe porphyrocalyx has produced many cultivars. The many-flowered cultivar ‘Wendy’ may come from this species alone or from a cross with Kalanchoe miniata.
A small to medium-sized tree, Chinese hawthorn has bright red fruit; its native origin is not stated. In northern Chinese cuisine, the ripe fruit is used in desserts, sweets, preserves and wine.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe fruits are used in northern Chinese desserts and traditionally in candies, preserves, wine and Cantonese sweet-and-sour sauce.

stories.summary: A wild rose native to Mediterranean Europe, it occurs from the Iberian Peninsula and southern France to parts of Italy and the larger western Mediterranean islands.

Perennial flowering plant native to temperate Eurasia, from Europe to Siberia and parts of western, central and eastern Asia. It can grow from underground stems, and its three accepted subspecies have distinct geographic ranges.

A perennial herb native to Malta, Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, southern Italy and Spain. It is deep-rooted and drought-resistant, with red flowers and jointed pods whose thorny yellow surface turns brown when mature.
A perennial flowering plant native to South Africa’s Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal, as well as Malawi, Mozambique, Tanzania and Zambia.
A small, variable succulent native to South Africa’s Western Cape Province. It usually has sharp triangular leaves with channels, keels and faint striped bands of spots, and it can form dense clumps.

A corm-forming flowering plant, Biarum tenuifolium has six generally recognised subspecies distributed from Portugal and Spain through the central Mediterranean to Turkey and Crete. Two Iberian subspecies are associated respectively with heavy terra rossa and loose sandy soils.

A creeping perennial herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Biarum mendax is restricted to the southwest and, in Portugal, to inland Alentejo. It grows on basic, non-calcareous soils along road embankments and traditional rain-fed olive groves. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment, based on work in 2016–2019, classified it as Endangered amid continuing population and habitat decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Biarum mendax
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Flowering plant native to the rainforest of southern Brazil. It forms rosettes of strap-shaped leaves with red tips and red inner leaves, producing blue flowers with red or purple bracts in summer.

A charophyte green alga native to Europe and now widespread worldwide, fragile stonewort inhabits fresh and brackish water. Its originally documented form has short end segments and a black, finely textured fossa wall.

A cactus-like shrub native to North Africa, Euphorbia officinarum has upright, branched stems with five to ten angles, strong paired spines and leaves reduced to tiny bumps. Its flowers range from yellow to red-purple depending on the subspecies.

Flowering plant indigenous to South Africa, where it occurs sparingly around Uitenhage, Patensie and north of Port Elizabeth. It typically lacks leaf blades, and its flower clusters remain shorter than its leaves.
A tropical ground-cover plant native to Brazil. Its pale-green oval leaves have alternating fishbone-like stripes and tend to close at night.

Ground-dwelling orchid native to the western Mediterranean. During the 2016–2019 mainland Portugal assessment, only 72 mature plants were counted across two separated woodland populations, leading to an Endangered assessment.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Dactylorhiza insularis
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Perennial herb native to Australian coastal areas and saline flats. It may lie flat or grow upright, and bears green flowers during October and November in its native range.

A medium-sized fern native to the Americas, it typically grows on dry, rocky slopes. Its clustered fronds do not unfurl as fiddleheads, and its unusually little-divided leaflets have golden hairs above and dense white-to-rusty hairs below.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, mountain parsley has a wider European distribution but in Portugal occurs only in the highlands of northeastern Trás-os-Montes, along woodland edges and in clearings. In the 2016–2019 mainland Portugal assessment, it was considered Vulnerable, with only three known locations and a small occupied area, although its national population was then regarded as stable.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Peucedanum oreoselinum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to Bermuda, Bermudiana has strap-like green to grey-green leaves. In spring it bears groups of purple-blue flowers with yellow centres, followed by dark pods containing many small black seeds.

A liverwort common across the Northern Hemisphere and widely distributed in Canada. It has a strongly scented, dark green leathery surface with purplish margins, though the name belongs to a complex containing several visually indistinguishable species.
A moss native to Eurasia and North America.
An annual climbing herb, Cuscuta monogyna has simple, broad leaves.
A flowering plant endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago.
A flowering perennial native to Albania, Bulgaria, Greece and Yugoslavia, this hellebore has basal, palm-shaped green leaves and leafless flower stalks. Its flowers are green to yellow-green.
A bulb-growing plant native from southern Europe to northern Iraq. It produces bluish-purple flowers in March and April on tall flowering stalks.

A summer-growing bulbous plant native to southern Africa from Zimbabwe through Malawi to South Africa’s Limpopo Province. Its sweetly scented white flowers turn green later and form a loose spike topped by a tuft of short pointed bracts.

A grapevine native to Asia, the Amur grape withstands severe frost but not drought. Its berries range from very acidic to sweet, and ripe fruit can be eaten raw or made into wine, juice, jellies and jams; the leaves are used in salad.
stories.edibilityNote: Ripe grapes are eaten raw; unripe fruit is acidic and bitter. Fruit is made into wine, juice, jellies and jams; leaves are used in salad.

stories.summary: Flowering plant native to central Europe and the Mediterranean region, it has a flattened oval bulb surrounded by many tiny bulbs. Its green leaves bear a central white stripe, while flat-topped clusters of white flowers have green-striped petal backs.

A flowering plant endemic to the northern half of the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in Portugal only on the upper Montesinho plateau. Recorded there once in 1989 and rediscovered in 2018, it grows in a mosaic of mountain grassland and hay meadows.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Viola bubanii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A rhizomatous perennial flowering herb endemic to Portugal, especially its central-western districts. Its flowers have pinkish-flesh petals with a purple-pink upper lip, while the mature seed capsules are very hard.
A flowering plant of the pea family found primarily in the western Mediterranean basin, Calvary clover lives in partnership with a bacterium capable of fixing nitrogen.

Climbing asparagus native from Africa through southern Asia to northern Australia. It has shiny, needle-like green branches and both fibrous and tuberous roots. Minute white flowers appear in July, followed by blackish-purple berries in September.
Orchid native to Assam in India, Yunnan in China, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam. Known as Low’s boat orchid, it has received the Royal Horticultural Society’s Award of Garden Merit.

A boat orchid native to Assam, the Himalaya, south-central China, Myanmar, Nepal, Tibet and Vietnam, it grows on trees or rocks and shaded cliffs. Its yellowish-green flowers have brown to reddish-brown lengthwise stripes, with similar red or brown markings on the yellowish lip.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A deciduous shrub native to Taiwan and the Philippines.

A leguminous shrub native to the Ibero-Maghrebi region, occurring in Spain, Algeria and Morocco. It branches heavily from the base and bears terminal clusters of yellow flowers followed by flattened, silvery hairy pods.

A flowering plant endemic to central and southern parts of the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal only around Monchique and the southwestern Alentejo hills, on rocky slopes and woodland edges. The Portuguese population was assessed as Vulnerable, with fewer than 1,000 mature plants estimated and continuing habitat decline inferred.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Silene mellifera
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A viburnum species endemic to the Azores, the Azorean laurustinus grows mainly on slopes in natural forests, generally above 200 metres. It occurs on eight of the archipelago’s nine islands.
An epiphytic bromeliad native to Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina, Queen's-tears is often grown as an ornamental.
A short-lived perennial native to Eurasia. It has grey, felted leaves and bright magenta flowers produced successively around July, and readily self-seeds in favourable places.
A moss of unstated native origin, found in Europe and Asia. It forms loose, regularly feathered mats on wet, lime-free rock beside mountain streams and waterfalls, and rarely produces spore capsules.

A conspicuous moss found chiefly in the north Atlantic, golden-head moss has strongholds in western Britain, Ireland and western Norway. It occurs most often in upland acidic grassland, especially near wet flushes.

A thyme-moss found in old-growth boreal forests across North America, Europe and Asia. It forms low lawns in moist but not wet ground, with leaves that curl strongly when dry and spread flat when moist.

An evergreen flowering shrub or tree native to Madeira and the Canary Islands. It has narrow leaves and brown, honey-scented spring flowers; cut stems release milky sap that can irritate skin and seriously harm the eyes.
A perennial herb whose native origin is not stated. It is self-supporting and has simple, broad leaves.

A small annual aquatic plant that grows in shallow salty places which dry out in summer, such as salt pans. Once considered extinct in Portugal after no observations since 1853, it was rediscovered in the Mondego estuary and Ria Formosa.

A bulbous plant occurring in mainland Portugal, it grows in traditional dry-farmed olive groves and fallow fields on basic soils. In assessments conducted from 2016 to 2019, it was known there from only two small population clusters near Beja and Beringel and assessed as Critically Endangered, with agricultural intensification the gravest threat.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Bellevalia trifoliata
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant, its acuminata and aestiva subspecies are native to mainland Portugal.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, it inhabits temporarily waterlogged coastal sands along the Atlantic coast of northwestern Iberia and southern France. Portugal's 2020 mainland Red List assessed it as Endangered after its northern coastal range had contracted in recent decades.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Centaurium chloodes
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Madeira and the Azorean islands of Terceira, Pico, Faial, São Miguel and Santa Maria, it also occurs from southern and western Europe to southwestern Asia. It favours uncultivated ground and flowers from April to July.
A flowering plant represented in continental Portugal by subsp. peixotoanum, which is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Seseli montanum belongs to the carrot family.
Flowering plant endemic to Romania’s Piatra Craiului Mountains. It grows on scree, prefers alkaline substrates and is a symbol of the surrounding massif and national park.
Herbaceous perennial native to France and Spain.

Flowering plant represented in mainland Portugal by three listed subspecies endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. Subspecies marizii is described as endemic to mainland Portugal and is protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A stonewort native to Europe and northern North America. It chiefly inhabits brackish water but also occurs in a few inland lakes.

Green alga with no stated native origin, widespread across much of Europe, Asia, Africa, North America, and Australia. It is often greyish-green and crusted with calcium carbonate, and can form extensive underwater meadows that shelter aquatic animals.

A small to medium alga with a cosmopolitan distribution. It is transparent, richly branched and lacks a cortex, or outer layer; it was the first member of its class to have its entire nuclear genome sequenced and published.
A stonewort with a cosmopolitan distribution.
Stonewort with a cosmopolitan distribution. It is a distinct species in the family Characeae.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, particularly Portugal and Galicia. It grows in shrubland clearings on acidic, usually schist-based soils and was assessed as Vulnerable in mainland Portugal after declines in habitat, locations and population.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Succisa pinnatifida
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Flowering plant of Mediterranean distribution, native in mainland Portugal, where it was recorded only once in Peneda-Gerês in 1945. It is assessed as regionally extinct in Portugal after more than 70 years without another record and unsuccessful searches nearby.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Geranium lanuginosum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An aquatic annual or perennial herb native to Europe, Asia and North America. It has segmented leaves and white, five-petalled flowers with yellow centres, and can photosynthesise underwater.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed along the European and Asian shores of the Mediterranean. In Portugal it inhabited moist coastal meadows, but its last known site was destroyed in the 1990s; it is critically endangered and possibly regionally extinct, though suitable habitat remains insufficiently surveyed.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Linum maritimum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Plant with no stated native origin, found throughout the Mediterranean Basin. It forms a partnership with the nitrogen-fixing bacterium Sinorhizobium medicae.

A shrub confined to northern Mediterranean coastal Spain and southern France, extending into Italy, and also found in the western Rif, Algeria and Ibiza. Its black, blackberry-like fruit is the largest in its genus but is toxic, and the leaves were traditionally collected for tanning and dyeing.
stories.edibilityNote: The blackberry-like black fruit is toxic; both leaves and fruits contain a convulsant compound.

stories.summary: A large shrub or small tree from China, tea-oil camellia has dark green evergreen leaves and fragrant white flowers in mid to late fall. Its seeds can be pressed for a sweetish oil used for seasoning and cooking.
stories.edibilityNote: The seeds are pressed to produce tea seed oil, used as a seasoning and cooking oil.

stories.summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, small coriander grows in cereal fields, fallows and beneath rain-fed olive groves on basic soils. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment classified it as Vulnerable, with only three subpopulations then known nationally.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Bifora testiculata
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It is an upright or ascending, hairless clover with large flower heads surrounded by prominent bracts, found in grassland, fields and hedges in Estremadura, Alentejo and Algarve.

A perennial legume of southern Europe's mountain regions, alpine bird's-foot trefoil sprawls across grassland or rocky surfaces. Its pea-shaped flowers may be yellow, orange or reddish and bloom from May to August.
A grass native to Eurasia, bristle bent forms dense tufts with hairlike leaves. Its yellow-green flower spikelets bear bristles, and it has neither rhizomes nor stolons.

A red alga recorded from Ireland, western Great Britain, Portugal and the Mediterranean. Its short, flat fronds rise from a creeping, branched holdfast and branch once or twice, with cylindrical growths at their tips.
A biennial herb of unstated native origin, it has a self-supporting form and simple, broad leaves.

An autumn-flowering plant found from Portugal and Morocco east to Turkey and the Caucasus, as well as in Great Britain. Though classified as one species, it is a complex of outwardly indistinguishable forms with different chromosome complements.

A perennial bunch grass native to Eurasia, China and India, rough reedgrass grows in tufts with short underground stems. It has upright stems, rough narrow leaves and open, lance-shaped flower clusters.

Perennial bulb-forming herb occurring in the northeastern Mediterranean, with no explicitly stated native origin. It bears daughter bulbs and flowers from March to April in habitats including scrub, fallow ground and olive groves.

A perennial plant from Syria, Lebanon, the Palestine region, the eastern Mediterranean and southern Europe. It has a ground-hugging rosette of deeply divided leaves, bright pink flowers nearly year-round and long-beaked fruits.

Herbaceous perennial flowering plant native to the eastern Mediterranean. It has wine-red flowers with white, red-spotted lower lips and evergreen, lightly hairy leaves that produce no scent when crushed.
stories.edibilityNote: In Jordanian and Palestinian cuisine, the leaves are stuffed with meat and rice and cooked with lamb riblets.

stories.summary: A perennial sedge native to tropical parts of the Americas, shortleaf spikesedge has spreading underground stems and several upright shoots. It produces tiny clusters of spikelets and is sometimes a weed in wet cultivated ground and irrigation ditches.
A banyan fig found from South and southern China through Indo-China and Peninsular Malaysia to parts of Malesia, including Java, the Lesser Sunda Islands, Sulawesi and Maluku.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
An evergreen tree native to South Africa.

A flowering plant native to Tunisia, Sardinia, Corsica, Sicily, Italy, Albania, Greece, the eastern Aegean Islands, Crete, Cyprus and Turkey, Malva cretica has been introduced to France. A possible subspecies may occur in Spain.
A flowering plant native to the shores of the western and central Mediterranean, it is known as tree mallow or sea mallow.
Annual herb native to central Europe, the Mediterranean and the Caucasus. It grows upright without support and has simple, broad leaves.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A tree native to Guangdong and Hainan in China, Taiwan and Vietnam. Its leaves are used in Taiwanese folk medicine as an expectorant.
A flowering plant native to continental Portugal.
Flowering plant recorded as introduced in continental Portugal.
An annual herb, Medicago doliata is self-supporting and has broad, compound leaves.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and introduced to the Madeira Archipelago.

Flowering plant of unspecified native origin, introduced in parts of mainland Portugal. It grows semi-prostrate to upright but tends to flatten when grazed. It flowers from May to June, producing blooms attractive to bees.

A perennial flowering herb native to mainland Portugal, it grows prostrate without rooting along its stems. It has deeply pink flowers and large pink fruiting heads, and occurs in scrub, woods and shady places.

A poisonous evergreen shrub native to Monos Island, Trinidad and Tobago, Venezuela and its Antilles, Guyana, Brazil, and northwest Argentina. It is commonly cultivated as an ornamental and used in ayahuasca and other potions.
Orchid native to the Mediterranean region from Portugal and Morocco east to Syria.

Flowering plant native to northwestern Africa, nearly all of Europe, the Caucasus, the Middle East and Central Asia. It resembles the dog rose but has downier leaves, especially on their undersides; its cultivar ‘Laxa’ is widely used in Europe as garden-rose rootstock.

Wild onion native to Spain, France, Italy, Morocco and Tunisia. It bears numerous small white or pink flowers and an egg-shaped bulb, often surrounded by bulblets; its strongly aromatic bulbs and foliage are cultivated for food.
stories.edibilityNote: The potently aromatic bulbs and foliage are widely cultivated for eating.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Rumex thyrsoides is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A flowering plant native to the Mediterranean region. It has edible leaves, bluish-violet flower heads and fleshy taproots.
stories.edibilityNote: The leaves are edible by humans.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

An annual herb native to the Mediterranean, western Europe, the Middle East as far as Iran, and North Africa, slender salsify grows in dry disturbed ground, vineyards, roadsides and meadows. Its pink-to-violet flower heads rise on hollow stalks swollen beneath them, and it produces two differently formed kinds of seed-bearing fruit.

A perennial herb found mainly in southern and central Europe, three-leaved anemone grows in hardwood forests and rocky places. It has three-part, toothed leaves and usually single white flowers, though pale pink or blue forms occur. Its shallow whitish underground stems can produce dense colonies.

A perennial, winter-deciduous caper found in parts of Spain, North Africa, the Middle East, Turkey and Crete. Its upright branches resprout in spring and can form a thick trunk, and its elongated fruit contains yellow pulp.

Woolly annual plant native to the Mediterranean region. It produces early flower heads beneath its basal leaf rosette and later yellow heads on upright stems. Its five seed types differ in size, position, dispersal and whether germination is immediate or delayed.
Annual herb with simple, broad leaves; its native origin is not provided in the supplied information.

An annual herb native from the Canary Islands across the Mediterranean region and neighboring areas to Iran, Cretanweed has variably hairy or bristly growth. Most leaves cluster around the base and resemble dandelion leaves, while its stalks carry single yellow flower heads or flat-topped groups of heads.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, downy restharrow belongs to the pea family.
An annual grass with a self-supporting growth form and simple, broad leaves.
A flowering plant whose subspecies australis is native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Union legislation.
Flowering plant whose subspecies Teucrium capitatum subsp. capitatum is recorded as native to mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.

Annual herb with a wide circum-Mediterranean distribution; no explicitly native origin is stated. It has simple broad leaves, and in mainland Portugal it occurs only in the Algarve on stabilized dunes and consolidated coastal sands.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Thesium humile
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal and Madeira, it is widespread around the Mediterranean. In mainland Portugal it is confined to limestone coastal cliffs in the far southwest, where only six locations were identified and its habitat was declining.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Triplachne nitens
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An annual herb with no native origin supplied, Valantia hispida is a very small, self-supporting plant. It has simple, broad leaves.

Perennial mint-family herb of unstated native origin, lesser calamint commonly grows around the Mediterranean, North Africa and parts of Central Asia. Its fragrant, grey-green leaves resemble oregano and smell of pennyroyal, while its flowers are lavender-pink. It is used as a culinary herb in Italian and Corsican cooking, including Roman-style artichokes and a southern Italian goat cheese.
stories.edibilityNote: Used as a culinary herb in Italian and Corsican food, including Roman-style artichokes and southern Italian goat cheese.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to Spain, including the Balearic Islands, France, including Corsica, and Italy, it has traditionally been used to treat haemorrhoids.

Orchid endemic to Portugal and western Spain. In mainland Portugal it occurs very sparsely in moist meadows on sandy or siliceous soils and was assessed as Endangered following habitat and population declines.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Serapias perez-chiscanoi
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An orchid occurring in Laos and on Java, Bali, Lombok and Sumbawa.
An epiphytic orchid from the cool, moist eastern Himalayas and Vietnam, it blooms around the spring snowmelt. Its fragrant flowers have snow-white petals and a yellow-marked lip.
An orchid endemic to Vietnam.
A flowering plant native to southeastern Brazil, from Espírito Santo to Rio Grande do Sul.
An orchid found in Assam, southern China and parts of Myanmar. Its populations face pressure from habitat degradation and collection for the plant trade.

An orchid native to the Malay Peninsula, Thailand, Myanmar and Borneo at low elevations. Its few very large, hanging flowers are pale yellow to cream with red stripes or spots, and have exceptionally long side sepals.

An orchid native to the Himalayas and the mountains of northern Indochina, Dendrobium thyrsiflorum has two recognized varieties. The variety minutiflorum is recorded from Laos, while the typical variety covers most of the species’ range.

Perennial climbing ivy native from Afghanistan through the Himalayas and southern China to mainland Southeast Asia. It has glossy evergreen leaves and orange-to-red fruits, and all parts are poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are poisonous; ingestion can cause gastrointestinal and nervous-system disturbances.

stories.summary: An annual herb of unstated native origin, it has broad compound leaves and a self-supporting form. It produces chemicals that suppress the growth of nearby plants.

A freshwater microscopic green alga with a cosmopolitan distribution, Pseudopediastrum boryanum occurs most commonly in nutrient-rich waters, but also in brackish water and some mountain water bodies. Its colonies form flat, star-like discs, while its decay-resistant cell walls are often preserved in lake sediments.

Perennial flowering herb native to Madeira and the Salvage Islands. It usually forms dense mats, has leaves divided into five leaflets, and bears flowers that generally open orange before turning reddish-brown after fertilization.
Annual flowering plant native to southwestern Europe and North Africa. It bears dense, spherical clusters of pale blue flowers, followed by showy fruits with striped, fan-like papery bracts.
A flowering plant native to a range extending from Europe to the Russian Far East and Iran.
Flowering plant native from Europe to China and Pakistan.

A perennial flowering plant indigenous to southeastern Africa. Though commonly called a fern, it is an asparagus with fine, bushy stems and needle-like leaves; its small red fruits turn black as they mature.
stories.edibilityNote: It is reported to have little or no nutritional value to people, but its edibility is not explicitly established.

stories.summary: A dense deciduous shrub native to the Korean Peninsula and nearby parts of Northeast China, Japan and the Russian Far East. Its late-spring to early-summer flowers are white to pink, often with small red spots on the upper petals. Azaleas are poisonous and cannot be eaten.
stories.edibilityNote: Azaleas are described as poisonous and not edible.

stories.summary: Self-supporting annual herb with compound broad leaves. It can grow to about 24 centimetres tall.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. In the 2020 Portuguese assessment, its occurrence on Arrábida's sea cliffs was the only mainland European record; only five individuals were then known, and it was assessed as Endangered.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Volutaria crupinoides
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A perennial grass whose native origin is not stated. It is self-supporting and has simple, broad leaves.
Flowering plant with two recorded forms, Valerianella coronata f. coronata and f. pumila, both native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal.

A small annual flowering herb native to mainland Portugal, it grows in scrub clearings and damp grassland on stony limestone ground. There, it is known only from scattered sites in the Algarve’s Barrocal and is assessed as Vulnerable.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Crucianella latifolia
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A tree found from Costa Rica to Bolivia, it has aromatic glands on its leaves and pleasantly scented wax granules on its fruits. The fruit wax is used for candles, varnishes and polishes.
A flowering plant native to mainland China, where its fertile form has particular cultural significance.
A tall, erect herb widespread across most of Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. It bears branching clusters of small white flowers.
A bulbous flowering plant native to Iran, Turkey and Turkmenistan. It produces large, showy clusters of silvery-pink, star-shaped flowers in early summer, followed by attractive fruiting clusters.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant, Herniaria scabrida has listed varieties found in mainland Portugal and described as native only to the Iberian Peninsula.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It is present there but is not protected under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, including mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant native to continental Portugal.

Annual herb found in pinewoods and heathlands of the western and northwestern Iberian Peninsula. It has spoon-shaped, serrated basal leaves and yellow, sunflower-like flower heads from April to August.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.
A perennial grass native to Portugal, Spain and Morocco. It has linear blue-green leaves and flowers arranged in branching clusters.
A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.
A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Micropyrum patens belongs to the grass family.
Flowering member of the mint family endemic to central and northern Portugal. It grows on granite-based ground beside paths and roads, on damp slopes and pastures, and along cultivated field edges.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Echinospartum ibericum is recorded in mainland Portugal’s Serra da Estrela.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Genista hystrix occurs in mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Armeria transmontana occurs in mainland Portugal. It is not protected by Portuguese or European Union legislation.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal and belongs to the rose family.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it is recorded from mainland Portugal.
Small shrub native to Haiti and the Dominican Republic. It has large leaves often tinted red or maroon beneath, and long, drooping tubular flowers in red-orange or red-purple with protruding stamens.

A long-lived perennial herb native to continental Eurasian cliffs and slopes, especially on limestone, white swallow-wort has upright stems with white five-petalled flowers. Its fruits contain many seeds topped with tufts of white hairs. The plant is poisonous.
stories.edibilityNote: The plant is described as poisonous; no qualified edible use is documented.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Vincetoxicum hirundinaria
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Evergreen flowering shrub or tree native to New Caledonia. Its toothed leaves have several thin leaflets, changing from coppery red to dark green, while pale green autumn flowers are followed by black fruit.
A small tree or multi-stemmed mallee endemic to Western Australia. It has smooth, variously coloured bark that sheds in ribbons and lemon-yellow flowers appearing from late winter to late spring.

Erect herb with no explicitly stated native origin, widespread across most of Europe and extending into Morocco, the Caucasus and southwestern Asia. It has almost round leaves in whorls of four and green fruits covered with long hooked hairs.

An evergreen flowering shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States and Mexico, Texas mountain laurel bears intensely fragrant purple flowers that smell like grape soda. Its pods contain orange or red seeds that are extremely toxic if swallowed.
stories.edibilityNote: The seeds are extremely toxic; consuming a single seed can kill an adult.

stories.summary: An orchid found from the Florida Everglades through the Caribbean, Mexico and Central America to northern Brazil.

An annual or biennial flowering herb native to western Europe, North Africa and the Mediterranean Basin, Cretan mallow has hairy stems, lobed leaves and small pink or light-purple flowers. Its leaf blades track the sun during the day and turn to face sunrise.
An orchid herb native to coastal and Andean Ecuador and surrounding countries, it ranges from Costa Rica to Ecuador.

A short-lived evergreen perennial native to South Africa, Bacopa is found predominantly along the country’s southern coast. It grows as an annual in colder climates and requires full sun to flower profusely.

A perennial flowering plant native to the Rocky Mountains of the western United States, blue columbine grows from foothills to above the timberline. Its large, scented flowers usually combine white or cream petals with blue sepals and have five long, nearly straight spurs. Bumblebees and hawkmoths are its main pollinators.

Herbaceous perennial native to subtropical Sichuan in southern China. Its trunklike false stems support a crown of large green leaves, while its yellow-green fruits are inedible, with sparse white pulp and many black seeds.
stories.edibilityNote: The yellow-green fruits are inedible, containing little white pulp and many black seeds.

stories.summary: Flowering tree native to China, the Korean Peninsula, Japan and the Russian Far East. It is used as a street tree within its native range but is susceptible to damage from late frosts.

A shrub or small-to-medium tree native to southern Africa, from southern Angola east to Mozambique and south to South Africa. It is readily recognised by its exceptionally long paired white thorns and coffee-coloured bark.
stories.edibilityNote: Gum from cracks in the bark was used to make sweets and formerly had economic importance as Cape Gum.

stories.summary: Herbaceous perennial or subshrub native to the Atlantic coasts of northern Europe. It has strongly aromatic, pale grey-green foliage covered in dense white cottony hairs and grows mainly in dry coastal places with saline soils.

Flowering plant endemic to South Africa and recorded in the Hottentots Holland Nature Reserve. It has finely divided leaves and white-to-pink flowers that appear from July to October in its native range, and it is grown for cut flowers and as an ornamental.

A shrub or medium-sized tree native to parts of eastern and central Africa, the African milkbush has fleshy young stems and green leaves that may be reddish underneath. Wounds release poisonous white latex, while cultivated forms can have purple-red foliage.
Annual flowering plant whose native origin is not supplied. The Zuni grind its seeds with cornmeal, form the mixture into cakes and steam them for food.
stories.edibilityNote: The Zuni traditionally grind the seeds with cornmeal, make them into cakes and steam them.

stories.summary: A herbaceous perennial typical of most of the Alps and Italy’s Apennines, it grows in meadows, uncultivated fields and mountain pastures. Its basal leaves have a greyish waxy coating, and its white funnel-shaped flowers appear from late April through June.
A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and recorded from mainland Portugal.

A woody-stemmed Mediterranean herb found mainly in coastal habitats, though occasionally inland on sandy ground and road cuttings. It has numerous dense, narrow, awl-shaped leaves, while its flowers form relatively loose spikes in spring and summer.

Bulbous perennial endemic to Morocco and Portugal, although Moroccan plants have often been confused with a distinct species. This dwarf bluebell has long, narrow leaves and blue, violet or white bell- or star-shaped flowers in spring. It grows in damp, often sandy open ground near sea level.
A tulip native to Central Asia and Iran. It has large, single bowl-shaped flowers in red, yellow or white and distinctive green leaves patterned with purple-maroon spots and stripes.

Rhizomatous perennial iris native to western China. Its glossy leaves grow atop bamboo-like stems, and its white to pale blue flowers have orange-yellow crests and purple dots. Most parts, particularly the rhizomes and leaves, are poisonous if swallowed and may cause stomach pain and vomiting.
stories.edibilityNote: Most parts are poisonous; ingested rhizomes and leaves may cause stomach pain and vomiting.

stories.summary: A flowering plant from northern Myanmar, Yunnan in China, South Korea and northern Kyushu in Japan, the Korean azalea has a notably disjunct distribution. It is recommended for hedges and has above-average resistance to the root rot that often affects azaleas.
A bromeliad endemic to the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil. Several cultivars are grown as ornamental plants.
An ornamental plant endemic to eastern Brazil, where it is known from Espírito Santo and Rio de Janeiro states. It is widely cultivated.
An evergreen dwarf shrub native to southern Spain, woolly lavender has striking silver, woolly leaves and deep violet-purple flower spikes with a familiar lavender scent.

A flowering shrub native to southern Madeira and Lanzarote in the Canary Islands. Its deeply divided leaves are covered in fine white hairs, giving it a downy appearance, and deep violet flower spikes bloom from late spring into summer.
A small herb whose native origin is not explicitly specified, found across parts of Asia including the eastern Himalayas. It grows in moist, shaded places, often beside streams.

A flowering plant endemic to the Azores, restricted to Corvo and Flores. It inhabits very humid rocky slopes, waterfall surroundings and lake margins, and was rediscovered in 1999 after going unobserved since 1938.
Valentine's sunflower is a plant native to Europe, with some occurrences in Morocco and Algeria. Most are found in Spain.
A flowering plant endemic to central and northern Portugal, it grows along woodland and hedge edges on ultrabasic, schist or limestone soils.
Flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and belonging to the daisy family.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed across the western Mediterranean. In Portugal it occurs only sporadically in Trás-os-Montes, on rocky outcrops and in holm-oak clearings. Portugal’s 2020 Red List assessed it as Vulnerable, with fewer than 1,000 mature plants estimated nationally.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Saxifraga dichotoma
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Flowering plant whose subspecies carpetana is native to mainland Portugal.
Flowering plant whose subspecies obovata is native to mainland Portugal.

Rock-growing bromeliad endemic to Brazil. This giant grows on rocky slopes in Rio de Janeiro’s Serra dos Órgãos and can take up to 40 years to produce its imposing red flower cluster. Its leaf tank can hold substantial rainwater.

An arable flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Linaria hirta occurs exclusively in extensive rain-fed farmland such as traditional olive groves, cereal fields and fallows. In mainland Portugal it was assessed as Vulnerable, with agricultural intensification identified as its main threat.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Linaria hirta
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant whose native origin is not stated, it occurs in mainland Portugal as an introduced species.

A plant endemic to Kenya, tiger-tooth aloe is restricted to a small rocky mountainous area in the southwest near Tanzania. It is extremely rare in the wild but common in cultivation. Short, straight triangular leaves grow densely along its stems, and it has twice the usual chromosome set reported for many aloes.

A biennial herb of unstated native origin, found in the western Mediterranean from southern Italy and Sicily through the Iberian Peninsula to North Africa. It has a persistent grey-white or yellow-green woolly covering and yellow flowers whose purple basal marks form a ring around the throat.

A short-lived perennial herb endemic to the Azores, it occurs on Pico, São Jorge and Terceira and is presumed extinct on Faial. It has large, showy white flowers tinged purple or lilac, with yellow markings. As a root hemiparasite, it probably exploits neighbouring plants’ roots.

A herbaceous plant endemic to the western islands of the Azores, it is protected under the Bern Convention and Habitats Directive. It is closely related to Euphrasia grandiflora, which is endemic to the archipelago’s central islands.
Flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal. It is not protected under Portuguese or European legislation.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira.
A flowering plant present in Portugal; its subsp. lobelioides is native and endemic to Macaronesia and occurs in Madeira.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal. It is protected under Portuguese or European legislation, including Annexes II and IV of the Habitats Directive.
A flowering plant whose variety sabularia is endemic to mainland Portugal. That variety is protected under Portuguese or European legislation.
A daisy-family flowering plant of unstated native origin; its subspecies Glossopappus macrotus subsp. chrysanthemoides is native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant in the daisy family endemic to mainland Portugal.
A perennial herb endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and northwest Africa. Its rose-purple flower heads rise above variable leaves whose veins are covered on both sides with distinctive white wool.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Klasea pinnatifida
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An annual herb native to Europe and parts of Asia and northern Africa. Its upright stem is often red or red-streaked, while its toothed leaves have smooth upper surfaces and powdery undersides. Powdery clusters of spherical buds remain closed as the fruit develops.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds are edible; shoots, stalks and leaves can be eaten as greens, historically used like spinach.

stories.summary: Plant species in the poppy family; its native origin is not supplied.

An annual herb native to North Africa and western Mediterranean Europe. Its flowers are white to pale pink, with dark purple tips only on the inner petals; it has become invasive in parts of South America where introduced.
Perennial subshrub native to the Canary Islands and Madeira, it belongs to the nettle family and grows in subtropical regions. It has also been introduced to the Azores.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.

Mediterranean flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. In the western Algarve it inhabits rock fissures, scree and limestone coastal cliffs. A 2020 mainland assessment classified Portugal's declining population as Critically Endangered, with fewer than 250 mature plants concentrated in one subpopulation.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Succowia balearica
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and introduced to the Azores and Madeira. It is not protected under Portuguese or European Union legislation.
A flowering plant whose subspecies Diplotaxis virgata subsp. virgata is endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and occurs in mainland Portugal.

An annual herb in the mustard family, it forms a basal leaf rosette and flowering stems that may have leaves or be leafless. In western Europe it blooms from June through October, while elsewhere in its range flowering may extend for up to eight months.
A flowering plant in the cabbage family with several varieties native to mainland Portugal, including laevigata, valentina and variegata.
An annual, self-supporting herb, Silene nocturna has simple broad leaves and remains under about forty centimetres tall.

A flowering plant in the carnation family, native in countries from the Mediterranean to northern Somalia and Pakistan. It is listed as invasive in Australia and France, occurring particularly in drier parts of southeastern Australia.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and Madeira.
Annual herb of unstated native origin. It supports itself and has broad compound leaves and dry fruit.

Tillandsia species native to Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina. Its recognised varieties and subspecies have more restricted ranges within Bolivia and Argentina, while the typical subspecies occupies most of the species’ range.

An annual legume whose wild forms are native to Anatolia, northern Iraq and the Anti-Lebanon Mountains of Syria and Lebanon. Its split grain resembles red lentils, but the bitter seeds require leaching through several changes of boiling water before human consumption; historically, they were eaten mainly by poor people or during famine.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds require repeated changes of boiling water to remove bitterness; historically they were eaten mainly by poor people or during famine.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A bedstraw species native to the Mediterranean Basin from Portugal and Morocco east to Turkey and Palestine, it is distinguished by numerous wart-like bumps on its mature fruit.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A tiny annual herb in the daisy family, growing to about five centimetres tall.

An annual herb found in southern Europe, northwest Africa, the Caucasus and the Middle East, edible star-hawkbit typically grows in Mediterranean scrub and forest. Its flowers are yellow and may host the fungus Puccinia rhagadioli.

An annual herb found in the northeastern Mediterranean and the Middle East, from Albania and Greece to Iraq and Iran. It has deeply divided leaves, a leafy stem that becomes nearly hairless above, and spindle-shaped, unwinged fruits.

An annual flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. There, it occurs only at scattered sites between Cape Espichel and the western Algarve. It grows on coastal cliffs with very thin, usually sandy but sometimes clay soils.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Limonium echioides
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Flowering subshrub native to coastal Mediterranean and Red Sea areas and parts of the Middle East and central Asia. It grows in salty soils and has succulent jointed stems that yellow with age, with stubby bluish-green leaves clasping each joint.

A woody plant native to mainland Portugal, Madeira and the Azores, sea knotgrass is usually prostrate, with thick, twisted stems and lance-shaped leaves. A 1913 Portuguese flora describes it as frequent on coastal sands and present in flower almost all year.
