stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to the south-western Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal only around the Monchique mountains. Portugal's population was estimated at fewer than 350 mature plants and thought to have declined by more than 60% since 2001, with eucalyptus plantations and their management identified as the main pressure.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Senecio lopezii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering grass endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it grows in mainland Portugal only along the southern Algarve coast, in openings and scrub edges on loose sand. During 2016–2019, only three current Portuguese locations were identified, and the species was assessed as Endangered there.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Trisetaria dufourei
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Tree native only to Madeira, including Porto Santo, and the Canary Islands. The distinct La Gomera subspecies is endangered.

A perennial flowering plant native to Mediterranean Europe and North Africa. Its vanilla-scented, pinkish-mauve flowers appear in winter, and deep rhizomes allow it to spread extensively on shady roadside banks.

Tree endemic to south-eastern New South Wales, where it grows in wet, high-rainfall forests on hills and plateaus. It has rough bark low on the trunk but smooth upper bark that often peels in ribbons, plus narrow curved leaves, white January flowers and conical or bell-shaped fruit.

A leafy liverwort distributed across northern parts of the Northern Hemisphere, from Europe and the Arctic to Asia and northern North America. Its green to brown-green shoots form sturdy mats or grow among other mosses, with asymmetrical leaves divided into three very unequal lobes. It occupies moderately shaded sites on rock, soil, tree bases and, rarely, dead wood.

A shrub-forming cactus endemic to Bolivia, it has upright light-green stems branching from the base. Yellowish-white flowers emerge from a long, dense structure of reddish-brown to gray wool and numerous spines.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal.

A small red marine alga with no native origin stated, it is recorded from Ireland, Great Britain, the Channel Islands and France. It forms branched tufts with strongly curled tips and banded-looking, spineless filaments.
A small marine red alga of unstated native origin, found around parts of Europe and eastern North America. It forms highly variable tufts and grows on other algae as well as artificial materials.

Perennial flowering herb native to Western and Central Europe, including the British Isles. It has white flowers with five petals split about halfway, and long, narrow grey-green leaves on roughly four-angled stems.

A small marine red alga found around Ireland, Britain, the Isle of Man, Norway, France and the Mediterranean. Its branches have strongly curled tips and distinctive three-celled spines. It grows on rocks, shells and other algae.

A deciduous willow shrub native to northern North America, tealeaf willow has green leaves with whitish undersides and produces flower clusters before its leaves emerge in spring. Its young spring leaves may be eaten; Inuit people also ate the leaves and shoots raw, dried, or stored in seal oil, and used the leaves for tea and soup.
stories.edibilityNote: Young leaves may be harvested in spring; Inuit people ate leaves and shoots raw, dried, or stored in seal oil, and made tea and soup.

stories.summary: A perennial grass native to Asia and Australia, it forms graceful, spreading clumps. Its narrow green leaves turn golden yellow and then beige, while arching, brush-like flower spikes change from silvery or pinkish white to brown as seeds form.

An orchid endemic to the Philippines, it naturally inhabits moist subtropical or tropical lowland forests. This robust plant sometimes hangs downward and can bear up to 30 strongly fragrant flowers in autumn.
A low-growing perennial herb native to South Africa. Its young leaves are hairy, and its white flowers have a slight pink tinge before turning yellow with age.

A climbing cactus native from Mexico to Honduras. Its scented flowers open at night, and it is widely cultivated as both an ornamental vine and dragon-fruit crop. Its red fruit has white or, less commonly, pink pulp and edible black seeds.
stories.edibilityNote: Cultivated as a dragon-fruit crop; the red fruit contains white or occasionally pink pulp and edible black seeds.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to every Canadian province except British Columbia and nearly all the United States except the Pacific coast states and Nevada.
A flowering shrub native to Jamaica and introduced to Madeira, Réunion and the Society Islands. It produces masses of pink flowers throughout the year.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A scrambling evergreen climber native to Madeira and the Canary Islands, fragrant jasmine is cultivated as a wall shrub.

Epiphytic evergreen perennial endemic to Espírito Santo in eastern Brazil. It forms basal rosettes of strap-shaped leaves and arching clusters of tubular red-and-yellow flowers followed by berries. It does not tolerate freezing temperatures and is often kept as a houseplant in temperate regions.

Succulent shrub native to South Africa. It has brittle branches and blue-green to blue-grey leaves that are flattened sideways and marked by translucent lines. Its usually knife-like leaves distinguish it from the similar Curio talinoides, whose leaves are rounded in cross-section.
Flowering plant native to Cuba and Jamaica. It tolerates shade and is grown as a houseplant or outdoors in warm climates.

An upright flowering tree native to Madeira and the Canary Islands. It grows in shady forests and thickets and has slightly inrolled leaves, elongated pyramidal flower clusters and white bell-shaped flowers.
A mint-family plant native to the western Mediterranean, particularly Spain and Portugal, and also to North Africa.

An annual, occasionally biennial herb native to the western Mediterranean, Albania and Macaronesia. Its solitary flower heads generally hang before flowering, and its brown fruits occur in two markedly different forms.

A large perennial bunch grass native to Africa and Yemen. It can withstand wildfire and drought, and may reproduce by cloning itself through seed. In some regions, including South Texas and Hawai‘i, it is an invasive weed and fire hazard.
An evergreen shrub native to South America, mainly Argentina and Uruguay. Its yellow flowers have conspicuous long crimson stamens, while its seed pods are covered in short red glandular hairs.
stories.edibilityNote: The seeds and green seed pods are toxic and can cause severe vomiting and other abdominal symptoms.

stories.summary: A thorny tree native to parts of Morocco, southwestern Algeria, Mauritania and Western Sahara. Its gnarled trunk supports a wide-spreading crown, while its hard nuts contain oil-rich seeds; the fruit is eaten, and oil from gently roasted seeds is used with bread, couscous and salads.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruit is eaten; oil from gently roasted seeds is traditionally used with bread, couscous and salads.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In Portugal, it occurs only around Serra de Nogueira and Sabugal, along oak-woodland edges and clearings. During mainland Portugal's 2016–2019 assessment, it was classed as Endangered, with about 120 mature plants in four known groups and an inferred continuing decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Nepeta caerulea
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.

A perennial plant native to Tanzania, Malawi and Mozambique, it grows in rocky crevices. Its fleshy, pale green leaves may have reddish markings and purple edges, while its many flowers are pale greenish to lilac with purple veins.
A miniature epiphytic orchid endemic to Ecuador’s coastal provinces. It lacks pseudobulbs and has a fan of red-green leaves, with elongated flower clusters bearing pink buds in winter and spring.
Dwarf succulent native only to South Africa. It has a thick, fleshy body with many green, often curved, spiny branches radiating from the top and leaves that fall off.
A daisy native to western Europe, Algeria, Morocco and Spain. Unlike the similar Bellis sylvestris, its seeds have scales on the pappus.
A perennial shrub native to Brazil's Atlantic Forest region, especially Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais, it grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical habitat.

A perennial sedge endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, associated with low-altitude marshes and peat bogs. In mainland Portugal it is known from only four locations between Minho and Baixo Alentejo and was assessed as Endangered.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Carex durieui
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An annual or short-lived perennial found across tropical and subtropical parts of several continents, it commonly grows in gardens, fields, roadsides and disturbed ground. Its daisy-like flower heads have tiny yellow centres and may have white or cream outer petals; young leaves can be eaten as salad, while fresh or dried leaves are also boiled.
stories.edibilityNote: Young leaves may be eaten as salad; fresh or dried leaves are boiled. Older leaves may taste unpleasant and upset the stomach.

stories.summary: Perennial shrub native to arid and semi-arid parts of the Middle East, North Africa and southern Europe. It is greyish and much-branched, with tiny, scale-like hairy leaves and pinkish, winged flower parts.
A flowering plant native to Central and Southern Europe.
A bulb-forming perennial native to Morocco and Algeria, it smells like garlic or leeks. Its flowers are pollinated by bees and other insects.

A stone plant native to the Cape Provinces of South Africa, the Carmine Fingerfig has violet-purple colouring on the undersides of its petals. It is also a notably successful naturalised stone plant in Malta’s natural habitats.
Flowering plant native to Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and adjoining parts of Brazil. It grows in wet tropical forests and is commercially available as a houseplant.
A flowering plant in the pea family native to mainland Portugal.
Upright Eurasian herb occurring from Portugal to Japan. It has narrow, roughly hairy, stemless leaves and single yellow flower heads at the tops of thin stems.
A fern native to Macaronesia, Mediterranean Europe, North Africa, western Asia and parts of the Sahara.

A plant native from western France to the western Mediterranean. Its flowers are bright yellow above and paler beneath, with a small white-tipped tooth, while its small oval leaves grow in hairy clusters.
A perennial grass of unspecified native origin, sea couch has a self-supporting form and simple, broad leaves. It is invasive in Mont-Saint-Michel Bay, where it has altered the area's ecology.

A perennial cereal grass of the Old World, distributed across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Its pointed grains are shiny black, and the millet can be ground into meal and prepared as porridge.
stories.edibilityNote: The millet grain can be ground into meal and prepared as porridge.

stories.summary: An evergreen flowering plant native to French Guiana, Bolivia and Brazil. It has large, velvety silver-green leaves with prominent veins and clusters of purple five-petalled flowers; older leaves often turn orange before falling.

An evergreen shrub or small ornamental tree native to southeastern Brazil. It has dark green, velvety leaves with prominent lengthwise veins and large royal-purple flowers, with some blooms throughout the year and the greatest abundance from May to January.
A moss of unspecified native origin, Flat Neckera was found in the colon of the Tyrolean Iceman.
A medium-to-large moss found worldwide in moist or wet habitats. It has feather-like branches and is especially common in lowland Great Britain.
Moss native to the Northern Hemisphere, with leaves ranging from yellow to yellow-copper.

A flowering plant endemic to the west coast of mainland Portugal, where it grows on sea cliffs exposed to fog. It was assessed as Vulnerable after southern populations disappeared during the past century, with invasive plants and cliff erosion contributing to continuing habitat decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Limonium plurisquamatum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A moss of unspecified native origin, recorded across Europe, parts of Asia, North Africa, North America, the Canary Islands and Madeira. It forms loose yellow-green to dark-green cushions, usually on trees, and its leaves draw loosely against the stem when dry.
A flowering plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula, Arabis stenocarpa belongs to the cabbage family and occurs in mainland Portugal.

A moss of the Northern Hemisphere, marsh forklet moss grows in cold springs, wet fens, and along streams and ditches. It forms soft yellow-green to green mats that break apart easily, with leaves bent distinctively backwards.
Flowering plant native to the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil.

A perennial herb native to Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama. Its dark green, velvety leaves carry a light green saw-toothed band along the central vein, while its bracts change from white to deep purple over time.
A moss whose native origin is not stated. It has a wide-ranging distribution across parts of the Americas, Europe and Asia, with a particularly strong presence in the eastern United States.

A small marine red alga of unspecified native origin, recorded around parts of Atlantic Europe and nearby islands. Its cylindrical branches appear banded, curl strongly inward at their tips and bear single-celled spines.

A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. In mainland Portugal it is recorded only near Vimioso, where about 75 mature plants occur in two groups on disturbed limestone soils, and it is assessed as Endangered.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Reseda barrelieri
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Annual herb native to the Mediterranean Basin in Europe and North Africa, and to western and central Asia and Pakistan. It has hairy, glandular, branching green or purplish stems, with solitary pink or purplish flowers distinguished by a long, ribbed tubular calyx.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
An orchid known only from Mount Kinabalu in Malaysian Borneo.

A plant native only to the Iberian Peninsula and Canary Islands, it is restricted in Portugal to the northwest. It inhabits shaded, damp ravines beneath deciduous woodland and also pit walls. During the 2016–2019 mainland Portugal assessment, it was declining and considered Endangered, with only four known locations.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Dryopteris guanchica
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. It readily forms hybrids with Tuberaria guttata.
Flowering plant represented in mainland Portugal by two subspecies, both endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.

A bunchgrass native to the Iberian Peninsula and Morocco, giant needle grass has narrow grey-green leaves and may remain evergreen or semi-evergreen depending on climate. Its tall flower spikes emerge silver-lavender in late spring, turn golden in summer and persist tan into winter.

A low-growing, semi-evergreen subshrub native to the Mediterranean Basin from Portugal to Turkey and south to northern Africa, it has fuzzy silver leaves. Its white flowers are veined pinkish-red, followed by reddish-brown seed pods.

A herbaceous perennial with a broadly Mediterranean distribution, prostrate Canary clover has woody stems, five-part hairy leaves and clusters of small white flowers. Its fruits are reddish-brown pods containing one or two seeds.

An evergreen flowering perennial native to the Amazonian basin of northwestern Brazil, it forms clumps of pale seafoam-green leaves edged and streaked with dark green. The leaf undersides are dark reddish-purple, while cultivated varieties may have nearly black, pink, red or white foliage.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal and distributed around the Mediterranean. It inhabits waterlogged clay and muddy soils; during Portugal’s 2016–2019 assessment, its few known locations and continuing national decline led to an Endangered rating.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Triglochin laxiflora
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A perennial shrub or vine native to the Chinese provinces of Sichuan, Yunnan and Guizhou and to western Indochina. It belongs to the legume family and bears orchid-like flowers.
A non-climbing perennial shrub endemic to central mainland Portugal. It grows chiefly in scrub and uncultivated ground, flowering from January to June.

An ornamental plant native to Rio de Janeiro state in southeastern Brazil, Goeppertia louisae has pointed, oval, dark green leaves with silvery light-green bands beside the central vein. The leaf undersides are usually purple, while the flowers are fully white.
An evergreen perennial native to Espírito Santo in eastern Brazil. Its glossy pale-green leaves have dark-green markings and deep-purple undersides, closing at night and opening again at dawn.

Ornamental plant native to Peru, with dark green leaves striped pink and white above when young; the pattern fades to solid green as the plant matures. The leaf undersides remain purple throughout its life.

Flowering plant endemic to Ecuador’s moist lowland and mountain forests. Its glossy leaves have purple undersides and a distinctive pattern of broad light- and dark-green bands; the flower bracts are very hairy.
An evergreen perennial native to southeastern Brazil. Its long elliptical leaves are dark green above and dark red below, with lime-green markings along their central ribs, veins and margins.

Banana relative native to Sichuan, Guizhou and Yunnan in China, and to Vietnam, where it grows high in the mountains. Its erect yellow, flower-like structures resemble a lotus before opening and may last several months.

A perennial herb of Atlantic coastal western Europe, especially Cornwall and the Channel Islands. It grows almost exclusively on dunes and sea cliffs close to the coast, resembling white clover but appearing earlier, growing more compactly and often having opaque blue-green leaves.

Small, stemless, ground-hugging annual herb endemic to the Mediterranean. In Portugal it occurs only beside paths and in scrub clearings in the limestone regions of Lisbon and Arrábida; a 2020 mainland assessment classified it as Vulnerable there.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Crepis pusilla
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A plant species endemic to Brazil.
Subshrub or shrub native to the western and central Mediterranean Basin.
An evergreen shrub native to Portugal, Spain and northern Morocco. It has woolly grey-green leaves and bright yellow spring flowers, sometimes with a dark brown blotch at each petal’s base.

A flowering plant endemic to the central coast of mainland Portugal, it inhabits salt marshes and salty sands. A mainland assessment reported only two known groups in the Tagus estuary and classified it as Critically Endangered.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Limonium daveaui
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal. There it is confined to the Tagus floodplain, mainly on drainage-ditch banks beside farmland, and was assessed as Endangered after surveys conducted from 2016 to 2019.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Galega cirujanoi
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A plant species endemic to Espírito Santo in eastern Brazil.

A small marine red alga of unstated native origin, recorded along the coasts of Great Britain, Ireland and continental Europe. Its finely branched form bears sparse, tiny spines near the tips, which help distinguish it from related species.

A perennial herb native to southern and eastern Africa and parts of South Asia, from India to Myanmar. It is covered in small hairs and bears narrow leaves and pale blue-purple, tubular-looking flowers on tall spikes.

A perennial groundcover found in southern Africa, lobster bush has hairy, succulent grey-green leaves with a strong scent likened to cannabis or skunk. Purple-blue flower spikes appear twice yearly, in late summer and late winter. Fresh leaves are steeped to make a mint-like tea.
stories.edibilityNote: Fresh leaves are steeped to make a tea described as similar to mint tea.

stories.summary: Evergreen shrub native to China’s Hainan Province and Taiwan. It has shiny leaves divided into umbrella-like clusters of leaflets and can grow independently or cling to tree trunks.
stories.edibilityNote: The fruits are inedible to humans.

stories.summary: Flowering bromeliad native to Bahia in eastern Brazil.
A multicellular marine red alga recorded in Ireland.
Flowering plant native to southeastern Brazil, from Espírito Santo to Santa Catarina.

A flowering tree of northeastern Brazil’s caatinga, also found in Bolivia and Paraguay. Its twisted branches bear thorns, while its small yellowish fruits are sweet and used to make jellies and other foods.
stories.edibilityNote: The sweet, yellowish fruits are eaten and used to make jellies and other preparations.

stories.summary: A coastal flowering plant apparently endemic to the Iberian Peninsula. It grows on coastal rocks and in salt marshes flooded at high tide; its current distribution remains uncertain because it may formerly have been confused with similar species.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Limonium maritimum
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: An aromatic biennial or short-lived perennial herb native to Europe, Western Asia and North Africa, ploughman’s-spikenard grows on chalky or limestone-rich ground. Its softly hairy leaves and roots have a faint spicy smell, especially in spring, and its branched stems bear clusters of small yellow flowers in late summer.
A flowering plant native to southern China, Indochina and Japan.
Flowering evergreen shrub native to Brazil. It has dark green, hairy leaves with lengthwise veins and clusters of brilliant purple flowers with black stamens throughout summer and autumn.

A herbaceous flowering bulb native to Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, the pink rain lily bears solitary pale pink to lavender flowers, typically after rain from late summer to early autumn. Its flowers are unusually large, strongly bent and often asymmetrical, and its leaves have a fine greyish waxy coating.
A flowering plant, Gnidia polystachya is recorded in both the Azores and Madeira, where it is introduced.

An evergreen tree native to tropical rainforests and riverside forests of northern and northeastern Australia, New Guinea and Java, it is usually multi-trunked and sometimes grows on other rainforest trees. Its leaves radiate in groups of seven leaflets, while long flower clusters can carry up to 1,000 small red flowers.

A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal, Limonium dodartii occurs there only on rocky greywacke cliffs along the southwest Alentejo coast. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment classified it as Vulnerable, with a very restricted range and population.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Limonium dodartii
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: Large climbing shrub native across a stated range including the Indian subcontinent, China, Malaysia and Myanmar. It has leathery, tapering leaves, greenish-white flowers and rounded brownish-black fruits.

A deciduous tree native across much of Europe and northern Anatolia, it also has isolated populations from northwestern Africa to northwestern Iran. Its fruit is edible but astringent and gritty straight from the tree; after overripening it sweetens, and it is also made into drinks, jam, juice and brandy.
stories.edibilityNote: Fruit is edible; it sweetens after overripening and is used for cider-like drinks, jam, juice and brandy. Ancient Greeks also pickled it.

stories.summary: A deciduous whitebeam tree native to Norway, eastern Sweden, south-western Finland and local areas of Latvia, the Swedish service-tree has deeply lobed leaves that are green above and densely white-haired beneath. White flowers appear in late spring, followed by bright red fruit in mid-autumn.

A moss native to North America and also found in Europe, brocade moss is usually golden to yellow-green, sometimes brownish. Its reddish stems bear branches mostly in one horizontal plane, and its nearly upright cylindrical capsules mature from July to September.

A fragrant, semi-succulent herb native to southern and southeastern Africa, it sprawls into a dense subshrub and roots where its branches touch the ground. Its crushed leaves smell like oregano, and during extreme drought it may wilt and remain semi-dormant until rain returns.
A flowering plant in the mint family native to eastern Africa, including Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.
A flowering plant native to Madeira, most often found in laurel forest but also in other woodland and thickets.

A small marine alga with no stated native origin, Ceramium pallidum is recorded in coastal waters of Europe and Morocco. It is delicate, regularly branched and filament-like, with strongly curled-in tips and a banded appearance.
An annual herb native to mainland Portugal and the Madeira Archipelago, it grows in sandy areas near the coast. It flowers from April to June.

Perennial shrub native to Central America, South America and the Caribbean. Its branches are stiff-haired, while its leaves have five nearly parallel veins; each small dark berry contains over 100 seeds.

A flowering plant of unspecified native origin, traveller's palm is widespread across Madagascar. Though not a true palm, it forms an immense, flat fan of paddle-shaped leaves and produces large white flowers followed by brilliant blue seeds.

An evergreen or semi-evergreen shrub native to southwestern China and adjacent northern Myanmar and Thailand. Its leaves are glossy above and densely hairy beneath, while its clustered flowers are pink outside and white inside. Birds eat its red fruits and disperse the seeds.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Pilosella galiciana is present in mainland Portugal.

A moss of unstated native origin, tall aloe-moss occurs in Europe, North America, North Africa, Australia and New Zealand. Its leaves curl slightly when dry but spread when moist, and its upright or slightly tilted capsules help distinguish it from similar mosses in winter and spring.
An evergreen tree or shrub native to southern Chile and Argentina. It grows very slowly in wet swamps and peat bogs, often spreading horizontally, and bears white flowers during the austral summer.

A low-growing annual native to western and northern Europe and northwestern Africa. Its rounded leaves have deeply cut edges, and its small pink to purple flowers appear from early spring into mid-autumn, typically March to October in Britain.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Ulex eriocladus belongs to the pea family and occurs in mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant endemic to Brazil.
A herbaceous plant in the carrot family.
Annual herb of unspecified native origin. It is a small plant, reaching about 17 cm tall.

A succulent native to Rwanda, Tanzania and Kenya, Orbea semota forms highly branched mats, with downward-curving stems that root where they touch the ground. Its foul-smelling flowers range from chocolate-brown with pale patterns to pure yellow in var. lutea, and bear fine hairs that move in the slightest breeze.
Flowering grass with native origins documented only by subspecies: subsp. hylodes is native to Macaronesia, while subsp. marina is native to mainland Portugal and Madeira.
A grass native to North America, the Caribbean, South America, Africa, Asia and Australia. It favours salty, wet places such as salt marshes and shallow depressions.

An evergreen shrub native to the Solomon Islands and Vanuatu, it has waxy, broad leaves patterned in shades of green, purple and silver. Its small white flowers have purple-pink spots concentrated near the petal bases.

Clump-forming perennial herb native to eastern China, Japan and Korea. Its fern-like foliage is joined in summer by tiny flowers in feathery plumes, and it naturally grows beside shaded waterways and in damp broadleaf forests.

A slightly spreading flowering shrub native to Portugal, western Spain and two small areas of northwestern France, it has green oblong leaves with rolled-under edges and variable hairiness. Its white flowers have five petals with narrowed yellow bases, and its outer sepals are hairy.

An aquatic or semi-aquatic fern predominantly known from Malaysia, Thailand, northeastern India and parts of southern China. It grows attached to streamside roots and rocks, fully or partly submerged, and produces young plantlets along mature leaf tips and margins that can detach and float to new sites.
A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal.

Perennial grass native to the Iberian Peninsula, the Balearic Islands and northwestern Africa. It has stout stems, tightly rolled leaves with sharp tips, and compact flowerheads; its fibre, called esparto, is used for cords, baskets, espadrilles and paper.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, Centaurea cordubensis occurs in mainland Portugal.

A root vegetable native to Southern Europe and the Near East, Spanish salsify forms a long, dark-skinned taproot with white flesh and sticky latex. Its roots, leafy shoots and open flowers can be eaten raw or cooked, though the thick root skin is usually considered inedible.
stories.edibilityNote: Roots, leafy shoots and open flowers are eaten raw or cooked; the thick black root skin is usually considered inedible.

stories.summary: A flowering sedge whose listed subspecies Carex oederi subsp. pulchella is native to the Azores.
Flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula, it occurs in mainland Portugal.

A perennial shrub native to California and the Baja California Peninsula, bladderpod bears bright yellow flowers nearly year-round and leathery pods. Indigenous tribes ate seeds and flowers after boiling or other cooking, while the Cahuilla cooked immature pods with hot stones; immature pods are edible in small quantities.
stories.edibilityNote: Seeds and flowers were eaten after cooking; Cahuilla cooked immature pods with hot stones, and immature pods are edible only in small quantities.

stories.summary: Flowering bromeliad endemic to the Atlantic Forest in São Paulo state, southeastern Brazil.
A multicellular marine red alga found in coastal regions including Mauritania, southern Africa, India, Sri Lanka, eastern Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea.

Large flowering yucca native to Texas and the Mexican states of Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas. Its mostly unbranched trunk bears clumps of stiff, sharply pointed leaves, with dead leaves hanging beneath them. Dense clusters of white or faintly purple flowers usually rise above the leaves in March and April.
A sedge native to Iceland, Macaronesia, Europe and western Asia as far as the Himalayas, and possibly Greenland. It has been introduced to eastern Canada, New Jersey and Tasmania.
A plant species native to eastern Brazil, Goeppertia lietzei has pointed, long, dark green leaves patterned with straight light-green bands. Its flowers are entirely white.
A shrub or tree endemic to Portugal, this plant is a species of oak.

Epiphytic cactus found in southeastern Brazil, where it grows mainly on trees and less often on rocks in subtropical rainforest. Mature plants become branching, pendant, leafless shrubs with flattened green stem segments and scarlet funnel-shaped flowers.

A climbing vine native to Central and South America and several Caribbean islands, Passiflora vesicaria has three-lobed, serrated leaves and solitary flowers surrounded by finely divided bracts. Its hairless to sparsely hairy fruit ripen yellow-orange to orange; the galapagensis variety is confined to the Galápagos Islands.
A fern endemic to the Azores and Madeira. In the Azores it occurs on every island except Graciosa, Santa Maria and Corvo.

A stout, hairy biennial occurring throughout the Mediterranean. It bears large divided leaves and clusters of mauve-blue to blue flowers, and seed preparations were historically used to kill body lice. All parts are highly toxic and should not be ingested in any quantity.
stories.edibilityNote: All parts are highly toxic and should not be ingested in any quantity.

stories.summary: A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A scrambling shrub native from the eastern Mediterranean eastward to Turkmenistan and the western Himalaya.
Bulbous plant native to the Pyrenees of Spain and France. It has large flowers with pale yellow petals and a dark yellow central cup.

An epiphytic cactus native to eastern Brazil, drunkard's-dream usually grows on trees rather than in the ground. Its branching stems consist of bottle-shaped segments tipped with yellow to orange flowers, followed by translucent white berries.

A climbing rose native to northeastern India, northern Myanmar and southwestern China. It is described as the largest wild rose, with hooked thorns and large white, cream or yellow flowers. Its hard yellow or orange hips often persist through winter into the next flowering season.

An annual flowering plant native to temperate North Africa, Europe and Western Asia, it has branching stems covered with stiff prickly hairs. Its spring-to-summer flowers have four red petals with dark bases, followed by ribbed, club-shaped seed capsules.
A herbaceous grass; its native origin and distinctive features are not documented here.

A tree fern native to New South Wales and Queensland, Australia. Its trunk tip and unfurling fronds bear conspicuous long, silky, straw-coloured scales, and its broad crown carries long light-green fronds.

A plant species with no stated native origin, ciliate medick is found throughout the Mediterranean basin. It partners with a nitrogen-fixing bacterium and is considered by some to be a subspecies of Medicago intertexta.
An annual grass native to the Mediterranean from Spain to Cyprus, and to Turkey. It has slender, relatively rigid upright stems and usually unbranched flower clusters.
Perennial sedge native to Europe, North Africa and Turkey. It is self-supporting and has simple, broad leaves.
A flowering plant endemic to the Azores archipelago. It is protected there.
A perennial grass of unstated native origin, sand dropseed is self-supporting and has simple, broad leaves.

A deciduous perennial groundcover native to parts of North Africa, the Caucasus and southern and central Europe, it has thin, grass-like leaves and small pale-purple flowers on slender green stems. It flowers around May and June.
Rhizomatous perennial of uncertain native origin. It has a thick, violet-scented rhizome, sword-shaped leaves and fragrant white flowers often flushed with blue or pale lavender.
stories.edibilityNote: Used in sweets, to mature Chianti wine and in gin; most parts, including rhizomes and leaves, are poisonous if ingested.

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to mainland Portugal's central-western Sintra Mountains and Cabo da Roca area, it favors rocky habitats and flowers from May to June.

An annual or biennial herb endemic to the Azores. It has stiff, brittle stems thickened at the base and open terminal flower clusters with five equal white petals. Its recorded island distribution is uncertain because it is difficult to distinguish from related Azorean species.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.

Flowering plant endemic to central-northern Portugal. It grows near waterways beneath broadleaf tree cover and was assessed as Vulnerable, with only eight known locations and continuing losses of habitat, subpopulations and mature plants.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Ranunculus henriquesii

stories.summary: A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and present in mainland Portugal.

A flowering shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico, screwbean has tightly twisted seedpods resembling screws. It also bears short, straight spines and numerous small yellowish flowers. Its edible pods were traditionally cooked in covered pits by the Pima and made into meal, cakes and syrup by Native Americans.
stories.edibilityNote: Edible seedpods were traditionally pit-cooked by the Pima and used by Native Americans to make meal, cakes and syrup.

stories.summary: A tree native to South America, including central Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Paraguay and Peru. It has a short trunk and rounded crown; its seedpods contain a sweet floury paste used for human flour and, in the 1940s, a fermented mildly intoxicating drink.
stories.edibilityNote: The sweet fruit paste is made into flour for human consumption and was fermented into an alcoholic drink in the 1940s.

stories.summary: A thorny shrub or tree primarily native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It has drooping branches, feathery foliage and paired straight thorns; Indigenous food uses include eating the blossoms and pods, grinding pods into cake meal, and making bread flour from seeds.
stories.edibilityNote: Indigenous uses include eating blossoms and pods, grinding pods into cake meal, and making traditional bread flour from seeds.

stories.summary: A flowering poppy native to the Mediterranean region and western Asia as far as the western Himalayas. It has spread widely beyond this range and is a minor weed of cereal crops.

A bulb-forming flowering plant endemic to the south-western Iberian Peninsula, it grows in open meadows on clay or sandy-clay soils with considerable moisture. A 2020 mainland Portugal assessment classified it as Endangered after identifying five locations and continuing habitat decline.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Narcissus fernandesii

stories.summary: A fern native to western and southern Europe and southwestern Asia, golden-scaled male-fern is most abundant in humid woodlands with moist soil. Its nearly evergreen light-green fronds have dense yellow-brown scales and a blackish spot where each side branch joins the central stem.

Plant native to Portugal and Spain and endemic to the southwestern Iberian Peninsula. It inhabits very moist, shaded places, usually beneath riverside woods and scrub. In mainland Portugal it was assessed as Vulnerable following population losses and marked habitat degradation.

sources.title: Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental — Campanula primulifolia
sources.attribution: Andre Carapeto % Ana Francisco, Paulo Pereira, Miguel Porto, felipe (2020). Lista Vermelha da Flora Vascular de Portugal Continental. Plazi.org taxonomic treatments database. Checklist dataset https://doi.org/10.15468/ge693f accessed via GBIF.org on 2026-09-12.

stories.summary: A flowering perennial of unspecified native origin, it grows on dry, rocky or sandy ground around the Mediterranean. Its leaves have a strong curry-like fragrance, while its summer clusters of yellow flowers keep their colour after picking and are used in dried arrangements.
stories.edibilityNote: Young shoots and leaves flavour Mediterranean meat, fish or vegetable stews and are removed before serving; the plant is sometimes used as a spice.

stories.summary: A delicate, patch-forming perennial herb native to Europe, it has creeping stems and rounded, ivy-shaped leaves. Solitary pale blue, bell-shaped flowers appear in summer and autumn.
A flowering plant native to mainland Portugal.
A self-supporting perennial grass with no native origin stated.
A grass native to Italy, Portugal, Spain, former Yugoslavia and Morocco.
Perennial plant native to the Iberian Peninsula. It forms mats and has hairy, rounded three-lobed leaves and orange-streaked, pea-like flower heads with reddish, hairy bases.
Tree native to the western and central Mediterranean, specifically parts of North Africa and southwestern Europe. It is a flowering member of the beech family.

A conifer native to the southwestern United States and Mexico, often occurring in small, scattered populations. Its dense foliage ranges from dull gray-green to bright blue-green, and its cones can remain closed for years until the supporting branch dies, including in wildfire.
A conifer native to the American Southwest, smooth Arizona cypress grows on canyons and slopes around Sedona, Arizona. Its notably smooth, unfurrowed bark can appear pink, cherry or grey.

A coniferous shrub or tree endemic to a small coastal area near Monterey, California, Gowen cypress has dense sprays of dark-green to yellow-green foliage. Its cones can remain closed for years, opening after wildfire kills the parent tree.

A coniferous tree native to Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador and Honduras. It has dense sprays of dark to yellow-green foliage and rounded shoots bearing scale-like leaves. Its cones may open when mature or remain closed for years, sometimes opening only after wildfire kills the parent tree.

Climbing perennial flowering plant native to the Mediterranean Basin and introduced to some similar climates. It bears solitary, funnel-shaped pink flowers on long stalks and deeply divided leaves with narrow, finger-like lobes.

A shrub or small tree endemic to south-eastern Australia, it has been widely introduced elsewhere and is often considered a weed. It has thin, rough bark on older stems, relatively large white flowers and flat-topped fruit that falls soon after maturing.

A shrub endemic to south-eastern continental Australia, heath tea-tree grows in heath and mallee. Its young stems have smooth bark that later becomes stringy, and it bears white flowers mainly from October to November; the fruit usually drops soon after releasing its seeds.
A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal.
A flowering grass endemic to Portugal’s Madeira Archipelago, it occurs on Madeira Island but not on Porto Santo, the Selvagens or the Desertas.
A grass native to the Madeira archipelago in the North Atlantic Ocean.
A forget-me-not species of unspecified native origin, it has small coiled flowers that open pure white and turn blue as they mature. Each mature flower produces four nutlets.
A flowering plant endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and recorded in mainland Portugal.

An aquatic plant native to warm-temperate South America, Brazilian waterweed has trailing stems that root at intervals and leaves arranged in whorls. It can spread across the water surface as a dense, light-blocking canopy and has separate male and female plants.

A perennial woody vine native to North America, from northeastern Mexico through parts of the southeastern and midwestern United States. It produces bright red fruits containing hard seeds shaped like small snail shells.

An evergreen shrub or tree endemic to the Canary Islands, it has a spreading form. The tagasaste subspecies has rough yellow-grey bark, velvety young growth, creamy-white scented flowers and flat pods that ripen from green to black; it is widely grown as livestock forage.

A tropical fern native to New Caledonia, the dwarf tree fern has a vertical trunk-like rhizome and bright green fronds. It does not tolerate temperatures below 15°C and must be grown under glass year-round in temperate regions.
A flowering grass native to mainland Portugal, Brachypodium rupestre occurs there without protection under Portuguese or European Community legislation.
A flowering grass native from the Mediterranean through Central Asia to Pakistan. It has a particularly widespread range across southern Europe, North Africa and western and central Asia.
A medium to large deciduous tree native to southeastern Africa. It has warm red to scarlet flowers and relatively smooth bark with intermittent thorns, which tend to be sharper on younger branches.
Cycad native to South Africa, where it is confined to the Eastern Cape. Its mostly underground stem bears dark green, ruffled-looking leaves, while female cones produce glossy scarlet seeds.

An evergreen tree native to parts of East Asia, including Japan, Korea, the Ryukyu Islands and Taiwan. Its glossy, waxy leaves smell of camphor when crushed, and its small fragrant white flowers are followed by clusters of black, berry-like fruit.
stories.edibilityNote: Camphor obtained from the tree has been used for centuries as a culinary spice.

stories.summary: A terrestrial orchid endemic to Tanzania. It grows among leaf litter and debris on rock faces, producing slender reed-like stems and narrow leaves.

A seagrass found in shallow coastal waters from northwestern Europe and the Mediterranean to the Black, Caspian and Aral seas, and off northwestern Africa. Its creeping seabed stems produce clusters of buoyant, strap-shaped leaves, forming dense summer meadows before most leaves disappear in winter.

An evergreen tree endemic to Portugal's Madeira Islands, it has leathery elliptical leaves, pale pink to purple flowers and fleshy fruits. It dominates some low coastal forests on northern Madeira and is threatened by habitat loss.

A shrub endemic to the central Iberian Peninsula. In mainland Portugal it is confined to high quartzite ridges at a single location in Serra do Ramiro, where fewer than 1,000 mature plants were reported during assessments conducted in 2016–2019.

stories.summary: A perennial herb native to Portugal and northwestern Spain. Its nodding flowers have blue petals with white tips and thick, curved blue nectar spurs hooked at the ends; it flowers from April to June.
A bulbous perennial herb endemic to Mexico, the Aztec lily has bright green, strap-shaped annual leaves and usually solitary, bright red flowers.
Evergreen ground orchid native to areas stretching from Asia to Pacific islands. It has large pleated leaves and tall stems bearing up to 25 white, brown, mauve and yellow flowers.

An annual ornamental herb with upright, succulent stems and thick, velvety flower heads shaped like a cockerel's comb. The flowers can be red, pink, whitish or creamy yellow, and are used in cut-flower arrangements.

A perennial herb endemic to Portugal’s coastal cliffs at Almada, south of Lisbon, it is known from sandy cliff walls near carbonate rock facing the Tagus. It has green leaves, an orange-yellow floral throat and conspicuous dark veins; only 34 plants were recorded on site, though inaccessible terrain may hold more.
